This guide covers whole-story editing with an LLM: an AI step reads the story as numbered blocks, the model answers with a structured list of edits, and APPLY_TEXT_EDITS validates and applies them — leaving links, captions, embedded objects and placeholders untouched. Use it for proofreading, spelling and style fixes, structural changes (subheadings, splits, merges) and fact-check notes.

Three pieces work together: GET_STORY_BLOCKS — reads the document as numbered, role-labelled text blocks. response_format: text_edits — makes the completion step answer with a strict JSON edit list instead of prose. APPLY_TEXT_EDITS — previews, applies, or reviews those edits in the Flow Monitor; invalid edits change nothing and are reported with a reason. Agents connected through StoryEditor tools get the same engine as readStoryBlocks, applyTextEdits, proposeTextEdits and applyProposedEdits — no flow authoring required.

Read — GET_STORY_BLOCKS renders the content root as one line per block ([b1 headline/p] …) and remembers each block's text as the stale-block guard. Ask — a completion step with response_format: text_edits receives that text and answers with {"edits": […]}. The parsed answer lands in flowContext.object; the raw JSON stays in flowContext.text. Apply — APPLY_TEXT_EDITS previews, applies, or reviews the edits. Every edit is resolved against the real XML, so text is inserted in the right nodes and hidden markup is preserved. The minimal flow: - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | You are a proofreader. Fix spelling and grammar only. Never change meaning or formatting. Use op "rewrite" for blocks with several fixes and op "replace" for single words. Return an empty edits array when the story is already correct. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: review allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] OPENAI_COMPLETION, HUB_COMPLETION and AZURE_OPENAI_COMPLETION all accept response_format: text_edits. Review mode needs the Flow Monitor (monitor: enabled: true on the section or action).

For a typical story, GET_STORY_BLOCKS produces: [b1 headline/p] Probe reaches asteroid Bennu [b2 summary/p] The contact lasted only a few seconds. [b3 text/p] The probe Osiris made breif contact with the surface on Tuesday. [b4 text/p] Scientists will know on Saturday wether the sample was collected. [b5 text/p] NASA says the mission cost 800 million dollars. What the model sees, and what it does not: Ids are b1, b2, … in document order. They are the only block references an edit may use, and they are deterministic for the same XML and the same options. Roles are parentLocalName/elementLocalName (for example headline/p, text/p), so the model can tell a headline from a body paragraph without knowing the DTD. Blocks are the nearest non-inline ancestor of text. Whitespace-only blocks are omitted entirely. Formatting in inlineElements (default b, i, u) is shown as literal tags when the element carries no attributes. Everything else — links, captions, embedded objects, placeholders, formatting with attributes — is hidden but kept: its text may be visible, its markup never is. ignoreElements subtrees are neither shown nor editable (byline, header, footer). Escaping: &, < and > inside text appear escaped in the block view. Configure reading with these options, and use the same values on APPLY_TEXT_EDITS: Option Default Meaning xpath /doc/story Content root that is read and written blockElements [] (auto) Elements that form editable blocks; empty means auto-detection by the nearest non-inline ancestor ignoreElements [] Elements never shown or edited, e.g. byline, web-image-group inlineElements [b, i, u] Formatting tags visible to and editable by the model A customer DTD that stores articles differently: - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/artikel ignoreElements: [byline, footer, header] inlineElements: [b, i, u, em, strong] Repeat the same four options on APPLY_TEXT_EDITS. The guard snapshot is keyed by xpath plus blockElements, ignoreElements and inlineElements; a step configured differently sees a different block set and reports stale_block for edits it cannot place.

With response_format: text_edits the step sends a strict JSON schema named text_edits: The root object is { "edits": [...] }; an empty array means nothing to change. Every item carries all seven string fields — op, block, target, as, find, replace, reason — and unused ones are "". No system prompt is injected. The operation rules live in the schema descriptions, so behavior must state the editorial rules you want enforced. The answer for the sample story: { "edits": [ { "op": "replace", "block": "b3", "target": "", "as": "", "find": "breif", "replace": "brief", "reason": "spelling" }, { "op": "rewrite", "block": "b4", "target": "", "as": "", "find": "", "replace": "Scientists will know on Saturday whether the sample was collected.", "reason": "spelling" }, { "op": "comment", "block": "b5", "target": "", "as": "", "find": "800 million dollars", "replace": "", "reason": "Verify the figure against the NASA press release." } ] }

Op Fields used Effect replace block, find, replace Changes text inside a block. find must be the exact, unique text as shown in the block view, including visible inline tags. replace: "" deletes the matched text. rewrite block, replace Gives the full corrected block in replace; only the differences are applied. Produces one finding per changed passage. comment block, find, reason Flags find with the note in reason. Never changes text. insert_before / insert_after block, replace, as Inserts a new block next to the anchor, with the text in replace. as is the new block's element type; empty means the anchor's type. delete block Removes the block. split block, find The new block begins at find; everything before it stays in the original block. merge block Appends the directly following block in the same container to this one. move_before / move_after block, target Moves block next to target. retype block, as Changes the block's element type to as. Prefer split, merge and move_* over retyping text: they move the existing nodes, so links, captions and embedded objects inside them survive. Types allowed for insert and retype are the ones already used under the same parent plus whatever insertElements lists. Restrict what the model can do with allowedOps — anything else fails with op_not_allowed instead of being applied. For proofreading, [replace, rewrite, comment] is the safe set.

Mode Writes? Allowed on a read-only document? Output preview never yes TextEditProposal apply (default) once, after validation no (unless forceWrite: true) TextEditReport review once, with what the user ticks no (unless forceWrite: true) TextEditReport Selection. When the input is an edits payload, selection is ignored — everything the model proposed is applied. When the input is a proposal from an earlier preview, selection chooses the finding ids to apply: omit it for all, pass [] to discard everything (each finding reports rejected). selection accepts an array, a comma-separated string or a template such as "{{ flowContext.picked }}". Comment findings are always kept: they never write anything. Review. mode: review shows a checklist in the Flow Monitor — "Review the proposed changes — uncheck any you do not want to apply." with Apply selected and Cancel. Comments are not selectable, and Cancel applies nothing. selection pre-checks ids. Review needs a writable document and an enabled Flow Monitor; otherwise the step fails with Review mode requires the Flow Monitor or APPLY_TEXT_EDITS: It is not possible to write content in read-only mode!. Atomic batches. atomic: true makes the batch all-or-nothing: if one non-comment edit fails, nothing is written and the other edits report batch_failed. Use it when a partially applied correction would be worse than none. Highlights. A preview marks its findings in the editor using markTag (default mark); mark: false turns that off. In Swing the marks are virtual editor marks, not content. In Prime they are stored in the story as <mark> elements: run CLEAR_TAGS before the story is saved, or set mark: false. Remove them with CLEAR_TAGS and tags: ["mark"] (or your configured markTag). Applying a marked proposal clears the preview marks first and then re-marks the remaining comments.

preview writes a TextEditProposal to object: Field Contents kind Always "text_edit_proposal" xpath Content root the proposal belongs to edits Normalized edits, with block ids remapped by the stale-block guard snapshot Block id → plain text at preview time (the guard) findings One entry per finding table Display rows for MONITOR_TABLE report The underlying report Each finding has id (f1, f2, … in payload order), edit (index into edits), an optional hunk (rewrite passage index), op, block, role, before, after, reason, label, kind ("edit" or "comment") and marked. table rows have exactly the columns #, Block, Original, Suggestion, Reason. apply and review write a TextEditReport: mode, proposed, applied, commented, unchanged, rejected, failed, results[] and findings[]. A row in results[] is { index, op, block, find, status, error?, hint? }, where status is one of proposed, applied, commented, unchanged, rejected or failed. - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Findings — uncheck anything you do not want" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}" # after preview - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Applied" data: "{{ flowContext.object.results }}" # after apply / review maxRows: 30

Preview the findings, show them, then let the producer tick what to apply. The prompt is deliberately narrow: the schema carries the operation rules, not the editorial ones. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | You are a meticulous newspaper proofreader working in the document's language. Fix only: spelling, grammar, punctuation, spacing, capitalisation, clear typos. Never rephrase, never translate, never change meaning, numbers, names, quotes or markup. Rewrite a whole block when it contains several fixes; use replace for single words. Put the rule you applied in "reason" (short: "spelling", "comma before a conjunction"). Return an empty edits array when the story is already clean. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview mark: true allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] - step: IF condition: '{{ (flowContext.object.findings | length) > 0 }}' then: - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Findings — uncheck anything you do not want" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: review atomic: true allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Applied" data: "{{ flowContext.object.results }}" maxRows: 30 else: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success title: "Proofreading" message: "No spelling or grammar fixes to apply."

preview never writes, so reviewers can run it on documents they cannot change. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Report spelling, grammar and style issues, and flag anything a human must verify. Never change meaning, wording or markup. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview mark: true allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Findings (highlights stay until CLEAR_TAGS)" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}"

Comments never change the document text, so this works on read-only stories too. In Prime, confirm Clear highlights before saving — Keep highlights leaves the <mark> elements in the story. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Flag text a human must verify: questionable facts, unattributed quotes, risky or misleading wording, names and numbers worth a second look. Use op "comment" only, one note per issue, and put the check to perform in "reason". Never suggest rewrites. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview mark: true allowedOps: [comment] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Notes to verify (reason = what to check)" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}" - step: MONITOR_CONFIRM message: "Have you checked these notes?" confirm: "Clear highlights" cancel: "Keep highlights" - step: IF condition: '{{ flowContext.confirmed }}' then: - step: CLEAR_TAGS tags: ["mark"] MONITOR_CONFIRM writes the boolean flowContext.confirmed.

Skip the checklist when the corrections are mechanical — but keep the batch atomic so a half-applied set never reaches the document. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Fix spelling and grammar only. Never change meaning, numbers, names or markup. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: apply atomic: true allowedOps: [replace, rewrite] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Applied" data: "{{ flowContext.object.results }}" maxRows: 30 When one edit fails, atomic marks every other edit in the batch batch_failed, so the report shows why the batch was not written.
documents.s: Apply all fixes in one batch

documents.t: A preview proposal can be filtered in code — for example, apply only the single-word replacements and leave rewrites for a human. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Fix spelling and grammar. Use replace for single words and rewrite for blocks with several fixes. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview allowedOps: [replace, rewrite] - step: SCRIPTING script: | const findings = (flowContext.object && flowContext.object.findings) || []; flowContext.picked = findings.filter((f) => f.op === 'replace').map((f) => f.id); return flowContext; - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: apply selection: "{{ flowContext.picked }}" allowedOps: [replace, rewrite] - step: CLEAR_TAGS tags: ["mark"] Passing selection: [] discards the whole proposal and nothing is written.
documents.s: Let a script pick the findings

documents.t: Structural operations move existing nodes instead of retyping them, so nothing inside a paragraph is lost. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Insert a short subheading before each block that starts a new topic: op "insert_before", "as": "h2", the subheading in "replace". When a new topic starts inside a block, use op "split" with "find" = the text where the new block begins. Never change, delete or move existing text. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: review allowedOps: [insert_before, split] insertElements: [h2] List in insertElements only elements your DTD allows under that parent; anything else fails with invalid_element_type.

The same engine is available to agents as tools. With reviewEdits: true, every write goes through the Flow Monitor checklist first: - step: HUB_COMPLETION maxToolIterations: 12 behavior: You are an editorial assistant. instruction: | 1. Call readStoryBlocks. 2. Call applyTextEdits with spelling and grammar fixes only — the user confirms the changes in the Flow Monitor checklist. Report the result. builtinTools: - class: StoryEditor only: [readStoryBlocks, applyTextEdits, clearMarks] config: allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] reviewEdits: true For an interactive agent that proposes first and applies only what the user accepts: - step: HUB_COMPLETION maxToolIterations: 12 toolChoice: required behavior: 'You are an editorial assistant. The user cannot type: every interaction uses tools.' instruction: | 1. Call readStoryBlocks. 2. Call proposeTextEdits with spelling and grammar fixes only (never restructure). 3. Present the numbered findings and ask which ones to apply using askMultipleChoice. 4. Call applyProposedEdits with the accepted ids. 5. Call clearMarks when you are done. builtinTools: - class: StoryEditor only: [readStoryBlocks, proposeTextEdits, applyProposedEdits, clearMarks] config: allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] reviewEdits: false - class: UserInteractionTools only: [askMultipleChoice] See Built-in AI Tools — StoryEditor for the full tool list and configuration. For agent tools, atomicEdits defaults to true, so a failed edit means the agent fixes it and resends the batch.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/em-al-wi/proactions-schema/main/schema/partial-section.schema.json section: Proofreading context: story monitor: enabled: true actions: - title: "Proofread story" flow: - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story ignoreElements: [byline, footer, header] inlineElements: [b, i, u, em, strong] - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | You are a meticulous newspaper proofreader working in the document's language. Fix only: spelling, grammar, punctuation, spacing, capitalisation, clear typos. Never rephrase, never translate, never change meaning, numbers, names, quotes or markup. Rewrite a whole block when it contains several fixes; use replace for single words. Put the rule you applied in "reason" (short: "spelling", "comma before a conjunction"). Return an empty edits array when the story is already clean. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview mark: true xpath: /doc/story ignoreElements: [byline, footer, header] inlineElements: [b, i, u, em, strong] allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] - step: IF condition: '{{ (flowContext.object.findings | length) > 0 }}' then: - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Findings — uncheck anything you do not want" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: review atomic: true allowedOps: [replace, rewrite, comment] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Applied" data: "{{ flowContext.object.results }}" maxRows: 30 else: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success title: "Proofreading" message: "No spelling or grammar fixes to apply." - title: "Check facts & wording" flow: - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story ignoreElements: [byline, footer, header] inlineElements: [b, i, u, em, strong] - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_edits behavior: | Flag text a human must verify: questionable facts, unattributed quotes, risky or misleading wording, names and numbers worth a second look. Use op "comment" only, one note per issue, and put the check to perform in "reason". Never suggest rewrites. instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_EDITS mode: preview mark: true xpath: /doc/story ignoreElements: [byline, footer, header] inlineElements: [b, i, u, em, strong] allowedOps: [comment] - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Notes to verify (reason = what to check)" data: "{{ flowContext.object.table }}" - step: MONITOR_CONFIRM message: "Have you checked these notes?" confirm: "Clear highlights" cancel: "Keep highlights" - step: IF condition: '{{ flowContext.confirmed }}' then: - step: CLEAR_TAGS tags: ["mark"]

A rejected edit never changes the document. Each failed row in results[] carries an error and a hint written for the model, so an agent can resend a corrected batch. Code Meaning What to do missing_params A field the op needs is empty. Require block, find, replace or target in behavior. invalid_op The op name is not one of the eleven operations. Spell the op exactly, or widen allowedOps. op_not_allowed The op is valid but excluded by allowedOps. Widen allowedOps, or make the prompt stop asking for it. unknown_block The block id is not in the read. Re-run GET_STORY_BLOCKS and use the ids it produced. stale_block The block's text changed since the read (or the two steps use different options). Re-run GET_STORY_BLOCKS; use identical options on both steps. not_found find does not occur in the block. find must be copied verbatim, including visible inline tags. ambiguous_match find occurs more than once in the block. Extend find with surrounding words so it is unique. overlapping_edit Two edits claim the same text. Apply one, or merge them into a single rewrite. search_matches_markup find cuts an escaped character, an unbalanced tag pair, or crosses formatting boundaries. Keep find inside one text run; include complete tag pairs. protected_markup The edit would remove or rewrite hidden content (links, embedded objects, formatting with attributes). Narrow find, or use split/move so the markup moves intact. invalid_element_type The requested as type is not used under that parent. Add the type to insertElements, or pick an existing type. invalid_position The block has no parent element, so it cannot be moved or inserted next to. Target a block inside a container. structure_required The block is the only element of its type in its parent and must stay. Change its text with replace/rewrite instead of deleting or splitting it. batch_failed Another edit in the same atomic batch failed, so this one was not applied. Fix the failing edit and resend the whole batch. escaped_markup, replacement_not_well_formed, disallowed_elements, disallowed_attributes, disallowed_node_type The replacement content is not valid for the document: re-escaped tags, broken XML, or elements/attributes that are not allowed. Return plain text plus the inline tags shown in the block view. not_markable The finding cannot be highlighted in the editor (nothing to mark at that position). Harmless: the edit is still applied; only the highlight is skipped. unknown_finding selection names a finding id that is not in the proposal. Use the ids from object.findings (f1, f2, …). Step-level failures stop the flow instead of producing rows: GET_STORY_BLOCKS: No XML found at xpath "<xpath>", edits must be an array or an object with an "edits" array, the read-only error, and Review mode requires the Flow Monitor.

Review mode requires the Flow Monitor — set monitor: enabled: true on the section or action, or use mode: preview. It is not possible to write content in read-only mode! — use mode: preview, or set forceWrite: true if the flow is trusted to write anyway. Many stale_block errors — the story changed after GET_STORY_BLOCKS, or the two steps use different xpath, blockElements, ignoreElements or inlineElements. Re-run the read with matching options. not_found for text you can see — the model re-worded or re-escaped find. Tell it to copy the text verbatim, including visible inline tags such as <b>. No XML found at xpath — your DTD stores content elsewhere; set xpath on both steps. Highlights stay in the editor — marks are virtual in Swing and stored as <mark> elements in Prime; clear them with CLEAR_TAGS and tags: ["mark"] (or your markTag). Applying a marked proposal clears them automatically. HTTP 400 about temperature — reasoning models reject it; omit options on the completion step. HTTP 400 about response_format or json_schema — text_edits uses OpenAI structured outputs; the model, Azure deployment or Hub target must support json_schema with strict: true. No streaming — streaming is disabled for json_schema response formats, so the text output arrives in one piece.
GET_STORY_BLOCKS APPLY_TEXT_EDITS Cut to Length — shorten a story to a target length with ranked LLM cuts and a selection panel Built-in AI Tools — StoryEditor Flow Monitor AI Integration
This guide covers integrating ProActions into the Swing Web Client, including embedding actions in toolbars, object panels, image toolbars, and using the ProActions API for programmatic access.

ProActions can be integrated into Swing through two main approaches: UI Integration - Embed ProActions in toolbars, object panels, and component toolbars API Integration - Programmatic access to ProActions functionality via JavaScript API Both approaches allow you to seamlessly integrate AI-powered workflows into your Swing workflows.

ProActions Installed: ProActions extension properly installed on Swing Configuration File: /SysConfig/pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml configured with actions Swing Extensions Knowledge: Basic understanding of Swing extension development JavaScript Knowledge: Familiarity with JavaScript for custom integrations
Actions can subscribe to runtime events and execute automatically without menu interaction.

Configure subscriptions with the events property on an action: - id: auto-postprocess title: "Auto post-process" hidden: true events: - source: "aikit" name: "aiKitFlowCompleted" condition: "{{ flowContext._eventPayload.actionId == 'source-action' }}" ifRunning: "queue" flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Post-processing triggered"

aikit - AI-Kit lifecycle events (aiKitReady, aiKitFlowCompleted, aiKitFlowCancelled, aiKitFlowError) system - System lifecycle events (onEditorReady) custom - User-defined events from EMIT_EVENT / DISPATCH_EVENT steps

Use these lifecycle events with source: "aikit" in action subscriptions: Event Emitted when Common condition/payload usage aiKitReady AI-Kit has loaded configuration and registered actions. Usually no payload filter needed. Use for startup automation. aiKitFlowCompleted Any action flow completes successfully. Filter by source action id: {{ flowContext._eventPayload.actionId == 'my-action-id' }} Example: - id: startup-check title: "Startup Check" hidden: true events: - source: "aikit" name: "aiKitReady" flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "AI-Kit is ready" - id: postprocess-after-summary title: "Postprocess After Summary" hidden: true events: - source: "aikit" name: "aiKitFlowCompleted" condition: "{{ flowContext._eventPayload.actionId == 'summary-action' }}" flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Summary flow completed"

Value Behavior skip Ignore new trigger while action is running queue Queue trigger and run after current execution completes parallel Start additional execution immediately condition is optional and evaluated per event. If evaluation fails, the trigger is skipped.

Triggered actions receive event metadata in flowContext: flowContext._event - Complete event object flowContext._eventName - Event name flowContext._eventPayload - Event payload Use these variables in subsequent steps: - id: auto-postprocess title: "Auto post-process" hidden: true events: - source: "aikit" name: "aiKitFlowCompleted" condition: "{{ flowContext._eventPayload.actionId == 'source-action' }}" flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Triggered by {{ flowContext._eventPayload.actionId }}" events.condition uses resolver boolean evaluation. Use flowContext._event, flowContext._eventName, and flowContext._eventPayload inside the condition.

Starting with v1.1.0, ProActions supports declarative integration with Swing's native UI components directly in your action configuration. This eliminates the need for custom JavaScript code for common integration scenarios.

Four integration types are available: inlineMenu - Add buttons to the inline text editor toolbar objectAction - Add actions to object three-dots menu contextMenu - Add items to right-click context menus onBlockDrop - Trigger actions when blocks are dropped in the editor All four are configured using the swing: property in your action definition.

Add buttons to the inline text editor toolbar that appears when selecting text in the editor. Configuration​ - title: "Shorten Selection" swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Shorten" icon: "fa fa-compress" allowReadOnly: false isEnabled: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.story.type == 'WireStory' }}" isActive: "{{ true }}" showIn: inlinetoolbar: true slashmenu: true blockmenu: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Shorten: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Configuration Options​ Property Type Required Default Description enable boolean Yes - Enable this integration label string No Action title Button label text icon string No - FontAwesome icon class (e.g., "fa fa-magic") allowReadOnly boolean No false Allow button to be active in read-only mode isEnabled string No "{{ true }}" Nunjucks expression for button enablement isActive string No "{{ true }}" Nunjucks expression for button visibility showIn object No all true Source-level visibility flags evaluated before isActive showIn supports: inlinetoolbar - visibility for inline text-selection toolbar slashmenu - visibility for contextual slash menu (ctx.component.getType() == "contextualtoolbar" and getSubType() == "slashmenu") blockmenu - visibility for contextual block menu (ctx.component.getType() == "contextualtoolbar" and getSubType() == "blockmenu") Visibility Evaluation Order​ Swing visibility for inlineMenu is resolved inside command isActive in this order: showIn source gate integration-level swing.inlineMenu.isActive action-level action.isAvailable isEnabled is evaluated separately and controls enabled/disabled state only. Where It Appears​ The inline integration can appear from these command sources: Inline text selection - ctx.component.getType() === "inlinetoolbar" Contextual block menu - ctx.component.getType() === "contextualtoolbar" and ctx.component.getSubType() === "blockmenu" Contextual slash menu - ctx.component.getType() === "contextualtoolbar" and ctx.component.getSubType() === "slashmenu" Use showIn to restrict where the action is shown. Conditional Visibility Examples​ Use Nunjucks expressions to control when buttons are enabled or visible: Only enable for paragraph elements: swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Format" isEnabled: "{{ ctx.activeDocument.getSelection().getNode().elementName == 'p' }}" Combine multiple conditions: swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Improve Paragraph" isEnabled: "{{ ctx.activeDocument.getSelection().getNode().elementName == 'p' and client.getChannel() == 'mychannel' }}" Check content item type: swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Headline Tool" isEnabled: "{{ ctx.activeDocument.getSelection().getNode().elementName == 'p' }}" Complete Example​ - title: "Improve Selected Text" description: "Use AI to improve the selected text" swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Improve" icon: "fa fa-magic" allowReadOnly: false isEnabled: "{{ ctx.activeDocument.getSelection().getNode().elementName == 'p' }}" flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: "You are a writing assistant that improves text clarity and style." instruction: "Improve this text: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

Add actions to the object three-dots menu that appears in search results, preview panes, and explorer grids. Configuration​ - title: "Generate Summary" swing: objectAction: enable: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Create a brief summary of: {textContent}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Summary: {{ flowContext.text }}" Configuration Options​ Property Type Required Description enable boolean Yes Enable this integration Where It Appears​ Object actions appear in: Search results - Three-dots menu for each result Preview pane - Object actions menu Explorer grid - Context actions for objects Notes​ Object actions use the action's title property for the menu label Custom labels and icons are not supported in the object menu The action executes in the context of the selected object Example​ - title: "Extract Keywords" description: "Extract keywords from the document" swing: objectAction: enable: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Extract 10 relevant keywords from: {textContent}" response_format: "list" # ...

Add items to right-click context menus throughout Swing. Configuration​ - title: "Process with AI" swing: contextMenu: enable: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Analyze: {textContent}" # ... Configuration Options​ Property Type Required Description enable boolean Yes Enable this integration Where It Appears​ Context menu items appear in: Explorer - Right-click menu on objects Various contexts - Context-specific right-click menus Notes​ Context menu items use the action's title property for the menu label Custom labels and icons are not supported The action executes in the context of the right-clicked item Complete Example​ - title: "Quick Translate" description: "Translate content to French" swing: contextMenu: enable: true flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{textContent}" target_lang: "FR" - step: SHOW_RESPONSE title: "Translation"

Trigger actions automatically when a block element is dropped in the editor. This is useful for processing content during drag-and-drop operations between stories, from old versions, or across channels. Configuration​ - title: "Auto-translate Dropped Content" swing: onBlockDrop: enable: true runWhen: isCrossStory: true when: "options.sourceLanguage !== options.targetLanguage" flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.xmlContent | safe }}" target_lang: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.targetLanguage }}" - step: REPLACE_XML at: CURSOR_PARAGRAPH Configuration Options​ Property Type Required Description enable boolean Yes Enable this integration runWhen object No Simple conditions that must all match for the action to run when string No JavaScript expression for complex conditions (evaluated after runWhen) runWhen Conditions​ Simple conditions based on block drop options. All specified conditions must match: Condition Type Description isCrossStory boolean Block is being moved between different stories fromOldVersion boolean Content is being restored from a previous version betweenChannelCopy boolean Block is being copied between different channels isSameContainer boolean Block is moved within the same container blockType string Block type (e.g., "image", "video") Condition matching: true - The option must be truthy false - The option must be falsy String value - Requires exact match Custom Expressions (when)​ Use JavaScript expressions for complex conditions. The expression has access to: options - Block drop information object ctx - Swing editor context swing: onBlockDrop: enable: true when: "options.sourceLanguage !== options.targetLanguage && options.textContent.length > 100" Accessing Block Drop Data in Flow​ When an action is triggered by a block drop, the drop information is available in flowContext._dropInfo: Property Type Description blockType string Type of the dropped block (e.g., "image", "video") textContent string Plain text content of the dropped block xmlContent string XML representation of the dropped block htmlContent string HTML representation of the dropped block isCrossStory boolean Whether block is from a different story fromOldVersion boolean Whether content is from a previous version sourceStoryId string ID of the source story targetStoryId string ID of the target story sourceLanguage string Language of the source story targetLanguage string Language of the target story betweenChannelCopy boolean Whether copying between channels isSameContainer boolean Whether moving within the same container referenceObject object Reference to associated object (path, srcPreview) txtPath string XPath to the dropped block element Convenience aliases are also available at the flowContext root level: flowContext._droppedContent - First available of: textContent, xmlContent, or htmlContent flowContext._droppedBlockType - The block type Example: Access Drop Data​ flow: - step: IF test: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.isCrossStory }}" then: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.textContent }}" target_lang: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.targetLanguage }}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Translated from {{ flowContext._dropInfo.sourceLanguage }}" Where It Works​ Block drop integration works in: Story editor - When dropping blocks into stories Report editor - When dropping blocks into reports Example: Translate Cross-Story Drops​ Automatically translate content when dropping from a story in a different language: - title: "Auto-translate Dropped Content" hidden: true monitor: enabled: false swing: onBlockDrop: enable: true runWhen: isCrossStory: true when: "options.sourceLanguage !== options.targetLanguage" flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.xmlContent | safe }}" target_lang: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.targetLanguage }}" - step: REPLACE_XML at: CURSOR_PARAGRAPH - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Content translated from {{ flowContext._dropInfo.sourceLanguage }} to {{ flowContext._dropInfo.targetLanguage }}" Example: Process Dropped Images​ Process images when dropped from external sources: - title: "Optimize Dropped Image" hidden: true swing: onBlockDrop: enable: true runWhen: blockType: "image" isCrossStory: true flow: - step: IF test: "{{ flowContext._dropInfo.referenceObject.path }}" then: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Processing image: {{ flowContext._dropInfo.referenceObject.path }}" Example: Complex Conditions​ Use the when expression for complex logic: - title: "Process Long Text Drops" hidden: true swing: onBlockDrop: enable: true runWhen: fromOldVersion: false when: | options.textContent && options.textContent.length > 500 && !options.isSameContainer flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Summarize: {{ flowContext._dropInfo.textContent }}" - step: SHOW_RESPONSE title: "Summary" Notes​ Block drop actions are typically configured with hidden: true since they are triggered automatically, not from the command palette Consider using monitor.enabled: false for quick actions to avoid UI interruption Multiple actions can register for block drop events - all matching actions will execute If conditions don't match, the action silently skips (no error shown)

You can enable multiple integration types for the same action to make it accessible from different locations: - title: "AI Content Processor" description: "Process content with AI" swing: # Inline toolbar (for text selection in editor) inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Process" icon: "fa fa-cog" # Object action (for object three-dots menu) objectAction: enable: true # Context menu (for right-click) contextMenu: enable: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process and improve: {textContent}" # ... This makes the action available in: Inline toolbar when text is selected Object three-dots menu in search/explorer Right-click context menu

The TEXT_MENU component is deprecated in v1.1.0. Migrate to inlineMenu for better integration with Swing. Old Approach (TEXT_MENU): AI_KIT: TEXT_MENU: story: items: - type: 'button' icon: 'fa fa-compress' title: 'Shorten' flowRef: 'shortenText' SECTIONS: - section: Text Actions actions: - title: "shortenText" hidden: true flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Shorten: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR New Approach (inlineMenu): AI_KIT: SECTIONS: - section: Text Actions actions: - title: "Shorten Text" swing: inlineMenu: enable: true icon: "fa fa-compress" label: "Shorten" flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Shorten: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Benefits of the new approach: No need for separate hidden actions Direct configuration in action definition Conditional enablement support Consistent with other Swing integrations Action remains accessible via command palette (Ctrl+K)

1. Use Descriptive Labels​ Choose clear, action-oriented labels for inline toolbar buttons: # Good swing: inlineMenu: label: "Improve Text" # Avoid swing: inlineMenu: label: "AI" 2. Add Conditional Enablement​ Prevent errors by enabling buttons only in valid contexts: swing: inlineMenu: enable: true label: "Format Paragraph" # Only enable for paragraphs with selected text isEnabled: "{{ ctx.activeDocument.getSelection().getNode().elementName == 'p' }}" 3. Choose Appropriate Icons​ Use FontAwesome icons that clearly represent the action: # Text improvement icon: "fa fa-magic" # Compression/shortening icon: "fa fa-compress" # Translation icon: "fa fa-language" # Generation/creation icon: "fa fa-lightbulb" 4. Combine Integrations for Consistency​ Make frequently-used actions available in multiple places: - title: "Generate Headlines" swing: inlineMenu: enable: true icon: "fa fa-heading" objectAction: enable: true contextMenu: enable: true 5. Handle Errors Gracefully​ Use TRY/CATCH in flows to handle failures: flow: - step: TRY try: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR catch: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Processing failed. Please try again." type: "error" 6. Test in All Contexts​ Test your integrations in: Report editor Story editor DWP editor Search results Explorer view 7. Respect Read-Only Mode​ Set allowReadOnly: false for actions that modify content: swing: inlineMenu: enable: true allowReadOnly: false # Disable in read-only mode
ProActions can be triggered from various UI locations in Swing using the SwingProActions.executeAction() method.
documents.s: UI Integration in Panels and Toolbars (Custom JavaScript)

documents.t: The primary method for triggering ProActions from custom UI: SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, actionId, options); Parameters: ctx - The Swing context object (can be null or undefined, will auto-detect if not provided) actionId - The ID or title of the action to execute (from your configuration) options (optional) - Configuration object with the following properties: onChangeViewSize?: (width: number, height: number) => void - Callback invoked when the view size changes. Primarily used by the CHANGE_VIEW_SIZE step to resize the command palette in Méthode Prime. onCompletion?: () => void - Callback invoked when the action execution completes successfully onError?: (err: Error) => void - Callback invoked when an error occurs during action execution onCancel?: (flowContext: ActionContextData) => void - Callback invoked when the user cancels the flow (e.g., clicks cancel in FORM, PROMPT, FILE_UPLOAD, USER_SELECT, or IMAGE_PICKER steps) flowContext?: ActionContextData - Prefilled context object that allows you to pass external data into the ProActions flow Basic Usage​ // Simple execution SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "my_action_id"); With Callbacks​ // With completion, error, and cancellation handling SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "my_action_id", { onCompletion: () => { console.log("Action completed successfully"); // Update UI or show success message }, onError: (err) => { console.error("Action failed:", err); // Show error notification to user }, onCancel: (flowContext) => { console.log("User cancelled the action"); console.log("Flow state at cancellation:", flowContext); // Handle cancellation - no error notification needed // The flowContext contains the state of the workflow at the time of cancellation } }); With Prefilled Context​ Use flowContext to pass external data into your ProActions workflow: // Pass custom data to the flow SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "process_article", { flowContext: { text: "Custom article text from external source", object: { category: "sports", priority: "high" }, list: ["tag1", "tag2", "tag3"] }, onCompletion: () => { console.log("Processing completed"); } }); This is useful when: Loading data from external APIs Pre-populating workflows with form data Chaining multiple actions with shared data Integrating with third-party systems Understanding Cancellation vs Errors​ ProActions distinguishes between user cancellations and errors: Cancellation: User explicitly cancels by clicking the cancel/close button in UI steps (FORM, PROMPT, FILE_UPLOAD, USER_SELECT, IMAGE_PICKER) Triggers onCancel callback Dispatches aiKitFlowCancelled custom event Does NOT trigger onError callback Not considered an error condition Error: Something goes wrong during flow execution (network error, invalid data, etc.) Triggers onError callback Dispatches aiKitFlowError custom event Should display error notification to user Example: Handling both scenarios correctly SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "process_article", { flowContext: { articleId: "123", mode: "summary" }, onCompletion: () => { // Flow completed successfully showNotification("Article processed successfully", "success"); refreshUI(); }, onCancel: (flowContext) => { // User cancelled - this is normal, not an error console.log("User cancelled processing"); console.log("Cancelled at step:", flowContext); // Don't show error notification - cancellation is intentional // Optionally save draft state from flowContext }, onError: (err) => { // Something went wrong - this is an actual error console.error("Processing failed:", err); showNotification("Failed to process article: " + err.message, "error"); } }); Listening to Custom Events​ ProActions dispatches custom DOM events that you can listen to for global handling: // Listen for flow cancellations document.addEventListener('aiKitFlowCancelled', (event) => { console.log('Flow cancelled:', { flowContext: event.detail.flowContext, cancelledAt: event.detail.cancelledAt, // Step name where cancelled reason: event.detail.reason // Always 'user_cancellation' }); // Global cancellation handling // e.g., log analytics, save draft state, etc. }); // Listen for flow completions document.addEventListener('aiKitFlowCompleted', (event) => { console.log('Flow completed successfully'); // Global completion handling }); // Listen for flow errors document.addEventListener('aiKitFlowError', (event) => { console.error('Flow error:', event.detail.error); // Global error handling }); These events are useful for: Centralized logging and analytics Tracking user behavior patterns Implementing global error handling Saving draft states on cancellation Updating global UI indicators

Add ProActions buttons to the editor toolbar. Step 1: Create a Custom Tab​ First, create a custom tab to organize your ProActions buttons: eidosmedia.webclient.extensions.editor.tabs.add({ name: "em-tab-proactions", label: "ProActions", }); Step 2: Register Commands​ Register commands that execute ProActions: eidosmedia.webclient.commands.add({ name: "custom.proactions.robot.rewrite.pressrelease", isActive: function (ctx) { if (ctx.component.getType() === "toolbar") { return true; } return false; }, isEnabled: function (ctx) { return true; }, action: function (ctx, params, callbacks) { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "robot.rewrite.pressrelease"); }, }); Step 3: Add Toolbar Buttons​ Add buttons to the toolbar that trigger your commands: eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.toolbar.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.robot.rewrite.pressrelease", label: "Rewrite (Press Release)", icon: "fas fa-robot", tabId: "em-tab-proactions", }); Complete Example: Text-to-Speech Button​ // Create tab eidosmedia.webclient.extensions.editor.tabs.add({ name: "em-tab-proactions", label: "ProActions", }); // Register command eidosmedia.webclient.commands.add({ name: "custom.proactions.tts", isActive: function (ctx) { if (ctx.component.getType() === "toolbar") { return true; } return false; }, isEnabled: function (ctx) { return true; }, action: function (ctx, params, callbacks) { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "proactions.tts"); }, }); // Add button eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.toolbar.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.tts", label: "TTS", icon: "fas fa-podcast", tabId: "em-tab-proactions", });

Add ProActions to the image component toolbar for context-aware image processing. Register Image-Specific Commands​ eidosmedia.webclient.commands.add({ name: "custom.proactions.vision.generatecaption", isActive: function (ctx) { if (ctx.area?.getName() === "story" && ctx.component.getType() === ctx.activeDocument?.CONSTANTS?.BLOCK_IMAGE) { return true; } return false; }, isEnabled: function (ctx) { if (ctx.component.getType() === ctx.activeDocument?.CONSTANTS?.BLOCK_IMAGE) { return true; } return false; }, action: function (ctx, params, callbacks) { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "vision_create_caption"); }, }); Add Buttons to Image Toolbar​ eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.components.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.vision.generatecaption", label: "Generate Caption", icon: "fas fa-glasses", allowReadOnly: false, }); eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.components.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.vision.describe.picture", label: "Describe Picture", icon: "fas fa-glasses", allowReadOnly: false, }); eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.components.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.stability.outpaint", label: "Outpaint using AI", icon: "fas fa-glasses", allowReadOnly: false, });

Integrate ProActions into custom object panels for document metadata processing. Register Object Panel​ var types = [ "EOM::CompoundStory", "EOM::Story", "WireStory", "EOM::CompoundMediaGallery", "EOM::MediaGallery", "EOM::Gallery", "EOM::LiveBlog", "Poll", ]; var options = { refreshOnShow: true, closeOnHide: true, init: function (ctx) { // Initialization logic }, preFillForm: function (ctx) { console.log("ObjPanel: preFillForm"); }, postFillForm: function (ctx) { console.log("ObjPanel: postFillForm"); // Add click handlers for ProActions buttons $("#getEntitiesOpenAI").click(function () { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "text_extract_keywords"); }); $("#getSEOOpenAI").click(function () { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "text_calc_seo_title"); SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "text_calc_meta_descr"); }); }, }; eidosmedia.webclient.extensions.objectpanel.register( types, "story-objectpanel.html", options ); Object Panel HTML (story-objectpanel.html)​ Your HTML file would include buttons that trigger the ProActions:

AI Tools
The ProActions API provides programmatic access to AI services and action execution.

1. List Services​ Get a list of all configured services: // List all services const services = aikit.listServices(); console.log(services); // ["HUB", "OPENAI_COMPLETION", "DEEPL", ...] // List services by type const completionServices = aikit.listServices("completion"); console.log(completionServices); // ["HUB", "OPENAI_COMPLETION", "HUB_AZURE", ...] Parameters: type (optional): Filter by service type ("completion", "speech", "transcription", etc.) Returns: Array of service names 2. Get Configuration​ Access the current ProActions configuration: const config = aikit.getConfig(); console.log(config.AI_KIT.SECTIONS); console.log(config.AI_KIT.SERVICES); Returns: The complete plugin configuration object 3. Find Actions Using a Prompt​ Find which actions use a specific prompt ID: const promptId = "c81b1538-d3da-47f1-836b-1158578a35d3"; const actionsUsingPrompt = aikit.getPromptUsingActions(promptId); console.log(actionsUsingPrompt); // ["Replace Headline", "Suggest Headlines", ...] Parameters: promptId: The UUID of the prompt to search for Returns: Array of action titles or IDs that use the specified prompt 4. Execute Chat Completion​ Execute LLM chat completions programmatically: Basic Usage​ const response = await aikit.executeChatCompletion("Hello, how are you?"); console.log(response.text); // The AI's response With Options​ const response = await aikit.executeChatCompletion( "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points", { systemPrompt: "You are a helpful assistant for authors", serviceName: "HUB", completionType: "HUB_COMPLETION", includeFullResponse: true, model: "gpt-6.1-sol", ctx: currentSwingContext, } ); console.log(response.text); // The summary text console.log(response.response); // Full API response (if includeFullResponse: true) Parameters: userPrompt (required): The user prompt string options (optional): Configuration object with the following properties: ctx: Swing context object (auto-detected if not provided) systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the AI's behavior serviceName: Which service to use (default: "HUB") completionType: Which completion step to use (default: "HUB_COMPLETION") includeFullResponse: Include full API response (default: false) model: Override the model (e.g., "gpt-6.1-sol", "gpt-6-astra") flowContext: Existing flow context to populate cfg: Additional step configuration options Returns: ActionContextData object containing: text: The main text response object: Parsed JSON object (if using structured outputs) list: Array of strings (if using list format) response: Full API response (if includeFullResponse: true) Other outputs depending on the completion configuration Advanced Usage with Custom Configuration​ const response = await aikit.executeChatCompletion( "Extract key information from the article", { serviceName: "HUB", model: "gpt-6.1-sol", cfg: { response_format: "json_object", options: { max_tokens: 500, }, }, } ); const extractedData = response.object; console.log(extractedData); 5. Execute Action from YAML​ Execute a complete ProActions workflow defined in YAML: const yamlDefinition = ` flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Generate a headline for this article" behavior: "You are a helpful assistant" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p" `; const result = await aikit.executeActionFromText(yamlDefinition); console.log(result); Parameters: yamlStr: YAML string defining the workflow Returns: ActionContextData object with workflow results

Generate Keywords Button​ $("#generateKeywords").click(async function () { var aikit = SwingProActions.getAiKitApi(); const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion( "Extract 5-10 relevant keywords from this article content", { systemPrompt: "You are an SEO expert. Return only comma-separated keywords.", model: "gpt-6-luna", ctx: ctx, // Swing Context } ); // Update the keywords field $("#keywords-field").val(result.text); });

Always wrap API calls in try-catch blocks: $("#process-button").click(async function () { try { var aikit = SwingProActions.getAiKitApi(); if (!aikit) { console.error("ProActions API not available"); return; } const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion("Process this content", { ctx: ctx, }); // Handle success updateUI(result); } catch (error) { console.error("ProActions execution failed:", error); // Show user-friendly error message showErrorNotification("AI processing failed. Please try again."); } });

Ensure the Swing context is properly passed: // In object panel postFillForm: function (ctx) { $("#aiButton").click(function () { // Pass the ctx from the closure SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "my_action"); }); }
Use consistent, descriptive action IDs: # Good - title: "Generate SEO Title" id: "text_calc_seo_title" # Avoid - title: "SEO" id: "action1"

Check service availability before using specific services: const services = aikit.listServices("completion"); const serviceName = services.includes("OPENAI_COMPLETION") ? "OPENAI_COMPLETION" : "HUB"; const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion(prompt, { serviceName: serviceName, });

Show loading indicators during API calls: $("#process-button").click(async function () { const $button = $(this); $button.prop("disabled", true).text("Processing..."); try { const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion("...", { ctx: ctx }); updateUI(result); } catch (error) { handleError(error); } finally { $button.prop("disabled", false).text("Process"); } });

Issue: SwingProActions is not defined Ensure ProActions extension is loaded before your custom scripts Check browser console for loading errors Issue: Action doesn't execute Verify the action ID matches exactly (case-sensitive) Check that the action is defined in pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml Ensure the context is valid Issue: API returns undefined Check that the extension is loaded: SwingProActions.extensions.get("pro-actions-ai-kit") Verify the service is configured in the services section Issue: Toolbar buttons don't appear Verify tab creation code runs before button registration Check command names match between command registration and button configuration Clear browser cache

Enable verbose logging: // Check if ProActions is loaded console.log("ProActions available:", typeof SwingProActions !== "undefined"); // Check if API is accessible var aikit = SwingProActions.getAiKitApi(); console.log("API available:", !!aikit); // List available services if (aikit) { console.log("Available services:", aikit.listServices()); }

Always validate user input before passing to AI services: const userInput = $("#user-field").val().trim(); if (!userInput || userInput.length > 10000) { showError("Invalid input"); return; } const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion(userInput, { ctx: ctx, });

Implement client-side rate limiting for repeated calls: let lastCallTime = 0; const MIN_INTERVAL = 2000; // 2 seconds $("#ai-button").click(async function () { const now = Date.now(); if (now - lastCallTime < MIN_INTERVAL) { showError("Please wait before making another request"); return; } lastCallTime = now; // Proceed with API call });

Don't expose internal errors to users: try { const result = await aikit.executeChatCompletion(prompt, { ctx: ctx }); } catch (error) { console.error("Internal error:", error); // Log for debugging showError("Processing failed. Please try again."); // User-friendly message }

This guide covers shortening a story by a known amount — typically the overmatter of a print slot — with an LLM that proposes cuts and an editor who chooses them. GET_STORY_BLOCKS reads the story with a size per block, the model answers with ranked cut candidates, and APPLY_TEXT_CUTS measures every candidate, preselects enough of them to reach the target, and lets the editor pick the cuts in a Flow Monitor panel with a live meter and editor highlights.

LLMs are good at deciding what can go and bad at hitting a length target. The work is split accordingly: The model only proposes cuts: delete a paragraph, drop or condense a passage, and alternatives for the same passage. It ranks them by priority. ProActions measures what each cut really saves, works out which cuts cannot be combined, and preselects cuts until the target is reached. The editor checks, unchecks or swaps cuts in the cut panel and applies the selection in one validated write. Four pieces work together: GET_STORY_BLOCKS with showLength: true — reads the story as numbered blocks and appends each block's character count. response_format: text_cuts — makes the completion step answer with a strict JSON list of cut candidates. APPLY_TEXT_CUTS — measures, preselects, and then previews, applies, or opens the cut panel. The cut panel — a dedicated Flow Monitor view with a meter, the cuts grouped by paragraph, and live highlights in the editor. The cut engine is built on the same block engine as Story Text Edits: links, embedded objects, placeholders and strikeouts are protected, and a cut that would damage them is never offered. Ready-to-use configuration A complete, commented section — input in characters or lines, up to three rounds of "ask for more cuts", and an outcome message — is shown in Complete Section Example. Copy it, adapt the values marked ◆ ADAPT, and include it in SECTIONS.

Read — GET_STORY_BLOCKS with showLength: true renders one line per block with its size ([b3 text/p · 412] …) and remembers each block's text as the stale-block guard. Ask — a completion step with response_format: text_cuts receives the blocks and answers with {"cuts": […]}. The parsed answer lands in flowContext.object. Measure — APPLY_TEXT_CUTS resolves every cut alone against a copy of the story and measures the characters it removes. Cuts that cannot be resolved, or that do not shorten the story, are reported in failed[] and never offered. Preselect — candidates that cannot be combined are linked as conflicts, and the cheapest set of cuts that reaches the target is checked. Choose and apply — in review mode the editor adjusts the selection in the cut panel; the chosen cuts are written in one atomic batch, and the story length is measured again afterwards.

showLength: true appends each block's visible character count to its line, so the model can size its cuts instead of guessing: [b1 text/p · 412] Major League Soccer's 2026 season has begun, with matches again streaming on Apple TV. … [b2 text/p · 618] The agreement also extends to more than 300,000 bars, restaurants and hotels. … [b3 text/p · 509] Apple TV, launched in 2019, has expanded its offerings beyond original films and series. … Block ids are unchanged (b1, b2, …), so edits and cuts parse the same way with or without sizes. Add an output of type json to also get the measured length as data: - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story/text showLength: true outputs: - type: text name: blocks - type: json name: storyLength # { chars: 1539, blocks: [{ id: "b1", role: "text/p", chars: 412 }, …] } The json output is written only when it is configured, so existing flows are unaffected. Choose xpath to match the print frame. The meter counts the characters of the blocks under xpath. If the overmatter refers to the body text, read only the body (Méthode story DTD: /doc/story/text); reading /doc/story would also count — and offer to cut — headline, summary and captions. Use the same xpath, blockElements, ignoreElements and inlineElements on GET_STORY_BLOCKS and APPLY_TEXT_CUTS, exactly as for story text edits.

A block's size is its visible text with every whitespace run counted as one space and the ends trimmed. Inline tags, hidden markup, and strikeout text do not count. The story length is the sum over the blocks. It can therefore differ slightly from the editor's own character counter, which may count line breaks or hidden text differently — the meter and the report always use this one definition, so the numbers are comparable with each other.

With response_format: text_cuts the completion step (OPENAI_COMPLETION, HUB_COMPLETION, AZURE_OPENAI_COMPLETION) sends a strict JSON schema named text_cuts: The root object is { "cuts": [...] }; an empty array means nothing can be cut. Every item carries all seven fields — op, block, find, replace, priority, group, reason — and unused string fields are "". No system prompt is injected. The field rules live in the schema descriptions, so behavior must state the editorial rules (what may be cut, what must stay). Field Meaning op delete, replace or rewrite (see below). block Block id, e.g. b3. find replace only: exact text copied from the block, unique within it, including inline tags. replace replace: the shorter text ("" removes the passage). rewrite: the complete shortened block. priority 1 = least important, cut first; 2 = normal; 3 = cut only if needed. Any other value counts as 2. group The same non-empty label on cuts that are alternatives for the same passage; at most one of them is applied. "" when the cut has no alternative. reason Short explanation shown to the editor. Op Effect delete Removes the whole block. replace Replaces find with the shorter replace; an empty replace removes the passage. rewrite Replaces the block with the condensed version in replace; only the differences are applied. Every cut must make sense on its own: the editor may apply any combination of cuts that are not alternatives of each other. An answer for the sample story above: { "cuts": [ { "op": "replace", "block": "b2", "find": " and player-curated city guides", "replace": "", "priority": 1, "group": "guides", "reason": "secondary feature" }, { "op": "rewrite", "block": "b2", "find": "", "replace": "The agreement also extends to bars and hotels. Apple Maps provides Matchday Guides.", "priority": 2, "group": "guides", "reason": "condense the paragraph" }, { "op": "delete", "block": "b3", "find": "", "replace": "", "priority": 2, "group": "", "reason": "background on the service" } ] } The first two cuts are alternatives (group guides); the third is independent. Pass the blocks with | safe When the blocks are part of a longer template — for example an instruction: block with more text — write {{ flowContext.blocks | safe }}. Without | safe, the template engine escapes <b> to <b>, the model copies the escaped text into find, and the cuts fail with not_found. A template that consists only of "{{ flowContext.blocks }}" is passed through unchanged.

APPLY_TEXT_CUTS takes the target in one of two units: Option Meaning cutBy Characters to remove, e.g. the overmatter. targetLength The desired story length; cutBy becomes current length − targetLength. Set exactly one of them (they conflict in the schema). Both accept a number or a template such as "{{ flowContext.cutBy }}"; a value that does not resolve to a number fails the step with APPLY_TEXT_CUTS: cutBy must be a number (or targetLength). When the input is a proposal from an earlier run (see Outputs), both options are optional: without them the proposal's own target is used. A new target on a proposal re-runs the preselection only for mode: apply with an automatic selection; in review the editor sees the new target in the meter and adjusts. If the story already fits (cutBy ≤ 0), the step reports action: fits and does nothing else. Lines instead of characters. charsPerLine (default 0 = off) adds an estimated line count to the meter and the report. Use the average characters per line of your print column; the estimate is deliberately simple (each block rounds up to whole lines, headings are not weighted). To let editors enter the overmatter in lines, convert it in a SCRIPTING step — the complete example accepts both 350 and 12 lines.

Measurement. Each cut is resolved and applied alone on a copy of the story, and its saving is the length difference. Because cuts are measured individually, the meter is exact for any combination of compatible cuts. A cut whose saving is not positive is reported as no_saving. Conflicts. Two cuts cannot be applied together when: they share a non-empty group (alternatives), or the block engine reports that they overlap — the same text, a rewrite and another edit of the same block, or a delete of a block another cut edits. Conflicts are symmetric. In the panel, checking a cut unchecks its conflicting cuts, so swapping an alternative is one click. Structure. A delete may not remove the last element of its type under its parent (the story must keep at least one paragraph of each kind). The panel disables such a delete with the tooltip Keep at least one block of this type, and the preselection skips it. Preselection. Starting from the lowest priority level that still has addable cuts, the smallest cut that covers the remaining amount is chosen; if none is large enough, the largest one is taken and the search continues. Ties go to the earlier cut. The result is deterministic: the same proposal always preselects the same cuts. Because priority 1 is used up first, the preselection may overshoot the target when the least important cut is large — the editor can swap it in the panel. Limits. At most 60 cuts are accepted per round (the rest fail with too_many_candidates), and a cut identical to an earlier one fails with duplicate. Only delete, replace and rewrite are accepted; any other op fails with op_not_allowed.
