documents.t: Mode Writes? Allowed on a read-only document? Output review (default) once, with what the editor applies no (unless forceWrite: true) TextCutReport preview never yes TextCutProposal apply once, the preselection or selection no (unless forceWrite: true) TextCutReport Every write is atomic: either all selected cuts are applied or none. A selection that contains two alternatives, or deletes every block of one type, is refused before anything is written. apply. Writes the preselection, or the ids in selection (an array such as ["c1","c3"], a comma-separated string, or a template). selection: auto (the default) and all both mean the preselection. preview. Returns the proposal and, with mark: true (default), highlights the preselected cuts. In Swing the highlights are virtual; in Prime they are stored as <mark> elements until CLEAR_TAGS removes them.

mode: review opens the cut panel in the Flow Monitor: Header — Cut 300 characters: 1962 → 1662. Uncheck what must stay, check alternatives to swap. Meter — Cut 238 of 300 characters, the new story length (Story: 1962 → 1724 characters), the estimated lines when charsPerLine is set, and either Target reached or 62 characters still missing. The bar turns from the warning to the success colour when the target is reached. Toolbar — Auto-select restores the preselection; Clear unchecks everything. Cuts — grouped by paragraph (b2 text/p · 618), each with a checkbox, its priority (P1), its saving (−126), the removed text struck through and the replacement, the reason, and Alternative to c2 where applicable. Actions — Apply selected cuts, Ask for more cuts (only with allowMore: true), and Cancel. With mark: true (default) the checked cuts are highlighted in the editor and the highlights follow every checkbox change. They are removed when the panel closes, whatever the outcome. The meter, toolbar and row labels follow the ProActions language (English, German, French, Italian, Spanish); the header and the action buttons are in English. The panel needs an enabled Flow Monitor (monitor: enabled: true on the section or action) and a writable document.

Ask for more cuts ends the step without writing and reports action: more, with the editor's current selection in proposal.preselected. A flow can then ask the model again and pass the earlier proposal with previous: - step: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS mode: review cutBy: "{{ flowContext.cutBy }}" allowMore: true previous: cutResult.proposal # a flowContext path; absent in the first round outputs: - type: object name: cutResult The earlier cuts are re-measured and keep their ids (c1, c2, …), new cuts continue the numbering, and the editor's selection is kept and topped up. previous is a path into the flow context, not a template; if nothing is stored there yet the step starts fresh, and a value that is not a cut proposal fails with APPLY_TEXT_CUTS: previous is not a cut proposal. Put the round in a WHILE loop as in the complete example.

preview writes a TextCutProposal to object: Field Contents kind Always "text_cut_proposal" xpath Content root the proposal belongs to cutBy Characters to remove currentChars Story length now charsPerLine Line estimate setting (0 = off) blocks [{ id, chars }] in document order candidates The usable cuts (see below) preselected Ids checked for the target failed Refused cuts: [{ index, op, block, error, hint }], index being the position in the cut list siblingCounts Internal: block-type counts used by the structure rule Each candidate has id (c1, c2, …), block, role, op, saves, priority, conflicts (ids), before and after (display text without tags), reason, plus the resolved edit and the highlight ranges. A delete also carries a siblingKey. review and apply write a TextCutReport: Field Contents kind Always "text_cut_report" action What happened (see below) cutBy Target in characters selected Ids of the selection the report is about plannedSaving Characters the selection removes missing Characters still missing: max(0, cutBy − plannedSaving) lengthBefore / lengthAfter Story length before and after; measured again after a write, equal when nothing was written linesAfter Estimated lines after the selection, on apply results when charsPerLine > 0 hint Why nothing was written, for failed, empty and fits edits The underlying TextEditReport when a write was attempted proposal The proposal; preselected holds the selection — feed it to previous for the next round action Meaning Written? applied The selection was written. yes cancelled The editor cancelled, or applied an empty selection. no more The editor asked for more cuts. no fits cutBy ≤ 0: the story already fits. no empty The model proposed no usable cut. no failed The selection was invalid, or the write was refused (see hint). no Branch on action to tell the editor what happened: - step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.cutResult.action }}" cases: applied: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: success message: "Cut {{ flowContext.cutResult.lengthBefore - flowContext.cutResult.lengthAfter }} characters." failed: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: error message: "Nothing was written: {{ flowContext.cutResult.hint | safe }}"

- step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story/text showLength: true outputs: - type: text name: blocks - step: MONITOR_INPUT message: "How many characters must be cut?" required: true outputs: - type: text name: cutByText - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_cuts behavior: | You are a newspaper sub-editor. Propose cuts to shorten the story. Never change facts, names, numbers or direct quotes. Prefer removing sentences over rewriting. Give every cut a priority and put alternative cuts of the same passage in one group. instruction: | {{ flowContext.blocks | safe }} Propose 5 to 10 cuts that together remove at least {{ (flowContext.cutByText | int) * 2 }} characters. - step: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS mode: review xpath: /doc/story/text cutBy: "{{ flowContext.cutByText }}" charsPerLine: 34

Works on read-only documents: the preselection is highlighted and the candidates are shown as a table (MONITOR_TABLE needs the Flow Monitor). - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story/text showLength: true - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_cuts behavior: "You are a newspaper sub-editor. Propose cuts to shorten the story without changing facts." instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS mode: preview xpath: /doc/story/text cutBy: 800 outputs: - type: object name: cuts - step: SCRIPTING script: | flowContext.cutRows = flowContext.cuts.candidates.map((cut) => ({ '#': cut.id, Block: cut.block, Saves: cut.saves, Priority: cut.priority, Cut: cut.before, Reason: cut.reason, })); return flowContext; - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Cut candidates (preselected: {{ flowContext.cuts.preselected | join(', ') }})" data: "{{ flowContext.cutRows }}" Remove the highlights with CLEAR_TAGS and tags: ["mark"] (or your markTag) when the editor is done.

No panel: the preselection is written directly. Use it only where an unattended cut is acceptable. - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS xpath: /doc/story/text showLength: true - step: HUB_COMPLETION response_format: text_cuts behavior: "You are a newspaper sub-editor. Propose cuts to shorten the story without changing facts." instruction: "{{ flowContext.text }}" - step: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS mode: apply xpath: /doc/story/text targetLength: 4500 selection: auto
documents.s: Cut automatically to a target length

documents.t: The production-ready section: the editor enters the amount in characters or lines, the model proposes cuts in up to three rounds, and an outcome message closes the flow. Values marked ◆ ADAPT are defined once and reused through YAML anchors. # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/em-al-wi/proactions-schema/main/schema/partial-section.schema.json section: Cut to Length context: story keywords: cut trim shorten overmatter length copyfit print monitor: enabled: true # the cut panel lives in the Flow Monitor defaultWidth: 620 actions: - id: proactions.text-cut.review title: "Cut story to length" keywords: cut trim shorten overmatter kürzen flow: # ── Settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── - step: SET charsPerLine: &charsPerLine 34 # ◆ ADAPT: average characters per print line maxRounds: 3 # ◆ ADAPT: LLM rounds the editor can request in total # ── 1 · Read the story ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── - step: GET_STORY_BLOCKS monitorLabel: "Reading the story" xpath: &xpath /doc/story/text # ◆ ADAPT: root of the print text ignoreElements: &ignoreElements [] # ◆ ADAPT: e.g. [factbox, quotebox] inlineElements: &inlineElements [b, i, u, em, strong] # ◆ ADAPT: inline tags of your DTD showLength: true outputs: - type: text name: blocks - type: json name: storyLength # ── 2 · How much must go? ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── - step: MONITOR_INPUT message: >- The story has {{ flowContext.storyLength.chars }} characters. How much must be cut? Enter characters (e.g. 350) or lines (e.g. 12 lines). placeholder: "e.g. 350 or 12 lines" required: true outputs: - type: text name: cutByText # Accepts "350", "-350", "350 characters", "12 lines" / "12 Zeilen" / "12 lignes" … - step: SCRIPTING script: | const raw = String(flowContext.cutByText || '').trim(); const number = raw.match(/\d+/); const amount = number ? Number(number[0]) : 0; const inLines = /(line|zeile|ligne|rig[ah]|l[ií]nea)/i.test(raw); flowContext.cutBy = inLines ? amount * flowContext.charsPerLine : amount; flowContext.cutRound = 0; flowContext.cutAction = 'more'; return flowContext; - step: IF condition: "{{ flowContext.cutBy <= 0 }}" then: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: warning message: 'Please enter a number of characters (e.g. 350) or lines (e.g. "12 lines").' - step: END_IF condition: "{{ flowContext.cutBy <= 0 }}" # ── 3 · Propose, choose, apply ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── - step: WHILE condition: "{{ flowContext.cutRound < flowContext.maxRounds and flowContext.cutAction == 'more' }}" do: - step: SCRIPTING script: | flowContext.cutRound = flowContext.cutRound + 1; // Ask for clearly more than is needed, so the editor has a real choice. const pending = flowContext.cutResult ? flowContext.cutResult.missing : flowContext.cutBy; flowContext.cutGoal = Math.ceil(1.75 * Math.max(pending, flowContext.cutBy / 2)); const earlier = flowContext.cutResult ? flowContext.cutResult.proposal.candidates : []; flowContext.covered = earlier .map((cut) => '- ' + cut.block + ' ' + cut.op + ': ' + cut.before.slice(0, 80)) .join('\n'); return flowContext; - step: HUB_COMPLETION monitorLabel: "Proposing cuts (round {{ flowContext.cutRound }})" response_format: text_cuts behavior: | You are an experienced newspaper sub-editor. The story must be shortened to fit its print slot. You propose cuts; the editor decides which of them are applied. Editorial rules (◆ ADAPT to your house style): - Never change facts, names, numbers, dates or direct quotes. Never add information. - Keep the language and the tone of the story; a shortened passage must read naturally. - Cut in this order: repetitions and redundant information, decorative detail and colour, additional examples, background, secondary reactions and quotes. Keep the core news (who, what, when, where, why) and the main quotes. - Prefer removing whole sentences or clauses over rewriting. Use "rewrite" only to condense a paragraph whose content must stay. - Give the editor a real choice: several small and medium cuts (a clause, a sentence, a paragraph) spread over the story, rather than a few large ones. Where useful, offer alternatives for the same passage, e.g. drop a sentence vs. condense it. Format (keep unchanged): - Every story line is "[id role · characters] text". Put the id (e.g. "b3") in "block" and use the character count to size your cuts. - Every cut must stand on its own: the editor may apply any combination of cuts that are not alternatives of each other. - Two or more cuts of the same passage are alternatives: give them the same "group" label. A cut without alternatives has an empty group. - priority: 1 = cut first (least important), 2 = normal, 3 = only if needed. - op "delete": removes the whole paragraph; "find" and "replace" are empty. - op "replace": "find" is copied character by character from the paragraph — typographic quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), apostrophes, dashes and inline tags such as … exactly as they appear — and occurs only once in it; "replace" is the shorter text. An empty "replace" removes the passage: then include one adjacent space in "find" so no double space remains. - op "rewrite": "replace" is the complete shortened paragraph, keeping its inline tags; "find" is empty. - reason: what is removed and why, in a few words and in the language of the story; no character counts. - Return an empty "cuts" array when nothing can be cut without losing essential content. instruction: | {{ flowContext.blocks | safe }} The story has {{ flowContext.storyLength.chars }} characters and must lose {{ flowContext.cutBy }}. Propose 5 to 10 cuts of different sizes that together remove at least {{ flowContext.cutGoal }} characters, so the editor can combine them to fit. {% if flowContext.covered %} These cuts were already proposed. Do not repeat them; propose different ones: {{ flowContext.covered | safe }} {% endif %} - step: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS mode: review cutBy: "{{ flowContext.cutBy }}" charsPerLine: *charsPerLine allowMore: true previous: cutResult.proposal # merges the earlier rounds (absent in round 1) xpath: *xpath ignoreElements: *ignoreElements inlineElements: *inlineElements outputs: - type: object name: cutResult - step: SET cutAction: "{{ flowContext.cutResult.action }}" # ── 4 · Outcome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── - step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.cutResult.action }}" cases: applied: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: success message: >- Cut {{ flowContext.cutResult.lengthBefore - flowContext.cutResult.lengthAfter }} characters: {{ flowContext.cutResult.lengthBefore }} → {{ flowContext.cutResult.lengthAfter }}. {% if flowContext.cutResult.missing > 0 %}Still {{ flowContext.cutResult.missing }} characters short of the target — run the action again for more cuts.{% endif %} more: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: warning message: >- No cuts were applied after {{ flowContext.maxRounds }} rounds. Run the action again to start over. cancelled: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: info message: "Cancelled — the story was not changed." empty: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: warning message: "No usable cuts were proposed: {{ flowContext.cutResult.hint | safe }}" failed: - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: error message: "Nothing was written: {{ flowContext.cutResult.hint | safe }}" To take the amount from a copyfit service instead of asking the editor, replace MONITOR_INPUT with a step that writes the overmatter (characters or lines) to flowContext.cutByText.

A refused cut never reaches the editor. It is listed in proposal.failed[] with an error and a hint: Code Meaning What to do not_found find does not occur in the block. Tell the model to copy find character by character, including typographic quotes and inline tags; pass the blocks with ` ambiguous_match find occurs more than once in the block. Ask for longer, unique find strings. stale_block The block changed since the read, or the steps use different block options. Re-run GET_STORY_BLOCKS; use identical options on both steps. unknown_block The block id is not in the read. Use the ids from GET_STORY_BLOCKS. op_not_allowed The op is not delete, replace or rewrite. The text_cuts schema already restricts ops; check custom schemas. protected_markup The cut would remove hidden content (embedded objects, strikeouts, placeholders). Expected: such paragraphs can be shortened with replace/rewrite, not deleted. structure_required The delete would remove the only block of its type. Expected: shorten the block instead. no_saving The cut does not make the story shorter. Harmless; the model lengthened or only reworded the passage. unchanged The cut changes nothing. Harmless. duplicate The same cut was already proposed in this or an earlier round. Harmless; the first one is kept. too_many_candidates More than 60 usable cuts in one round. Ask for fewer, larger cuts. escaped_markup, replacement_not_well_formed, disallowed_elements, disallowed_attributes, disallowed_node_type The replacement is not valid content. Return plain text plus the inline tags shown in the block view. When an applied selection fails, report.action is failed, hint explains why, and report.edits holds the story text edits report with per-edit errors. Step-level failures stop the flow instead: APPLY_TEXT_CUTS: set cutBy or targetLength, cutBy must be a number, previous is not a cut proposal, cuts must be an array or an object with a "cuts" array, mode must be one of review, preview, apply, Review mode requires the Flow Monitor, and the read-only error.

Review mode requires the Flow Monitor — set monitor: enabled: true on the section or action, or use mode: preview. It is not possible to write content in read-only mode! — the story is not checked out; use mode: preview or forceWrite: true for trusted flows. Many not_found failures — the blocks reached the model escaped (<b>): use {{ flowContext.blocks | safe }} in multi-line instructions. Otherwise the model re-typed quotes or dropped inline tags; ask it to copy find character by character. Only a few, large cuts — ask for a number of cuts of different sizes ("5 to 10 cuts of different sizes"), and for more characters than needed so the editor can combine. The preselection overshoots — the least important cuts (priority 1) are used first, even when large. Swap them in the panel, or ask the model to rank large cuts as priority 2. The meter disagrees with the layout — the meter counts the blocks under xpath. Point xpath at the element the print frame shows (e.g. /doc/story/text), and set charsPerLine to your column's average. Highlights stay in a Prime story after a preview — run CLEAR_TAGS with tags: ["mark"]. The review panel removes its own highlights when it closes. HTTP 400 about response_format or json_schema — text_cuts uses structured outputs; the model or Hub target must support json_schema with strict: true.
APPLY_TEXT_CUTS GET_STORY_BLOCKS Story Text Edits Flow Monitor AI Integration

This guide covers OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT and HUB_VOICE_AGENT — full-duplex voice sessions against the OpenAI Realtime API. The model listens to the microphone, speaks its responses out loud, can call tools and skills mid-conversation, and hands back a transcript (and optionally structured data) when the session ends.

A voice agent step opens a live audio session instead of a single request/response completion: - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT service: OPENAI_REALTIME behavior: | You are a helpful editorial voice assistant. After completing a task, ask "Is there anything else I can help you with?" Keep the conversation going until the user explicitly says they are done. Only call end_session after: (1) you have spoken all results verbally, (2) the user confirms they are done. Never call it after just one task. voice: marin maxDurationSecs: 300 The step runs until the model calls end_session, the user clicks End session in the pinned voice bar, or maxDurationSecs elapses (default 300s). When it finishes, the transcript is written to flowContext.text and any structured result the model provided to flowContext.object, so downstream steps can act on the conversation like any other completion. OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT connects directly using a short-lived ephemeral key from your OpenAI service configuration. HUB_VOICE_AGENT is identical but routes through ProActions Hub over WebSocket (a proxy cannot relay WebRTC media), for centralized key management without exposing OpenAI credentials to the browser. When to use a voice agent: You need a live, spoken conversation — microphone in, audio out The model should perform actions or call tools while talking You want a transcript for downstream steps (summaries, logging, structured extraction) When not to: text-only interaction (use OPENAI_COMPLETION/HUB_COMPLETION), or transcribing audio without a live back-and-forth (use OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION).

Voice agents require all of the following: A secure browser context (https://) with microphone permission MediaDevices.getUserMedia, Web Audio API, and AudioWorklet support The Flow Monitor enabled, because the pinned Voice Bar contains the session controls A Realtime-capable OpenAI model, such as gpt-realtime-2.1 Network and Content Security Policy (CSP) rules that permit the connections described below For direct OpenAI sessions, the browser needs HTTPS and WSS access to api.openai.com; WebRTC media must also be permitted for the preferred transport. If WebRTC negotiation fails, the step falls back to WebSocket. For Hub sessions, Swing or Prime must provide an EDAPI token. The browser needs WSS access to the Hub relay, and Hub needs WSS egress to api.openai.com:443. Standalone clients cannot run HUB_VOICE_AGENT because they do not provide the required EDAPI token.

Use a dedicated service entry for voice agents. A voice endpoint is a base URL: the step appends /v1/realtime/... for direct OpenAI or /proactions/realtime for Hub. Do not reuse a completion service whose endpoint already ends in /v1 or /proactions.

Hub keeps the OpenAI API key on the server. Define a dedicated service in /SysConfig/ProActions/services.ai-kit.services.yaml: HUB_REALTIME: # The step appends /proactions/realtime, producing # {BASE_URL}/swing/proactions/realtime in a standard Swing deployment. endpoint: '{BASE_URL}/swing' target: openai-realtime model: gpt-realtime-2.1 Then reference it from the step: - step: HUB_VOICE_AGENT service: HUB_REALTIME behavior: | You are a helpful voice assistant. Ask whether the user needs anything else before calling end_session. The target must identify an OpenAI Realtime-capable target in Hub. Claude, Gemini, and ordinary chat-completion targets are not interchangeable with a Realtime target. The Hub administrator must configure the matching target and deploy a Hub version that provides the Realtime WebSocket relay — requires ProActions Hub 1.3.0 or later with hub.realtime enabled. See Realtime Relay. # ProActions Hub config.yaml aiTargets: - id: openai-realtime provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} options: model: gpt-realtime-2.1 realtime: enabled: true The deployment must expose WSS /proactions/realtime, authenticate the EDAPI or Hub token sent in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, preserve the requested WebSocket subprotocols, and forward the selected target to OpenAI Realtime. If a reverse proxy sits in front of Hub, configure WebSocket upgrades, trusted TLS, and a connection timeout long enough for maxDurationSecs. Confirm relay availability with your Hub administrator; a Hub installation that only exposes the HTTP endpoints under /v1 does not support HUB_VOICE_AGENT. At session start, AI-Kit automatically verifies that the WebSocket upgrade selects the realtime subprotocol and that Hub creates the upstream OpenAI session within 15 seconds. It fails before opening the microphone when the relay route, authentication, proxy subprotocol forwarding, target credentials, or Hub egress are not ready.

Direct mode loads the long-lived OpenAI API key into browser-delivered ProActions configuration so it can request a short-lived session key. The audio session uses the short-lived key, but this does not prevent a browser user from inspecting the configured long-lived key. Prefer Hub for production use. # /SysConfig/ProActions/services.ai-kit.services.yaml OPENAI_REALTIME: apiKey: 'sk-...' # Base URL only: do not append /v1. endpoint: 'https://api.openai.com' model: gpt-realtime-2.1 - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT service: OPENAI_REALTIME behavior: | You are a helpful voice assistant. Ask whether the user needs anything else before calling end_session. OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT defaults to a service named OPENAI_COMPLETION for compatibility. Only rely on that default when the service already uses the base endpoint https://api.openai.com and a Realtime model. A typical completion endpoint such as https://api.openai.com/v1 is not valid for this step. Voice steps resolve behavior from the step itself and do not inherit defaultBehavior from the service. Configure behavior explicitly unless a loaded skill supplies all required instructions, including when to call end_session.

OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT defaults to WebRTC — OpenAI's recommendation for browser clients, with native echo cancellation and automatic barge-in truncation. If the WebRTC handshake can't complete (e.g. UDP blocked by a firewall), the step automatically falls back to WebSocket; a warning is posted to the monitor when this happens. - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT transport: websocket # force WebSocket instead of the WebRTC/auto-fallback default HUB_VOICE_AGENT always uses WebSocket — the Hub proxy relays the connection, and WebRTC media can't be proxied. Microphone-permission and hardware errors (denied access, no device found) are surfaced as clear, localized messages and are not retried over the fallback transport — the WebSocket path needs the same microphone, so silently retrying would only replace an explicit permission error with a confusing timeout.

By default the model decides when the user has finished speaking (semantic_vad). Tune it via vad:: - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT vad: type: semantic_vad # or server_vad eagerness: low # semantic_vad only — how quickly it ends a turn bargeIn: speech # default — the user's voice interrupts the agent; # set 'off' for noisy rooms (speech is still # captured and answered after the response ends) For noisy environments, server_vad gives you explicit silence-duration control: vad: type: server_vad threshold: 0.6 # raise for noisy rooms (default 0.5) prefixPaddingMs: 300 silenceDurationMs: 500 idleTimeoutMs: 15000 # prompt the user after 15s of silence (server_vad only, 5000-30000) Background noise is additionally filtered server-side before it reaches VAD or the model: noiseReduction: far_field # default — laptop/desk/conference mics # noiseReduction: near_field # headset users # noiseReduction: none # leave unconfigured

Set type: push_to_talk to disable server-side VAD entirely. The model never decides when the user is done speaking — the user explicitly opens and closes the mic via a hold control in the voice bar: vad: type: push_to_talk The VAD tuning fields (eagerness, threshold, prefixPaddingMs, silenceDurationMs, idleTimeoutMs) are ignored in this mode — there is no automatic turn detection to tune. bargeIn applies in every mode (see below). Controls — the voice bar renders a single hold button instead of the mute toggle: Mouse: press and hold to talk, release to send Touch: tap and hold, lift to send Keyboard: hold Space while the monitor panel has focus, release to send — clicking anywhere in the monitor (the transcript, the bar) focuses it. Space keeps its normal behavior in the monitor's text inputs and on focused buttons, and is never captured while you are typing in the editor. Barge-in while the agent is speaking is controlled by bargeIn: vad: type: push_to_talk bargeIn: press # press (default) | speech | off press (default) — pressing the hold control interrupts playback immediately and opens the mic. The press gesture doubles as barge-in; there is no separate interrupt affordance. speech — the agent keeps talking while you hold, and is cut off the moment your voice is actually detected on the microphone. Resting a finger on the control (or an accidental grab) never interrupts. When microphone analysis is available, a hold with no detected speech is discarded instead of being transcribed. off — never interrupt. Presses while the agent is responding are refused: the mic stays closed and the release does nothing. Wait for the Ready — hold the button to talk label, then press. Use this when the agent's answer must always be heard in full (e.g. spoken confirmations). bargeIn is the same field in every mode: under semantic_vad/server_vad the default is speech (the server's own barge-in trigger) and off lets the agent finish while your speech is captured and answered afterwards; press exists only under push_to_talk, where it is the default. Short presses: a hold shorter than ~300ms is treated as an accidental tap — the buffered audio is discarded instead of sent, so the agent won't respond to a quick brush of the button. Between presses the bar's label tracks the session: Processing… / Responding… while the agent works on your turn, and Ready — hold the button to talk once it is your turn again. Wait for the ready label before pressing again — pressing while the agent is responding is the barge-in gesture and cancels the rest of its answer. A complete push-to-talk step — everything outside vad: works exactly as in the other examples in this guide: - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT # or HUB_VOICE_AGENT behavior: | You are a helpful editorial voice assistant. Only call end_session after you have spoken all results and the user confirms they are done. vad: type: push_to_talk bargeIn: speech # agent yields as soon as the user's voice is heard; # omit for the default (press interrupts immediately) maxDurationSecs: 300 builtinTools: - class: StoryEditor config: fields: headline: '/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p' Use this mode for noisy or shared environments where automatic VAD would trigger falsely, or where explicit control over when the model listens is required.

- step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT model: gpt-realtime-2.1 # falls back to the service config's model, then gpt-realtime-2 voice: marin # output voice (default: marin) reasoningEffort: low # reasoning-capable models only (gpt-realtime-2 family); default: low transcriptionModel: gpt-4o-transcribe # server-side transcription of the user's speech reasoningEffort: low is OpenAI's recommendation for production voice agents — it keeps latency down while retaining basic reasoning. Use none to omit the field entirely for non-reasoning models.

Voice agents resolve tools, builtinTools, skills, when: conditions, and config: blocks through the same request builder as OPENAI_COMPLETION — anything you already know about tool calling applies here, with one difference: everything is resolved once, when the session starts, not per turn. - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT behavior: | You are a helpful editorial voice assistant. ... skills: - editorial-style builtinTools: - class: StoryEditor config: fields: headline: '/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p' summary: '/doc/story/summary/p' - alias: web_search target: mcp.brave-search-server.brave_web_search args: ui_lang: en-US autoDiscoverTools: true Skills loaded via skills: are prepended to the session's behavior before it is sent to the Realtime API, and read_skill_reference/read_skill_instruction become callable tools exactly as in a completion step. See the Agent Skills guide. when: conditions and config: blocks on builtinTools entries are evaluated once at session start against the editor/flow state at that moment — see Conditional Tool Exposure and Configuring Built-in Tools. A read-only document, for example, can drop all writing tools from the session entirely. autoDiscoverTools: true works during a live session: when the model calls activateTools, the newly resolved tools are added to the session's tool list and pushed to the running connection via a Realtime session.update — the model can use them in its very next turn without restarting the session. showToolCalls: true displays each tool call in the monitor as a collapsible entry (name, arguments, result) — useful while developing a voice agent's tool set. showToolCalls: true toolsReuseContext: true # pass the full flowContext to tool sub-flows, not just the tool arguments User-defined tools: (script/template/steps-based function calling) work exactly as documented in Tool Calling — the same script, scriptRef, template, and steps handler forms are supported.

The model signals completion by calling the built-in end_session tool — always present, and reserved: a user-defined tool named end_session in your config is replaced by the built-in one, with a warning, since the bridge intercepts that name before user-tool dispatch. Your behavior decides when the conversation is complete. The model can pass a concise human-readable summary and an optional machine-readable result when it calls end_session: behavior: | ... Complete the requested editorial task, then call end_session with a concise summary. The summary is appended to the Step's text output. If the model passes a result object, it is written to flowContext.object by default. An outputs mapping changes the destination key: - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT behavior: | Extract the key facts the user dictates. When done, call end_session with a short summary and result containing the structured facts. outputs: - type: object name: extractedFacts The user can end the session immediately with End session in the pinned voice bar. At maxDurationSecs (default 300), the Step asks the model to finish and call end_session; if it has not completed after a ten-second grace period, the Step force-closes while preserving the transcript and usage collected so far.

Output Description text Markdown-formatted transcript, alternating **You:** / **Agent:** turns object Structured result passed via end_session({ result: ... }) — only written if the model provided one messages Raw transcript array of { role, content } turns, for downstream steps (only written when included in outputs:) usage Token usage accumulated across completed responses (only written when included in outputs:) text is always written and defaults to flowContext.text. object is written only when end_session supplies a result. messages and usage are opt-in and are written only when included in outputs. Every configured name replaces the default flow-context key. - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT behavior: '...' outputs: - type: text name: text - type: object name: object - type: messages name: conversationTurns - type: usage name: voiceUsage - step: MONITOR_STATUS type: success message: | # Session Summary {{ flowContext.text }}

Add the service to /SysConfig/ProActions/services.ai-kit.services.yaml: HUB_REALTIME: endpoint: '{BASE_URL}/swing' target: openai-realtime model: gpt-realtime-2.1 Create /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/voice-assistant.ai-kit.section.yaml: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/em-al-wi/proactions-schema/main/schema/partial-section.schema.json section: Voice Tools context: story monitor: # Voice controls are pinned inside the Flow Monitor. enabled: true actions: - title: Voice Assistant flow: - step: HUB_VOICE_AGENT monitorLabel: Voice Assistant service: HUB_REALTIME model: gpt-realtime-2.1 voice: marin behavior: | You are a helpful editorial voice assistant. Read the story before answering questions about it or editing it. After completing a task, ask whether the user needs anything else. Keep the conversation open until the user explicitly says they are done. Speak all results before calling end_session with a concise summary. builtinTools: - class: StoryEditor config: fields: headline: '/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p' summary: '/doc/story/summary/p' maxDurationSecs: 1200 showToolCalls: true outputs: - type: messages name: voiceConversation - type: usage name: voiceUsage onError: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Voice assistant failed: {{ flowContext.error }}' Include the section from /SysConfig/pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml: AI_KIT: SERVICES: !include /SysConfig/ProActions/services.ai-kit.services.yaml SECTIONS: - !include /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/voice-assistant.ai-kit.section.yaml To use direct OpenAI instead, define OPENAI_REALTIME as shown above and replace the step with: - step: OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT service: OPENAI_REALTIME # WebRTC is the default; use transport: websocket only when explicitly required.

The Voice Agents guide appears under Guides > Configuration and the action appears in the expected CMS context. The browser is in a secure context and microphone permission is granted. The Flow Monitor is enabled and shows the pinned Voice Bar. The configured endpoint is a base URL and does not already end in /v1 or /proactions. The configured model and Hub target support OpenAI Realtime. Direct mode can reach OpenAI over HTTPS/WSS and WebRTC; Hub mode can reach its WebSocket relay. Hub mode runs in Swing or Prime with an available EDAPI token. Reverse proxies preserve WebSocket upgrades and subprotocols, and CSP connect-src permits the required WSS origin. The behavior tells the model when to call end_session. StoryEditor remains available on read-only documents so the agent can read them; its write tools return document_read_only without changing content.

Symptom Check Request URL contains /v1/v1/realtime Use an OpenAI base endpoint without /v1, such as https://api.openai.com. Hub URL contains /proactions/proactions/realtime Use the Hub base endpoint before /proactions; in a standard Swing deployment this is {BASE_URL}/swing. Hub returns 404 or the WebSocket never upgrades The deployed Hub or reverse proxy does not expose /proactions/realtime; contact the Hub administrator. Hub authentication fails Run in Swing/Prime and confirm an EDAPI token is available and WebSocket subprotocol headers are preserved. Direct session uses the wrong model Set model: gpt-realtime-2.1 in the dedicated service or step. Microphone access fails Use HTTPS, grant site permission, verify an input device exists, and check browser policy. WebRTC falls back to WebSocket Check UDP/media negotiation, firewall policy, and browser diagnostics. The fallback is expected when WebRTC cannot connect. Voice Bar does not appear Enable the Flow Monitor for the action/section. Agent never ends the session Add explicit end_session conditions to behavior, or use End session in the Voice Bar. To verify a Hub deployment, run the example flow with browser developer tools open. The Network panel must show a WebSocket request ending in /proactions/realtime?model=... with status 101, and the selected subprotocol must be realtime. Hub logs must show the authenticated CMS user, selected Realtime target, and an upstream connection to OpenAI. A 404 means the relay is unavailable; 401/403 indicates EDAPI authentication or subprotocol forwarding; an upstream connection error indicates target credentials or Hub egress. Use the Hub release supplied by your administrator that explicitly includes this relay; the AI-Kit repository does not define a standalone Hub version number. See Service Configuration, AI Integration, OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT, and HUB_VOICE_AGENT for related configuration details.
This guide covers best practices for designing effective, maintainable, and user-friendly ProActions workflows.

Start with the simplest solution that solves the problem. Good - Simple and clear: - title: 'Improve Text' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Improve this text: {selectedText}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Avoid - Unnecessarily complex: - title: 'Improve Text' flow: - step: GET_TEXT_CONTENT at: CURSOR - step: SET originalText: '{{ flowContext.selectedText }}' - step: IF condition: '{{ flowContext.originalText }}' then: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Improve: {{ flowContext.originalText }}' - step: SET improvedText: '{{ flowContext.text }}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

Each action should do one thing well. Good - Focused actions: - title: 'Translate to French' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'FR' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR - title: 'Translate to German' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'DE' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Avoid - Multi-purpose actions: - title: 'Translate' flow: - step: PROMPT promptText: 'Choose language: FR, DE, ES' - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: '{{ flowContext.text }}' # Complex, error-prone, harder to use

Show complexity only when needed. Good - Start simple, add options: # Basic action - title: 'Generate Headline' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate headline for: {textContent}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: '/doc/story/headline/p' # Advanced action with options - title: 'Generate Headline (Advanced)' flow: - step: FORM form: count: type: number label: 'Number of options' tone: type: select label: 'Tone' options: [Professional, Casual, Urgent] - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate {{ flowContext.count }} {{ flowContext.tone }} headlines' response_format: 'list' - step: USER_SELECT promptText: 'Choose headline:' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: '/doc/story/headline/p'

Use clear, action-oriented titles: Good: - title: 'Translate to French' - title: 'Generate Headline Suggestions' - title: 'Improve Selected Text' - title: 'Create Audio Version' Avoid: - title: 'French' # Unclear what it does - title: 'Headlines' # Is it generating or editing? - title: 'AI' # Too vague - title: 'Process' # What kind of processing?

Group related actions under clear section names: Good: section: Translation Tools section: Content Generation section: Text Enhancement section: Image Processing Avoid: section: AI Tools # Too broad section: Stuff # Unprofessional section: My Actions # Not descriptive

Use descriptive variable names: Good: - step: SET articleTitle: '{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}' targetLanguage: 'FR' wordCountLimit: 500 Avoid: - step: SET t: '{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}' lang: 'FR' n: 500

Always inform users about what's happening: Good - With feedback: - title: 'Generate Article' flow: - step: SHOW_PROGRESS status: 'Generating article...' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Write article about: {selectedText}' - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 50 status: 'Doing something else' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Do something else: {selectedText}' - step: HIDE_PROGRESS - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: 'Article generated successfully' - step: INSERT_TEXT at: CURSOR Avoid - No feedback: - title: 'Generate Article' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Write article about: {selectedText}' - step: INSERT_TEXT at: CURSOR

For UI steps that require data preparation, use inlineSteps to show the interface immediately while processing happens in the background. This improves perceived performance by eliminating wait time. Supported Steps: USER_SELECT, FORM, SHOW_RESPONSE Good - Immediate UI with background processing: - title: 'Suggest Headlines' flow: - step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate 6 headlines for: {textContent}' response_format: 'list' promptText: 'Select a headline' enableKeyboardControl: true - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: '/doc/story/headline/p' How it works: The modal displays immediately with a loading indicator inlineSteps execute in the background When processing completes, results populate the UI seamlessly Errors are displayed in-place within the modal

Check for required input before processing: Good: - title: 'Translate Selection' flow: - step: IF condition: '{{ client.isTextSelected() }}' then: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'FR' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR else: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: warning message: 'Please select text to translate' Avoid: - title: 'Translate Selection' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' # Fails if no text selected - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

Let users make decisions when appropriate: Good: - title: 'Generate Headlines' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate 5 headline options' response_format: 'list' - step: USER_SELECT promptText: 'Choose a headline:' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: '/doc/story/headline/p'
Always give users a way to cancel: Good: - step: FORM form: topic: type: text label: 'Article Topic' required: true buttons: - type: cancel label: 'Cancel' - type: submit label: 'Generate'

Use the END step with notifications to terminate workflows gracefully while informing users: Good - End with notification: - title: 'Process Article' flow: - step: END condition: '{{ not client.isTextSelected() }}' notification: type: 'warning' message: 'Please select text before running this action' title: 'No Selection' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Process: {selectedText}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Also good - Conditional end with context: - title: 'Smart Translation' flow: - step: SET wordCount: "{{ client.getTextContent().split(' ').length }}" convertTo: number - step: END condition: '{{ flowContext.wordCount > 10000 }}' notification: type: 'error' message: 'Text is too long ({{flowContext.wordCount}} words). Maximum is 10,000 words.' title: 'Text Too Long' - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{textContent}' target_lang: 'FR' Avoid - Silent termination: - step: END condition: '{{ someCondition }}' # User doesn't know why workflow stopped

Always handle potential errors: Good: - title: 'Process with AI' flow: - step: TRY try: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Process: {textContent}' - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: 'Processing complete' catch: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Processing failed. Please try again.'

Provide alternatives when services fail: Good: - title: 'Smart Translation' flow: - step: TRY try: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'FR' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR catch: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: warning message: 'Translation service unavailable. Using fallback...' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Translate to French: {selectedText}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

For simpler error handling scenarios, use the onError configuration at the action level. This provides a way to handle errors for the entire action without wrapping individual steps in TRY/CATCH blocks: - title: 'Extract Keywords' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Extract keywords from: {textContent}' response_format: 'list' onError: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Failed to extract keywords. Please try again.' How it works: If any step in the flow throws an error, execution stops The steps in onError are executed instead The error is available in flowContext.error The action's result becomes whatever the onError steps produce — the original error is not re-thrown When to use onError vs TRY/CATCH: Use onError when you need consistent error handling for an entire action Use TRY/CATCH when you need granular error handling for specific steps within a flow Combine both for complex scenarios with both action-level and step-level error handling
ProActions provides several mechanisms to alter how a step runs — wrapping it, changing what it receives, or controlling what it outputs.

Use TRY to intercept a step's failure without aborting the flow: - step: TRY try: - step: REST url: 'https://api.example.com/data' method: GET catch: # Provide a fallback value so the flow can continue - step: SET object: '{ "items": [] }'
documents.s: Wrap a Step with Error Handling (TRY)

documents.t: onError at the action level acts as a top-level catch decorator for the entire flow. Any unhandled error in any step triggers it: - title: 'Process Article' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: '...' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR onError: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Something went wrong: {{ flowContext.error }}'

inlineSteps on USER_SELECT, FORM, and SHOW_RESPONSE runs background steps while the UI is already visible. This effectively wraps the preparation logic around the UI step without blocking: - step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate options for: {textContent}' response_format: list promptText: 'Pick an option:'

Some steps (e.g., SELECTED_OBJECT, REST) let you control the flowContext key they write to via an outputs declaration. Use this when two steps would otherwise write to the same default key: - step: SELECTED_OBJECT outputs: - type: object name: selectedImage # written to flowContext.selectedImage, not flowContext.object - step: REST url: '...' outputs: - type: json name: apiResponse # written to flowContext.apiResponse, not flowContext.json

Use IF to conditionally skip a step group, or END to abort the flow early if a precondition isn't met. Both act as pre-execution guards on the steps they wrap: # Guard: only run the translation if text is actually selected - step: IF condition: '{{ client.isTextSelected() }}' then: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: FR - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR else: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: warning message: 'Select text first' # Abort guard: stop the flow if a word-count limit is exceeded - step: END condition: '{{ flowContext.wordCount > 10000 }}' notification: type: error message: 'Text too long ({{ flowContext.wordCount }} words). Limit is 10,000.'

For HUB_COMPLETION steps that use function/tool calling, the toolErrorBehavior option controls how the LLM reacts to a failed tool invocation — effectively decorating the LLM's internal retry loop: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Look up the latest news on {textContent}' toolErrorBehavior: retry # retry (default) | once | fail maxToolIterations: 5 # cap the total tool-call loop Value Behavior retry (default) LLM may retry a failed tool call in the same completion once A tool that has already failed once is skipped on subsequent calls in the same completion; failure is passed back to the LLM but not retried fail Any tool failure immediately throws an error, stopping the step

Document your intentions: Good: - title: 'Process Article' flow: # Step 1: Extract article content excluding metadata - step: SET text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["caption", "credit"] }) | safe }}' # Step 2: Send to AI for processing - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Summarize: {{ flowContext.text }}' # Step 3: Show result to user for approval - step: SHOW_RESPONSE message: '{{ flowContext.text }}'

Establish and follow patterns across your workflows: Good - Consistent pattern: # All translation actions follow same pattern - title: 'Translate to French' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'FR' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR - title: 'Translate to German' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'DE' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

Set reasonable token limits for LLM calls: Good: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate headline: {textContent}' max_tokens: 100 # Headlines don't need many tokens Avoid: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate headline: {textContent}' # No limit - may waste tokens

Request only the format you need: Good: # For lists - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate 5 topics' response_format: 'list' # For structured data - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Analyze sentiment and extract topics' response_format: 'json_object' # For simple text - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Improve this text' response_format: 'text'

Eliminate redundant operations: Good: - title: 'Translate' flow: - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{selectedText}' target_lang: 'FR' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR Avoid: - title: 'Translate' flow: - step: GET_TEXT_CONTENT at: CURSOR - step: SET textToTranslate: '{{ flowContext.selectedText }}' - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: '{{ flowContext.textToTranslate }}' - step: SET translatedText: '{{ flowContext.text }}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR
Provide sensible defaults: Good: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate content' model: 'gpt-6-luna' options: max_tokens: 500

Define templates for common operations: # In TEMPLATES section TEMPLATES: improveText: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: "You are a professional editor." instruction: "Improve: {selectedText}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR # In actions - title: 'Quick Improve' flow: - step: CALL_TEMPLATE name: improveText

For new configurations, use scoped reusable blocks (BLOCKS, section.blocks, action.blocks) and call flows/scripts by reference. AI_KIT: BLOCKS: flows: improveText: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: 'You are a professional editor.' instruction: 'Improve: {selectedText}' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR SECTIONS: - section: Editing blocks: vars: improveFlowRef: global.flows.improveText actions: - title: Quick Improve flow: - step: CALL_FLOW ref: '{{ section.vars.improveFlowRef }}'
documents.s: Prefer Scoped Reusable Blocks for New Work

documents.t: Keep existing CALL_TEMPLATE.name actions as-is. Add new reusable logic under BLOCKS and start using CALL_FLOW.ref. If needed, use CALL_TEMPLATE.ref as a bridge while migrating. For scripts, move inline SCRIPTING.script snippets to scoped scripts and reference them with SCRIPTING.scriptRef.

When using reusable modules via imports, keep these runtime rules in mind: Section imports are automatically available to every action in the section. Action imports are merged with section imports for that action. If section and action both define the same alias, the action alias overrides in that action scope. Defining the same alias twice in a single imports list is invalid and fails at load time. Circular import chains are detected and rejected. SECTIONS: - section: Editorial imports: - from: /SysConfig/ProActions/lib/common.ai-kit.module.yaml as: common actions: - title: Editorial Rewrite imports: - from: /SysConfig/ProActions/lib/editorial.ai-kit.module.yaml as: common # overrides section alias for this action only flow: - step: CALL_FLOW ref: imports.common.flows.rewrite

Keep service configs in one place: # services.ai-kit.services.yaml HUB: endpoint: '{BASE_URL}/swing/proactions' target: openai defaultBehavior: | You are a professional writing assistant. Provide clear, concise responses. DEEPL: endpoint: /swing/proactions/proxy/forward/deepl
Get feedback from actual users: Is the action name clear? Is the workflow intuitive? Are error messages helpful? Is feedback adequate?

Document changes and maintain versions: # headlines.yaml # Version: 2.0 # Last updated: 2024-01-15 # Changes: Added tone selection, improved prompts section: Headlines actions: - title: 'Generate Headlines' # workflow...
Write for all skill levels: Good: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: 'Translation complete. Your text has been replaced.' Avoid: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: 'NLP proc complete. Obj updated.'

Use tooltips and descriptions: - step: FORM form: temperature: type: range label: 'Creativity Level' tooltip: 'Higher values produce more creative results, lower values are more predictable' min: 0 max: 1 step: 0.1 default: 0.7

- title: 'Improve with Preview' flow: - step: SET originalText: '{selectedText}' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Improve: {{ flowContext.originalText }}' - step: FORM form: comparison: type: diff prevText: '{{ flowContext.originalText }}' text: '{{ flowContext.text }}' showDeletions: true interactive: true buttons: - type: cancel label: 'Keep Original' - type: submit label: 'Use Improved' - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR in: '{{ flowContext.comparison }}'

- title: 'Guided Article Creation' flow: # Step 1: Collect requirements - step: FORM form: topic: type: text label: 'Topic' tone: type: select label: 'Tone' options: [Professional, Casual] # Step 2: Generate outline - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Create article outline about {{ flowContext.topic }}' response_format: 'list' # Step 3: Let user select sections - step: USER_SELECT promptText: 'Choose sections to include:' # Step 4: Generate full article - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Write {{ flowContext.tone }} article about {{ flowContext.text }}' - step: INSERT_TEXT at: CURSOR

- title: 'Process Multiple Items' flow: # ... - step: FOR items: '{{ flowContext.paragraphList }}' var: currentParagraph do: - step: SHOW_PROGRESS message: 'Processing paragraph {{ flowContext.currentParagraph_index }}...' - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Improve: {{ flowContext.currentParagraph }}'

Use WHILE + TRY + SLEEP to retry a failing step a fixed number of times before giving up. This is the standard approach for transient service errors (rate limits, temporary unavailability). - title: 'Generate with Retry' flow: # Initialize retry counter and a flag that signals success - step: SET retryCount: 0 convertTo: number - step: SET retrySuccess: false # Keep looping while we haven't succeeded and haven't exhausted attempts - step: WHILE condition: '{{ not flowContext.retrySuccess and flowContext.retryCount < 3 }}' do: - step: TRY try: # The step we want to retry on failure - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate a summary for: {textContent}' # If HUB_COMPLETION succeeds, mark as done to exit the loop - step: SET retrySuccess: true catch: # On failure: increment counter and wait before the next attempt - step: SET retryCount: '{{ flowContext.retryCount + 1 }}' convertTo: number - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: warning message: 'Attempt {{ flowContext.retryCount }} failed. Retrying...' # Exponential-style delay: 1 s, 2 s, 3 s - step: SLEEP delay: '{{ flowContext.retryCount * 1000 }}' # After the loop: check whether we eventually succeeded - step: IF condition: '{{ not flowContext.retrySuccess }}' then: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Service unavailable after 3 attempts. Please try again later.' - step: END - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR onError: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: 'Unexpected error: {{ flowContext.error }}' Key points: retrySuccess acts as a break flag — set it to true inside try: to exit the loop cleanly. The SLEEP duration grows with each attempt, giving the external service time to recover. The IF check after the loop prevents the rest of the flow from running if all retries failed. For LLM tool-call retries specifically, HUB_COMPLETION has a built-in toolErrorBehavior option (retry / once / fail) that controls how the LLM handles failed tool invocations.

ProActions executes steps sequentially by default — each step completes before the next starts. Two mechanisms break that linearity: PARALLEL (concurrent branches) and inlineSteps (background processing tied to a UI step). Both require deliberate state design.
documents.s: State Management in Parallel and Async Workflows

documents.t: When all branches complete, their flowContext changes are merged back into the main context. The merge is a shallow, deterministic operation based on branch order in the steps list — later branches overwrite keys written by earlier ones, regardless of which branch actually finishes last. Design accordingly — give each branch its own dedicated keys. - title: 'Parallel Analysis' flow: # Run sentiment analysis and keyword extraction concurrently - step: PARALLEL steps: - # Branch 1: sentiment — writes to flowContext.sentiment - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: | Analyze the sentiment of this article. Return JSON: { "sentiment": "positive|negative|neutral", "score": 0.0-1.0 } response_format: json_object - step: SET sentiment: '{{ flowContext.object }}' - # Branch 2: keywords — writes to flowContext.keywords - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: | Extract 5 keywords from this article. Return a JSON array of strings. response_format: list - step: SET keywords: '{{ flowContext.list }}' # Both branches are done — use the merged results - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: | Sentiment: {{ flowContext.sentiment.sentiment }} Keywords: {{ flowContext.keywords | join(", ") }} Rules for safe parallel state: Use unique variable names per branch (branch1Result, branch2Result, not both using result). Read only immutable inputs (built-in variables like {textContent}, or values set before the PARALLEL step) inside branches — don't read keys that another branch may be writing. Do any cross-branch aggregation after the PARALLEL step completes.

Inside a WHILE or FOR loop, flowContext persists across all iterations. Use this deliberately to accumulate results: - title: 'Batch Tag Paragraphs' flow: # Initialize an accumulator before the loop - step: SET taggedResults: '[]' - step: GET_ZONES at: PARAGRAPHS - step: FOR items: '{{ flowContext.zones }}' var: paragraph do: # Process each paragraph - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Extract topic tags from: {{ flowContext.paragraph.text }}' response_format: list # Append results — build up state across iterations - step: SET taggedResults: '{{ flowContext.taggedResults + [{ "text": flowContext.paragraph.text, "tags": flowContext.list }] }}' # taggedResults now contains all paragraphs with their tags - step: SHOW_RESPONSE message: '{{ flowContext.taggedResults | tojson }}'

When you use inlineSteps on USER_SELECT, FORM, or SHOW_RESPONSE, those steps execute in the background while the UI is already shown. The background steps write to flowContext normally; their outputs are available once the user interacts with the UI (e.g., submits the form or selects an item). Steps after the UI step can safely read all background-written state. - title: 'Choose from Background-Generated Options' flow: # Store any state you need in the background BEFORE launching inlineSteps - step: SET articleTitle: '{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}' # USER_SELECT shows immediately; HUB_COMPLETION runs in the background - step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: 'Generate 5 headlines for an article titled "{{ flowContext.articleTitle }}"' response_format: list promptText: 'Choose a headline:' enableKeyboardControl: true # flowContext.text is the user-selected headline — available here after UI interaction - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: '/doc/story/headline/p' What to avoid: Do not write to a key inside inlineSteps that the outer flow reads before the UI step completes — the outer flow is paused waiting for user input, so this is safe, but be aware that inlineSteps errors are rethrown like any other step failure and are then handled by the action's normal onError (or TRY/CATCH), not just surfaced as in-modal messages. Do not share mutable state between inlineSteps branches and the outer flow's pre-UI steps if both run concurrently.

Avoid: SERVICES: HUB: endpoint: 'https://prod-server.company.com/swing/proactions' # Breaks in dev/test environments Do: SERVICES: HUB: endpoint: '{BASE_URL}/swing/proactions' # Works in all environments
Avoid: - title: 'Do Everything' flow: # 50 steps doing unrelated things Do: - title: 'Translate Text' # Focused on translation - title: 'Generate Summary' # Focused on summarization

Authors often need to aggregate content from external sources like: Police reports and press releases Government announcements Wire services and news feeds Social media posts This workflow automates content import and transforms it into publication-ready articles.

# /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/content-robot.ai-kit.section.yaml section: ProActions Tools keywords: '' actions: # # Step 1 - Import Content # - title: 'Content Robot - Import' flow: # Prompt user for URL - step: PROMPT promptText: 'URL:' # Extract remote content - step: HUB_CONTENT_EXTRACTION # Write content into active document - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p" in: "{{ flowContext.object.title | safe }}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/text/p" in: "{{ flowContext.object.content | safe }}" # Check if there's an image and download it - step: IF condition: "{{ flowContext.object.image }}" then: # Create image object as input for UPLOAD_IMAGE step - step: SET image: url: "{{ flowContext.object.image }}" # Download the image to the basefolder - step: UPLOAD_IMAGE objectType: Image # Correlate the downloaded image using EDAPI - step: REST url: "{{ client.getEdapiUrl() }}/v3/object/{{ client.getDocumentId() }}/correlate" method: POST headers: token: "{{ client.getEdapiToken() }}" body: sourceLinkName: "see_also" targetLinkName: "see_also" targetSource: "{{ flowContext.object.id }}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: "A picture was downloaded and correlated to your story." title: "ProActions - Content Robot" # # Step 2 - Rewrite content # - title: 'Content Robot - Rephrase and improve article (Reports)' keywords: Summary Rephrase flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: | # Task You are a author tasked with transforming a police report into a polished newspaper article. Your goal is to maintain the factual integrity while enhancing readability and engagement for the general public. Follow these steps to create a compelling article: Title: Develop a concise and engaging title that reflects the core incident or issue, capturing readers' attention. Teaser Text: Write a brief teaser (approximately 2-3 sentences) summarizing the main event or issue, designed to entice readers to explore further. Body Text: Expand the content into a well-structured article. Ensure it includes: - An engaging introduction that sets the scene or context. - A detailed account of the incident, including key facts and figures. - Contextual information, such as background details or related trends. - A conclusion that summarizes the main points and, if applicable, suggests implications or calls to action. # Example Police Report: "On October 15th, at 10:00 PM, officers responded to a burglary at 123 Main St. The suspect was apprehended on-site and charged with breaking and entering." Rephrased Article: Title: "Suspect Caught in Late-Night Burglary at Local Residence" Teaser Text: A quick response by local police led to the arrest of a burglary suspect at a residence on Main Street. Body Text: On the evening of October 15th, a swift police response resulted in the apprehension of a suspect involved in a burglary at 123 Main Street. Officers arrived at the scene shortly after receiving an emergency call and managed to catch the suspect in the act. The individual has been charged with breaking and entering, marking another success in local law enforcement's ongoing efforts to combat property crimes. This incident highlights the importance of community vigilance and timely reporting in ensuring neighborhood safety. instruction: | The input text: {{ client.getTextContent() }} response_format: name: 'article_object' schema: type: object properties: title: type: string teaser: type: string body: type: string required: - title - teaser - body - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: /doc/story/grouphead/headline/p in: "{{ flowContext.object.title | safe }}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: /doc/story/summary/p in: "{{ flowContext.object.teaser | safe}}" - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: /doc/story/text/p in: "{{ flowContext.object.body | safe }}"

The HUB_CONTENT_EXTRACTION step fetches and parses web content: - step: PROMPT promptText: 'URL:' - step: HUB_CONTENT_EXTRACTION This step: Takes a URL from the PROMPT step (stored in {{flowContext.text}}) Fetches the web page Extracts structured content (title, body, images) Returns an object with extracted data in flowContext.object Extracted object structure: { title: "Article title", content: "Main content with HTML", image: "https://example.com/image.jpg" }
The | safe filter prevents HTML escaping: - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/text/p" in: "{{ flowContext.object.content | safe }}"
documents.s: Step 2: Insert Content with Safe Filter

documents.t: The workflow checks if an image was extracted: - step: IF condition: "{{ flowContext.object.image }}" then: # Image processing steps

The UPLOAD_IMAGE step downloads and saves the image: - step: SET image: url: "{{ flowContext.object.image }}" - step: UPLOAD_IMAGE objectType: Image This: Creates an image object with the URL Downloads the image Uploads it to Méthode Stores the new image ID in flowContext.object.id

The REST step links the image to the article: - step: REST url: "{{ client.getEdapiUrl() }}/v3/object/{{ client.getDocumentId() }}/correlate" method: POST headers: token: "{{ client.getEdapiToken() }}" body: sourceLinkName: "see_also" targetLinkName: "see_also" targetSource: "{{ flowContext.object.id }}" Client functions used: client.getEdapiUrl() - EDAPI base URL client.getDocumentId() - Current document ID client.getEdapiToken() - Authentication token

The HUB_COMPLETION step with structured output: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: | Transform a police report into a newspaper article with: - Title - Teaser - Body instruction: | The input text: {{ client.getTextContent() }} response_format: name: 'article_object' schema: type: object properties: title: type: string teaser: type: string body: type: string required: - title - teaser - body This returns a structured object: { title: "Engaging headline", teaser: "Brief summary", body: "Full article text" } Accessible as: {{ flowContext.object.title }} {{ flowContext.object.teaser }} {{ flowContext.object.body }}

Use | safe Carefully: Only use on trusted content to avoid XSS vulnerabilities Validate URLs: Check URL format before extraction Handle Missing Images: Always check if images exist before processing Structured Output: Use JSON schemas for consistent, parseable results Error Handling: Wrap external calls in TRY blocks User Feedback: Show notifications for success and failure states

Content extraction fails: Verify URL is accessible Check if site requires authentication Some sites block automated content extraction Try the URL in a browser first HTML not rendering: Ensure you're using | safe filter Check if content contains invalid XML Use SANITIZE step if content has problematic XML Image upload fails: Verify image URL is accessible Check Méthode permissions Ensure image format is supported Check file size limits EDAPI correlation fails: Verify EDAPI credentials Check that object IDs are valid Ensure link names exist in schema Check EDAPI logs for detailed errors

# pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml AI_KIT: SERVICES: # Use ProActions Hub as endpoint for DeepL Write DEEPL_WRITE: endpoint: /swing/proactions/proxy/forward/deepl-write SECTIONS: - section: Examples actions: # Configure the action to send text to DeepL Write - title: 'Send selected text to DeepL Write' id: deeplWriteSelection swing: inlineMenu: enable: true icon: "fa fa-pencil" label: " DeepL Write" allowReadOnly: false flow: # Store current text - step: SET currentText: "{selectedText}" # Send to DeepL Write - step: DEEPL_WRITE instruction: "{{ flowContext.currentText | safe }}" # Show comparison in form - step: FORM form: # Current text section headline1: type: "headline" text: "Current Text" inlineHtml: type: "html" html: |

{{ flowContext.currentText }}

hrNew: type: "hr" # Improved text section with DeepL logo headlineNew: type: "html" html: |

# Diff component showing changes inlineDiff: type: "diff" mode: "words" prevText: "{{ flowContext.currentText }}" text: "{{ flowContext.text }}" showDeletions: false # Custom buttons buttons: - type: "cancel" label: "Discard" - type: "submit" flowAttribute: "mode" name: "copy" class: "btn btn-info" label: "Copy" - type: "submit" flowAttribute: "mode" name: "replace" label: 'Replace' # Handle button action - step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.mode }}" cases: 'replace': - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR 'copy': - step: WRITE_CLIPBOARD - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: "Copied text to clipboard" title: "ProActions"
Store the original text for comparison: - step: SET currentText: "{selectedText}" This preserves the original so it can be shown alongside the improved version.

Send text to DeepL Write for improvement: - step: DEEPL_WRITE instruction: "{{ flowContext.currentText | safe }}" Key points: Uses the | safe filter to prevent XML escaping Sends request through ProActions Hub proxy Returns improved text in flowContext.text

Display before/after comparison: - step: FORM form: inlineDiff: type: "diff" mode: "words" prevText: "{{ flowContext.currentText }}" text: "{{ flowContext.text }}" showDeletions: false Diff component options: mode: "words" - Highlight word-level changes (also: "chars", "lines") prevText - Original text text - New text showDeletions: false - Hide deleted text, only show additions

Define multiple action buttons: buttons: - type: "cancel" label: "Discard" - type: "submit" flowAttribute: "mode" # Stores button value in flowContext.mode name: "copy" class: "btn btn-info" label: "Copy" - type: "submit" flowAttribute: "mode" name: "replace" label: 'Replace' Button types: cancel - Closes form without continuing flow submit - Submits form and continues flow flowAttribute - Variable name to store button's name value

Execute different actions based on button pressed: - step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.mode }}" cases: 'replace': - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR 'copy': - step: WRITE_CLIPBOARD - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Copied text to clipboard" type: success The SWITCH step checks flowContext.mode (set by the button) and executes the corresponding case.

Authors often need multiple headline options to choose from. This workflow: Reads the article content from the current document Sends it to an AI service with instructions to generate headlines Displays the suggestions to the user Replaces the headline with the selected option

Create a section file for headline-related actions: # /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/headlines.yaml section: Headlines actions: - title: 'Suggestions: Suggest alternative headlines' flow: # Show selection UI immediately while generating in background - step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: # Generate headline suggestions using AI - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: | # Context You are an AI assistant helping authors improve their content. # Task Your task is to suggest a maximum of 6 creative, engaging, and relevant headlines based on the article provided. The headlines should capture the essence of the article and be suitable for a news audience. Make sure to offer a variety of styles, such as informative, catchy, or thought-provoking options. The generated titles must not exceed 100 characters in length. Do not end the headlines with full stops and do not use double quotation marks unless you are quoting someone directly. Do not put the headlines in quotation marks! Do not hallucinate. Do not make up factual information. instruction: 'The article content is as follows: {textContent}' response_format: 'list' promptText: 'Suggested headlines:' enableKeyboardControl: true # Replace headline with selected option - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p" Note: Using inlineSteps displays the selection modal immediately with a loading indicator while the AI generates headlines in the background. This eliminates perceived wait time and provides better user experience.

Add a contextual button that appears when editing headlines: # /SysConfig/ProActions/menu.oneclick.yaml story: items: - type: 'button' icon: 'fa fa-list' title: 'Suggest headlines' flowRef: 'suggest_headlines' forContentItem: - grouphead forElement: - p - dummyText Note: To use flowRef, add an id to your action: actions: - id: suggest_headlines # Add this ID for flowRef title: 'Suggestions: Suggest alternative headlines' flow: # ... rest of the configuration

Include the headline section in your main configuration: # pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml AI_KIT: SERVICES: !include /SysConfig/ProActions/services.yaml ONECLICK_MENU: !include /SysConfig/ProActions/menu.oneclick.yaml SECTIONS: - !include /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/headlines.yaml

The HUB_COMPLETION step sends the article content to the AI service: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: | You are an AI assistant helping authors improve their content. Your task is to suggest 6 creative headlines... instruction: 'The article content is as follows: {textContent}' response_format: 'list' Key points: {textContent} - Built-in variable containing the full document text response_format: 'list' - Returns an array of strings instead of plain text behavior - Provides context and constraints for the AI model

The USER_SELECT step presents the list to the user: - step: USER_SELECT promptText: 'Suggested headlines:' This automatically: Displays all items from the previous step's list output Allows the user to select one option Stores the selected text in flowContext.text

The REPLACE_TEXT step updates the document: - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p" This replaces the content at the specified XPath with the value from flowContext.text (REPLACE_TEXT's default text input) set by the previous step.
Modify the behavior prompt to change the number of headlines: behavior: | Your task is to suggest a maximum of 10 creative headlines...

Customize the headline style: behavior: | Generate headlines in these styles: - 2 informative headlines (straightforward, factual) - 2 catchy headlines (engaging, attention-grabbing) - 2 thought-provoking headlines (questioning, analytical)
Change the XPath to target different document elements: # For sub-headlines xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/subheadline/p" # For different document types xpath: "/doc/story/title"

Clear Instructions: Provide specific constraints (character limits, style, tone) Content Quality: The AI can only work with the content provided - ensure articles are complete User Choice: Always let users select from suggestions rather than auto-replacing Context Awareness: Use the OneClick menu to make the action available only in relevant contexts

No suggestions appear: Check that ProActions Hub is configured correctly Verify the article has content ({textContent} is not empty) Check browser console for errors Suggestions are off-topic: Ensure the article content is complete and relevant Refine the behavior prompt with more specific instructions Consider sending only the first few paragraphs instead of full content XPath doesn't work: Verify the XPath matches your document structure Use browser dev tools to inspect the document XML structure Test the XPath in the browser console: client.getElementByXPath("/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p")
