Outpainting extends images beyond their original boundaries by using AI to generate additional content. This is useful for: Adjusting image dimensions for different layouts Converting portrait images to landscape (or vice versa) Creating header/banner versions of existing images Filling in cropped areas

# /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/stability-ai.ai-kit.section.yaml section: StabilityAI actions: - title: 'Outpaint with StabilityAI' id: "stabilityai_outpaint" isAvailable: "{{ client.getSelectedElement() === 'web-image' }}" flow: # Get selected image information - step: SELECTED_OBJECT outputs: - type: object name: selectedObject # Read high-res version of the image - step: EDAPI_OBJECT_CONTENT format: highres inputs: - type: text name: "selectedObject.id" # Send image to Stability AI's outpaint endpoint - step: STABILITY_AI_OUTPAINT left: 200 right: 200 up: 200 down: 200 inputs: - type: imageName name: "selectedObject.name" # Create a new version of the selected image - step: UPDATE_BINARY_CONTENT inputs: - type: text name: "selectedObject.id" # Show notification to user - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: "Outpainting {{ flowContext.selectedObject.name }} successful." title: "StabilityAI"

Add a button to the image toolbar in Swing: // /methode/methdig/methode-servlets/conf/swing/com.eidosmedia.swing.web-app/app/plugins/pro-actions-custom/image_toolbar.js eidosmedia.webclient.commands.add({ name: "custom.proactions.stability.outpaint", label: "Outpaint", isActive: function (ctx) { return true; }, isEnabled: function (ctx) { if (ctx.component.getType() === ctx.activeDocument.CONSTANTS.BLOCK_IMAGE) { return true; } return false; }, action: function (ctx, params, callbacks) { SwingProActions.executeAction(ctx, "stabilityai_outpaint"); }, }); // Add button to image toolbar eidosmedia.webclient.actions.editor.components.addButton({ action: "custom.proactions.stability.outpaint", label: "Outpaint using AI", icon: "fas fa-expand-arrows-alt", allowReadOnly: false, });

The isAvailable condition ensures the action only appears for images: isAvailable: "{{ client.getSelectedElement() === 'web-image' }}" This expression: Returns true when an image is selected Returns false otherwise Hides the action when not applicable

The SELECTED_OBJECT step retrieves information about the selected image: - step: SELECTED_OBJECT outputs: - type: object name: selectedObject This stores object metadata in flowContext.selectedObject: { id: "12345", name: "photo.jpg", type: "Image", // ... other metadata }

The EDAPI_OBJECT_CONTENT step downloads the image binary data: - step: EDAPI_OBJECT_CONTENT format: highres inputs: - type: text name: "selectedObject.id" Key points: format: highres - Gets the high-resolution version inputs - Customizes which variable to use for object ID Uses selectedObject.id from the previous step

The STABILITY_AI_OUTPAINT step extends the image: - step: STABILITY_AI_OUTPAINT left: 200 # Extend 200 pixels to the left right: 200 # Extend 200 pixels to the right up: 200 # Extend 200 pixels upward down: 200 # Extend 200 pixels downward inputs: - type: imageName name: "selectedObject.name" Parameters: left, right, up, down - Pixels to extend in each direction inputs - Maps selectedObject.name to the expected input variable

The UPDATE_BINARY_CONTENT step saves the outpainted image: - step: UPDATE_BINARY_CONTENT inputs: - type: text name: "selectedObject.id" This: Preserves metadata Updates the binary content with the outpainted result, without creating a new version

Check Availability: Use isAvailable to show actions only when appropriate High-Res Images: Always use format: highres for best quality Reasonable Sizes: Don't extend too far (max ~400px per side for quality) User Feedback: Show progress for long operations Error Handling: Wrap in TRY blocks - image processing can fail Custom Inputs: Use the inputs array to map variables correctly

Action doesn't appear: Check isAvailable condition Verify an image is actually selected Check browser console for JavaScript errors Image download fails: Verify EDAPI credentials are correct Check object ID is valid Ensure user has read permissions Outpainting fails: Check Stability AI API key configuration Verify image format is supported (JPEG, PNG) Check image size isn't too large Review Stability AI service logs Update fails: Verify user has write permissions Check object isn't locked by another user Custom button not showing: Verify JavaScript file is loaded Check component type detection logic Ensure SwingProActions is available Check browser console for errors

Display progress indicators during multi-step workflows.

This example demonstrates how to: Use SHOW_PROGRESS, UPDATE_PROGRESS, and HIDE_PROGRESS steps Perform numerical calculations in Nunjucks templates Use WHILE loops for iterative processing Provide user feedback during long-running operations
No external services required ProActions AI-Kit 1.0.8 or later

Long-running workflows can leave users wondering if the system is still working. Progress bars provide visual feedback and improve user experience by: Showing that processing is ongoing Indicating how much work remains Displaying status messages Preventing users from interrupting operations prematurely

# Example in pro-actions.ai-kit.yaml section: Examples actions: - title: 'Progress Example' flow: # Initialize variables - step: SET messagePrompt: "Create a short (about 5-10 words) reassuring message to the user that the current loading activity will be completed soon. Be creative!" completion: 0 # Show the progress bar - step: SHOW_PROGRESS position: bottom # Process in steps until completion - step: WHILE condition: "{{ flowContext.completion < 100 }}" do: # Increase percentage - step: SET completion: "{{ flowContext.completion + 25 }}" convertTo: number # Use AI to generate a status message - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "{{ flowContext.messagePrompt }}" # Wait a moment - step: SLEEP # Update the progress bar - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: "{{ flowContext.completion }}" # Show full progress bar for a moment - step: SLEEP

Set up the initial state: - step: SET messagePrompt: "Create a short reassuring message..." completion: 0 Key points: messagePrompt - Template for AI-generated messages completion - Tracks progress from 0 to 100
Display the progress indicator: - step: SHOW_PROGRESS position: bottom Options for position: bottom - Bottom of the screen (default) top - Top of the screen

Use WHILE loop to incrementally update: - step: WHILE condition: "{{ flowContext.completion < 100 }}" do: # Increase by 25% each iteration - step: SET completion: "{{ flowContext.completion + 25 }}" convertTo: number # Update the progress bar - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: "{{ flowContext.completion }}" Numerical calculation in templates: "{{ flowContext.completion + 25 }}" # Addition "{{ flowContext.total - flowContext.processed }}" # Subtraction "{{ flowContext.count * 2 }}" # Multiplication "{{ flowContext.total / flowContext.parts }}" # Division Type conversion: - step: SET count: "{{ flowContext.stringNumber }}" convertTo: number # Ensures it's stored as a number
Show what's happening: - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: "{{ flowContext.completion }}" status: "Processing item {{ flowContext.currentItem }}..."
Remove the progress bar when complete: - step: HIDE_PROGRESS Or it will auto-hide when the flow completes.

Track progress through distinct phases: - title: 'Article Analysis Pipeline' flow: - step: SHOW_PROGRESS # Phase 1: Extract content (0-20%) - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 10 status: "Extracting article content..." - step: SET text: '{{ client.getTextContent() }}' - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 20 status: "Content extracted" # Phase 2: Analyze sentiment (20-40%) - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 25 status: "Analyzing sentiment..." - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Analyze sentiment in JSON: {{ flowContext.text }}" response_format: json_object outputs: - type: object name: sentiment - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 40 status: "Sentiment analyzed" # Phase 3: Extract topics (40-60%) - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 45 status: "Extracting topics..." - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Extract main topics: {{ flowContext.text }}" response_format: "list" outputs: - type: list name: topics - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 60 status: "Topics extracted" # Phase 4: Generate summary (60-80%) - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 65 status: "Generating summary..." - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Summarize: {{ flowContext.text }}" outputs: - type: text name: summary - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 80 status: "Summary generated" # Phase 5: Create report (80-100%) - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 85 status: "Creating report..." - step: SET text: | # Article Analysis Report **Sentiment:** {{ flowContext.sentiment.sentiment }} **Topics:** {{ flowContext.topics | join(', ') }} **Summary:** {{ flowContext.summary }} - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: 100 status: "Report complete!" - step: SLEEP - step: MARKDOWN_TO_HTML - step: SHOW_RESPONSE mode: html - step: HIDE_PROGRESS

Meaningful Messages: Show what's actually happening, not just percentages Accurate Percentages: Base percentages on actual progress, not guesses Clean Up: Always hide progress when done (or let flow complete) Sleep Before Hide: Add small delay so users can see 100% completion Error States: Update progress even when errors occur

Progress bar doesn't appear: Check that SHOW_PROGRESS is called Verify no JavaScript errors in console Ensure ProActions UI components are loaded Progress doesn't update: Verify UPDATE_PROGRESS is inside the loop Check that percentage variable is numeric Ensure percentage is between 0-100 Progress bar freezes: Check for infinite loops in WHILE conditions Add SLEEP steps to allow UI updates Verify loop termination conditions Percentage calculation wrong: Use convertTo: number for numeric operations Check division by zero Round percentages: {{ (value * 100) | round }}

Modern digital publications often need audio versions of articles for: Accessibility (screen reader alternatives) Multi-platform distribution (podcasts, smart speakers) Mobile consumption (listen while driving) This workflow automates the creation of high-quality audio narrations.

# /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/tts.ai-kit.section.yaml section: Speech / TTS keywords: 'Voice' actions: - title: 'Text to Speech (OpenAI)' flow: # Extract text content, excluding image captions and credits - step: SET text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["web-image-caption", "caption", "credit"] }) | safe }}' targetName: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/,\\?]/g, '') | truncate(50) }}.mp3" # Generate speech audio - step: HUB_SPEECH # Upload to Méthode - step: UPLOAD options: name: "{{ flowContext.targetName | safe }}" workFolder: "{{ client.getDocumentWorkfolder() }}" folderPath: "/Production/Product/Audio" type: "Audio" attributes: "" systemAttributes: "<props></props>" application: 'Swing ProActions' options: showPath: true showSystemAttributes: true showAttributes: true createMode: 'AUTO_RENAME' # Notify user of success - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: "Successfully created audio version of your object." title: "Text to Speech"

The SET step prepares both the text content and the target filename: - step: SET text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["web-image-caption", "caption", "credit"] }) | safe }}' targetName: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/,\\?]/g, '') | truncate(50) }}.mp3" Key features: Excluding tags: client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["web-image-caption", "caption", "credit"] }) This retrieves text content but excludes specified XML elements. Useful for removing: Image captions Photo credits Pull quotes Sidebars Any non-narrative content Dynamic filename: targetName: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/,\\?]/g, '') | truncate(50) }}.mp3" Creates a safe filename: Gets article title from metadata Removes invalid filename characters (/, \, ?) Truncates to 50 characters Adds .mp3 extension

The HUB_SPEECH step sends text to the speech synthesis service: - step: HUB_SPEECH This step: Uses the text variable from the previous SET step Calls the configured TTS service (e.g., OpenAI TTS) Returns binary audio data Stores the result in flowContext.blob by default

The UPLOAD step saves the audio file: - step: UPLOAD options: name: "{{ flowContext.targetName | safe }}" workFolder: "{{ client.getDocumentWorkfolder() }}" folderPath: "/Production/Product/Audio" type: "Audio" options: createMode: 'AUTO_RENAME' Upload options: name - Filename for the uploaded file workFolder - Base Méthode work folder folderPath - Relative path within work folder type - Méthode object type createMode: 'AUTO_RENAME' - Automatically rename if file exists
Customize the speech synthesis parameters: - step: HUB_SPEECH voice: "alloy" # OpenAI TTS voices: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer speed: 1.0 # Speed from 0.25 to 4.0

Customize which elements to exclude: # Exclude more elements text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["web-image-caption", "caption", "credit", "sidebar", "pullquote", "infobox"] }) | safe }}' # Include everything text: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}' # Only specific sections text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ includeTags: ["text", "headline", "summary"] }) | safe }}'

Exclude Non-Narrative Content: Always exclude captions, credits, and other elements that don't belong in narration Safe Filenames: Use replace() to remove invalid characters and truncate() to limit length User Feedback: Show notifications on success and provide clear error messages Auto-Rename: Use createMode: 'AUTO_RENAME' to avoid overwrite conflicts

Audio quality is poor: Check the TTS service configuration Try different voices Adjust speed parameter Ensure text is clean (no XML tags, special characters) Upload fails: Verify folder path exists in Méthode Check write permissions Ensure workFolder is correct Check filename for invalid characters Wrong content in audio: Verify excludeTags list is correct Check document structure with client.getTextContent() in console Test with smaller text selections first File already exists error: Use createMode: 'AUTO_RENAME' to automatically rename Or increment filename manually Or use timestamp in filename
Content Import and Rewrite - Import and transform content Progress Bar - Show progress for long operations
Debugging ProActions workflows is essential for identifying and fixing issues. This guide covers debugging techniques, tools, and best practices.
The DEBUG step logs flow context and variables to the console.

- title: 'Debug Example' flow: - step: SET myVariable: "Hello World" count: 42 - step: DEBUG - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {textContent}" Console Output: [DEBUG] Current flow context: { myVariable: "Hello World", count: 42 }

Place DEBUG steps at key points in your flow: - title: 'Complex Workflow' flow: - step: GET_TEXT_CONTENT at: CURSOR - step: DEBUG - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {selectedText}" - step: DEBUG - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: CURSOR

Problem: Variable shows as undefined - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Value: {{ flowContext.myVar }}" # Shows: "Value: undefined" Debug: - step: DEBUG id: "Check if myVar exists" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Value: {{ flowContext.myVar }}" Solution: Ensure variable is set before use: - step: SET myVar: "Hello" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Value: {{ flowContext.myVar }}"

Problem: LLM step hangs or fails - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process this" # Times out or errors Debug: - step: TRY try: - step: DEBUG id: "Before LLM call" - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Test" max_tokens: 10 - step: DEBUG id: "After LLM call - response received" catch: - step: DEBUG id: "Error occurred" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Service error: {{ flowContext.error.message }}" Check: ProActions Hub is running API keys are configured Network connectivity Browser network tab for failed requests

Problem: Script execution fails with cryptic error - step: SCRIPTING script: | flowContext.result = params.data.toUpperCase(); return flowContext; # Error: Cannot read properties of undefined Debug: Check the console for detailed SCRIPTING error log showing: What variables are available Where in the script the error occurred The full error message and stack trace Solution: Verify variables exist before using: - step: SCRIPTING script: | if (!params?.data) { throw new Error("params.data is required"); } flowContext.result = params.data.toUpperCase(); return flowContext; Or use optional chaining and defaults: - step: SCRIPTING script: | flowContext.result = (params?.data ?? '').toUpperCase(); return flowContext;

Start with a minimal flow and add complexity: # Start simple - title: 'Test Basic' flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Flow started" # Add one step at a time - title: 'Test With LLM' flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Flow started" - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Say hello" options: max_tokens: 5 - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "LLM response: {{ flowContext.text }}"

Create test actions for individual steps: - title: 'Test GET_TEXT_CONTENT' flow: - step: GET_TEXT_CONTENT at: CURSOR - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Selected: {selectedText}" - title: 'Test HUB_COMPLETION' flow: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Say hello" options: max_tokens: 5 - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Response: {{ flowContext.text }}"
- title: 'Quick Check' flow: - step: SET name: "John" age: 30 - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Name: {{ flowContext.name }}, Age: {{ flowContext.age }}"

- step: SCRIPTING script: | console.log('[Custom Debug] Variable check:', { textContent: flowContext.textContent?.substring(0, 100), userName: flowContext.userName, customVar: flowContext.customVar }); return flowContext;

The SCRIPTING step provides detailed error logs when script execution fails: - step: SCRIPTING script: | // This will fail with a helpful error message const result = flowContext.undefinedVar.someMethod(); return flowContext; Console Output: ====================================================================== 🐛 SCRIPTING ERROR in action: "My Action Name" ====================================================================== Type: script Mode: sync Script Preview: 1 | // This will fail with a helpful error message 2 | const result = flowContext.undefinedVar.someMethod(); 3 | return flowContext; Available Context: - Context keys: step, client, cfg, flowContext, ctx - FlowContext keys: text, selectedText, myVariable Error Details: Message: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'someMethod') Stack Trace: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'someMethod') at eval (eval at evalInScope ...) ... ====================================================================== What the error log shows: Action name: Which action the error occurred in Type and Mode: Whether it's script/template and sync/async Script preview: First 20 lines of the failing script with line numbers Available context: What variables are accessible in the script Error details: The actual error message and stack trace Debugging script errors: Check the "FlowContext keys" to verify variables exist Look at the script preview line numbers to locate the error Use the error message to understand what went wrong Add console.log() statements before the failing line: - step: SCRIPTING script: | console.log('Checking variable:', flowContext.undefinedVar); const result = flowContext.undefinedVar?.someMethod() ?? 'default'; return flowContext;

Symptoms: Actions don't appear Console shows parsing errors Debug: Check browser console for error messages Validate YAML syntax with online validator Check indentation (use spaces, not tabs) Ensure quotes are properly closed Example Error: YAML parse error at line 15: unexpected token Solution: Go to line 15 in YAML file Check for missing colon, dash, or quote Verify indentation is correct

Symptoms: Sections not loading Console shows errors Debug: # Check if file exists AI_KIT: SECTIONS: - !include /SysConfig/ProActions/sections/my-actions.ai-kit.section.yaml Solution: Verify the include path format is valid: absolute (/SysConfig/...), or relative with ./ / ../ (resolved from the current file) Check file exists and is readable Ensure proper file permissions

Symptoms: Service steps fail "Service not configured" errors Debug: - title: 'Test Service Config' flow: - step: TRY try: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Test" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: success message: "Service working" catch: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: "Service error: Check configuration" Check: Service is defined in SERVICES section Endpoint URLs are correct ProActions Hub is running (if using Hub)
Use the network tab to debug API calls:
Open browser DevTools (F12) Click "Network" tab Execute your ProActions workflow
Filter by "XHR" or "Fetch" Look for requests to your services Check for 401, 403, 404, 500 errors
Click on a request to see: Headers: Check authentication headers Payload: Request body sent to API Response: API response or error message Timing: How long the request took
Cause: Step type doesn't exist or is misspelled Solution: Check step name spelling, verify step is registered
Cause: Variable not set before use Solution: Add DEBUG step to check flow context, ensure variable is set
Cause: Service not defined in SERVICES section Solution: Check service configuration in services.ai-kit.services.yaml
Cause: User doesn't have access to action Solution: Check forUsers, forGroups, forTeams in action configuration
Cause: XPath doesn't match document structure Solution: Verify XPath with browser inspector, simplify XPath

# Start with this - title: 'Test' flow: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "It works!" # Then add - title: 'Test with Variables' flow: - step: SET myVar: "Hello" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "{{ flowContext.myVar }}" # Then add more - title: 'Test Full Flow' flow: - step: SET myVar: "Hello" - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {{ flowContext.myVar }}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "{{ flowContext.text }}"
# Good - step: DEBUG id: "After fetching text content - checking selectedText" # Avoid - step: DEBUG id: "Debug 1"
Comment out or remove DEBUG steps before deploying: - title: 'Production Flow' flow: # - step: DEBUG # id: "Debug: Starting flow" - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {textContent}"
- step: TRY try: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {textContent}" catch: - step: DEBUG id: "Error details" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: error message: "An error occurred"

Create test actions with hardcoded data: - title: 'Test with Sample Data' flow: - step: SET testText: "This is sample text for testing" testCount: 5 - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {{ flowContext.testText }}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Result: {{ flowContext.text }}"

When a flow doesn't work: Check browser console for errors Verify YAML syntax is valid Add DEBUG steps to inspect variables Test with simplified flow Check service configuration Verify permissions (forUsers, forGroups, forTeams) Test individual steps separately Check network tab for API errors Verify XPaths match document structure Ensure development mode is enabled Clear configuration cache Refresh browser
Use Templates - Template syntax and functions Configuration Basics - Configuration fundamentals
ProActions uses Nunjucks templating to provide dynamic variable access and transformations. This guide explains how to use template syntax and access client functions for advanced workflows.
documents.s: How to Use Nunjucks Templates and Client Functions

documents.t: Use single braces {} for built-in ProActions variables: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Process: {textContent}" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Selected: {selectedText}"
Use double braces {{ }} for: Custom flow variables Client function calls Filters and transformations - step: SET myVariable: "Hello" - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "{{ flowContext.myVariable }}"

All variables are stored in flowContext: - step: SET articleTitle: "Breaking News" wordCount: 500 isPublished: false - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: | Title: {{ flowContext.articleTitle }} Words: {{ flowContext.wordCount }} Published: {{ flowContext.isPublished }}

Use dot notation to access nested properties: - step: SET article: title: "My Article" author: name: "John Doe" email: "john@example.com" tags: - news - technology - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: | Title: {{ flowContext.article.title }} Author: {{ flowContext.article.author.name }} Email: {{ flowContext.article.author.email }} First Tag: {{ flowContext.article.tags[0] }}
The client object provides access to document and platform functions.

- step: SET # Document identifiers docId: "{{ client.getDocumentId() }}" docLoid: "{{ client.getDocumentLoid() }}" docUuid: "{{ client.getDocumentUuid() }}" docName: "{{ client.getDocumentName() }}" # Document properties objectType: "{{ client.getObjectType() }}" workflowStatus: "{{ client.getWorkflowStatus() }}" productName: "{{ client.getProductName() }}" channel: "{{ client.getChannel() }}" issueDate: "{{ client.getDocumentIssueDate() }}"

- step: SET # Get entire user metadata object metadata: "{{ client.getMetadata() }}" # Access specific metadata fields (depends on your Méthode configuration) title: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}" author: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.author }}" category: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.category }}" # Get metadata as string metadataString: "{{ client.getMetadataString() | safe }}"
- step: SET systemMetadata: "{{ client.getSystemMetadata().props.productInfo.issueDate }}" systemMetadataString: "{{ client.getSystemMetadataString() | safe }}"
- step: SET virtualAttributes: "{{ client.getVirtualAttributes() }}" virtualAttributesString: "{{ client.getVirtualAttributesString() | safe }}"
- step: SET selectedElement: "{{ client.getSelectedElement() }}" selectedElementXpath: "{{ client.getSelectedElementXpath() }}"

- step: SET # Get text content with options text: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}' # Get text excluding certain tags textNoCaption: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["caption", "credit"] }) | safe }}' # Get XML content xml: '{{ client.getXmlContent() | safe }}'

- step: SET # Container identifiers containerId: "{{ client.getContainerId() }}" containerLoid: "{{ client.getContainerLoid() }}" containerUuid: "{{ client.getContainerUuid() }}" # Container properties containerObjectType: "{{ client.getContainerObjectType() }}" containerWorkflowStatus: "{{ client.getContainerWorkflowStatus() }}" containerProductName: "{{ client.getContainerProductName() }}" containerChannel: "{{ client.getContainerChannel() }}" # Container metadata containerMetadata: "{{ client.getContainerMetadata() }}"
- step: SET appName: "{{ client.getAppName() }}" # 'swing' or 'prime' baseUrl: "{{ client.getBaseUrl() }}" isReadonly: "{{ client.isReadonly() }}"
Filters transform values using the pipe | operator.
Prevents HTML escaping (use for HTML/XML content): - step: SET htmlContent: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}'

- step: SET # Uppercase upper: "{{ flowContext.text | upper }}" # Lowercase lower: "{{ flowContext.text | lower }}" # Capitalize first letter capitalize: "{{ flowContext.text | capitalize }}" # Title case title: "{{ flowContext.text | title }}" # Trim whitespace trim: "{{ flowContext.text | trim }}" # Truncate with length short: "{{ flowContext.longText | truncate(50) }}" # Truncate with custom ending shortCustom: "{{ flowContext.longText | truncate(50, true, '...') }}"

- step: SET # Remove invalid filename characters filename: "{{ flowContext.title | replace(r/[\\/:*?\"<>|]/g, '_') }}" # Remove multiple spaces cleaned: "{{ flowContext.text | replace(r/\\s+/g, ' ') }}" # Remove special characters alphanumeric: "{{ flowContext.text | replace(r/[^a-zA-Z0-9 ]/g, '') }}"

- step: SET # First item first: "{{ flowContext.myList | first }}" # Last item last: "{{ flowContext.myList | last }}" # Join array into string joined: "{{ flowContext.tags | join(', ') }}" # Array length count: "{{ flowContext.myList | length }}"

ProActions also adds custom filters for object and array traversal. These are available in the same {{ }} templates and can be chained with built-in Nunjucks filters. - step: SET users: - id: 1 profile: name: "Ada" role: "Editor" - id: 2 profile: name: "Linus" role: "Reviewer" # Find one item, then safely access nested attributes reviewerName: "{{ flowContext.users | find('id', 2) | getAttr('profile') | getAttr('name') | default('Unknown') }}" # Extract one attribute path from each item userNames: "{{ flowContext.users | pluck('profile.name') | join(', ') }}" Notes: find(attribute, value) returns the first matching array item. getAttr(attribute) reads own properties only (no prototype traversal). pluck(path) returns an array of values for each element using a dot path.
- step: SET # Round number rounded: "{{ flowContext.decimal | round }}" # Round to decimals precise: "{{ flowContext.decimal | round(2) }}" # Absolute value absolute: "{{ flowContext.number | abs }}"

Provide default value if variable is undefined: - step: SET value: "{{ flowContext.maybeUndefined | default('Default Value') }}" default(...) keeps the standard built-in Nunjucks behavior. The custom resolver filters do not override it.
- step: SET message: "{{ 'Published' if flowContext.isPublished else 'Draft' }}"
- step: SET status: "{{ flowContext.count > 100 and 'Long' or 'Short' }}"
- step: SET # Get title from metadata and create safe filename filename: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/:*?\"<>|]/g, '_') | truncate(50) }}.txt"
- step: SET # Get text without captions, trim, and truncate summary: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["caption", "credit"] }) | trim | truncate(200) }}'
- step: SET docInfo: "Document: {{ client.getDocumentName() }} (ID: {{ client.getDocumentId() }}) - Status: {{ client.getWorkflowStatus() | upper }}"

- title: 'Export with Custom Filename' flow: - step: SET # Create filename from title and date exportFilename: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/:*?\"<>|]/g, '_') }}_{{ client.getDocumentIssueDate() }}.txt" # Get content text: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}' - step: DOWNLOAD filename: "{{ flowContext.exportFilename }}"

- title: 'Create Audio Version' flow: - step: SET # Get text excluding images and captions text: '{{ client.getTextContent({ excludeTags: ["web-image-caption", "caption", "credit"] }) | safe }}' # Create filename from metadata targetName: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\/:?]/g, '') | truncate(50) }}.mp3" - step: HUB_SPEECH - step: UPLOAD options: name: "{{ flowContext.targetName | safe }}" workFolder: "{{ client.getDocumentWorkfolder() }}" folderPath: "/Production/Product/Audio" type: "Audio"

- title: 'Process Based on Category' flow: - step: SET category: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.category }}" - step: IF condition: "{{ flowContext.category === 'Breaking News' }} " then: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: "Generate urgent, attention-grabbing content." instruction: "Create breaking news alert: {textContent}" else: - step: HUB_COMPLETION behavior: "Generate standard professional content." instruction: "Summarize: {textContent}"
documents.s: Example 3: Conditional Processing Based on Metadata

documents.t: - title: 'Process Container Documents' flow: - step: SET containerName: "{{ client.getContainerMetadata().metadata.general.title }}" documentCount: 0 - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Processing container: {{ flowContext.containerName }}"

- title: 'Smart Export' flow: - step: SET # Build comprehensive document info docType: "{{ client.getObjectType() }}" docTitle: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | trim }}" docAuthor: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.author | default('Unknown') }}" docDate: "{{ client.getDocumentIssueDate() }}" # Create structured filename filename: "{{ flowContext.docType }}_{{ flowContext.docTitle | replace(r/[\\s]+/g, '_') }}_{{ flowContext.docDate }}.txt" # Get content content: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}' # Build export text text: |- Document: {{ flowContext.docTitle }} Type: {{ flowContext.docType }} Author: {{ flowContext.docAuthor }} Date: {{ flowContext.docDate }} --- {{ flowContext.content }} - step: DOWNLOAD filename: "{{ flowContext.filename }}"

Use default filter to handle missing fields: - step: SET title: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | default('Untitled') }}" subtitle: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.subtitle | default('') }}"

- step: SET workFolder: "{{ client.getDocumentWorkfolder() }}" category: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.category | default('General') }}" year: "{{ client.getDocumentIssueDate() | truncate(4, true, '') }}" targetPath: "{{ flowContext.workFolder }}/{{ flowContext.category }}/{{ flowContext.year }}"

- step: SET language: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.language | default('EN') }}" targetLang: "{{ 'FR' if flowContext.language === 'EN' else 'EN' }}" - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{selectedText}" target_lang: "{{ flowContext.targetLang }}"
- step: SET testValue: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}" - step: DEBUG - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Value: {{ flowContext.testValue }}"

When templates get too complex, use SCRIPTING: - step: SCRIPTING script: | const metadata = client.getMetadata(); const title = metadata?.metadata?.general?.title || 'Untitled'; const date = client.getDocumentIssueDate(); const filename = `${title.replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, '_')}_${date}.txt`; return { filename, title, date };
# Good - prevents HTML escaping text: '{{ client.getTextContent() | safe }}' # Avoid - may escape HTML entities text: "{{ client.getTextContent() }}"

# Good - handles missing metadata title: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | default('Untitled') }}" # Risky - may fail if metadata missing title: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}"
# Good - removes invalid characters filename: "{{ flowContext.userInput | replace(r/[\\/:*?\"<>|]/g, '_') }}" # Risky - may contain invalid characters filename: "{{ flowContext.userInput }}"

# Good - split complex operations - step: SET rawTitle: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title }}" cleanTitle: "{{ flowContext.rawTitle | replace(r/[\\s]+/g, '_') }}" filename: "{{ flowContext.cleanTitle }}.txt" # Avoid - hard to read - step: SET filename: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\s]+/g, '_') }}.txt"

- step: SET # Extract title from metadata and create safe filename: # 1. Get title from metadata # 2. Replace spaces with underscores # 3. Remove invalid filename characters # 4. Truncate to 50 characters # 5. Add extension filename: "{{ client.getMetadata().metadata.general.title | replace(r/[\\s]+/g, '_') | replace(r/[\\/:*?\"<>|]/g, '') | truncate(50, true, '') }}.txt"

ProActions Hub includes a built-in admin panel for monitoring runtime metrics, reviewing configuration, and diagnosing issues — all from a browser-based dashboard. The panel is protected by stateless API key authentication independent of the main auth system.
auth: admin: enabled: true apiKeys: - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY} Set the environment variable (minimum 32 characters): PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)

Open your browser and navigate to: https://swing.your-env.em-cms.cloud/swing/proactions/admin/panel Enter your admin key in the login screen and click Sign In. Key Length Requirement Admin API keys must be at least 32 characters long. Shorter keys are rejected during configuration validation.

auth: admin: enabled: true apiKeys: - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY_1} - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY_2} allowedNetworks: - 127.0.0.1 - 10.0.0.0/8 Field Type Default Description enabled boolean false Enable admin authentication apiKeys string[] [] API keys for admin access (min 32 chars each, required when enabled) allowedNetworks string[] [] Optional IP/CIDR allowlist (empty = all IPs allowed)
You can configure multiple admin keys to support key rotation or multiple administrators: auth: admin: enabled: true apiKeys: - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY_PRIMARY} - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY_SECONDARY}

Restrict admin access to specific IP addresses or CIDR ranges: auth: admin: allowedNetworks: - 127.0.0.1 # Localhost only - 10.0.0.0/8 # Private network range - 192.168.1.50 # Specific workstation When allowedNetworks is configured, requests from non-listed IPs receive a 403 Forbidden response. Reverse Proxy If ProActions Hub is behind a reverse proxy, enable hub.security.trustProxy so the guard uses the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For instead of the proxy IP.

Admin authentication is fully independent of the main authentication system (EDAPI or token-based). This means: Admin panel works even when auth.enabled: false Admin keys are separate from EDAPI credentials or auth tokens No session or cookie is required — every request sends the key via the x-admin-key header # Main auth disabled, admin auth enabled auth: enabled: false admin: enabled: true apiKeys: - ${PROACTIONS_ADMIN_KEY}
The admin panel organizes information into seven tabs.

Overview of the running instance: Process information — PID, hostname, Node.js version, uptime, platform Memory usage — RSS, heap used, heap total, external Configuration summary — counts of AI targets (aiTargets), legacy targets, guardrails, proxies, tools and MCP servers Request totals and top targets — selection counts by type (legacy targets, AI targets, proxies, tools, MCP) and a top-8 targets table marking each target as new engine or legacy Runtime usage charts — visual breakdown of request distribution across providers and proxies

AI provider usage metrics collected in real time: Summary cards — total requests, token usage, streaming ratio, error rate, active models, and fallback attempts (extra composite attempts, i.e. requests recorded by N−1 when a composite retried or fell back N times) Token usage by provider — horizontal stacked bar chart (prompt vs completion tokens) Latency by model — average response time with min/max range Finish reason distribution — doughnut chart showing completion, stop, length, etc. Detailed tables — per-provider, per-model, and per-action breakdowns with tokens, errors, and latency AI Targets — table of configured aiTargets entries with their provider or composite strategy, model, guardrails, Realtime flag, timeout, and per-target request/last-used counters Guardrails — table of configured guardrails with per-guardrail checks, flagged, denied, redacted, logged, and checkErrors counters Configured targets — table showing all legacy AI targets from configuration When no AI-Link requests have been made yet, a placeholder card is shown.

Voice-agent relay diagnostics: Relay status — enabled/disabled, and the configured Realtime targets (id only) Live sessions — currently open sessions with request ID, target, model, correlation labels, start time, age, and directional bytes Aggregates — pending/active/admitted/rejected/completed/failed totals, directional bytes, duration summaries, and rejection/close categories Token accounting — totals split by modality (input text/audio/image, cached, output text/audio), provider-response status distribution, input-audio transcription usage, and per-target/per-model breakdowns of sessions, responses, tokens, bytes and duration Aggregates cover closed sessions only. Disabled Realtime shows a placeholder.
Proxy configuration and usage: Configured proxies — ID, URL, and header removal settings Usage statistics — request counts per proxy target

MCP (Model Context Protocol) server status and metrics: Server health — connection status, transport type, auto-connect setting Server metrics — average latency (with min/max), error count and error rate Tool inventory — available tools per server with invocation counts Tool-level metrics — per-tool latency and error badges
Full runtime configuration view with sensitive values automatically redacted. Displayed as formatted JSON.
Process-level information: Node.js version, platform, PID Uptime — formatted as days/hours/minutes Memory breakdown — detailed heap and RSS statistics Runtime usage snapshot — raw usage data

The navigation bar provides quick actions: Control Description Auto Refresh Toggle automatic data refresh every 30 seconds Refresh Manually reload all data Reset Statistics Clear all runtime metrics (with confirmation dialog) Theme Toggle Switch between light and dark mode (persisted in localStorage) Logout Clear stored admin key and return to login screen
All endpoints except /admin/panel require the x-admin-key header.
GET /admin/panel Serves the admin panel HTML page. This endpoint is public (no authentication required) — authentication happens client-side via the API key.

GET /admin/runtime Returns process information, configuration summary, runtime usage, and MCP connection health. This is the primary endpoint used by the dashboard on every refresh. Response structure: { "process": { "pid": 1234, "hostname": "hub-server", "nodeVersion": "v22.x.x", "uptimeSeconds": 86400, "platform": "linux", "memoryMb": { "rss": 120, "heapUsed": 80, "heapTotal": 100, "external": 5 } }, "configurationSummary": { "targets": { "count": 5, "items": [...] }, "aiTargets": { "count": 4, "items": [ { "id": "openai", "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-6-luna", "guardrails": ["no-cc"], "realtimeEnabled": false } ] }, "guardrails": { "count": 1, "items": [{ "name": "no-cc", "type": "regex", "phase": "pre", "onFail": "deny" }] }, "realtime": { "enabled": false, "count": 0, "items": [] }, "proxies": { "count": 2, "items": [...] }, "tools": { "count": 1, "items": [...] }, "mcp": { "count": 3, "items": [...] } }, "runtimeUsage": { ... }, "mcpConnections": [ ... ] }
GET /admin/runtime/usage Returns only the runtime usage statistics (subset of the diagnostics endpoint).

POST /admin/runtime/reset Clears all runtime usage counters and resets the uptime anchor. This action is logged at warn level with the admin username and client IP. Response: { "success": true, "message": "Runtime statistics have been reset" } Audit Trail Every statistics reset is logged with the admin identity and client IP address for audit purposes.

Endpoint Description GET /admin/config Full configuration (all sections, secrets redacted) GET /admin/config/targets AI target configurations GET /admin/config/proxies Proxy configurations GET /admin/config/mcp MCP server configurations GET /admin/config/auth Authentication configuration GET /admin/config/hub Hub/server configuration All configuration responses are sanitized — sensitive fields such as API keys, tokens, passwords, and secrets are automatically redacted.

Header-based: Every API request includes the x-admin-key header Timing-safe comparison: Key validation uses crypto.timingSafeEqual to prevent timing attacks Stateless: No sessions or cookies — the key is validated on every request Header cleanup: The admin key header is removed from the request after validation
Status Meaning 401 Missing or invalid admin key 403 Admin access not configured, or client IP not in allowedNetworks
All configuration and diagnostic responses pass through the sensitive data filter. Fields matching keywords like password, token, apiKey, secret, authorization, and key are replaced with [REDACTED].

Use strong keys — generate with openssl rand -base64 32 or equivalent Restrict networks — use allowedNetworks to limit access to known admin IPs Enable trust proxy — when behind a reverse proxy, so IP allowlisting works correctly Rotate keys — configure multiple keys and rotate periodically Monitor resets — statistics reset actions are logged for audit compliance
Verify your admin key is at least 32 characters Check that auth.admin.enabled is true in configuration If using allowedNetworks, confirm your IP is listed (check behind proxy)
The admin key may have expired or been rotated — try logging out and back in Check that the Hub process is running and healthy Review browser developer console for network errors

AI-Link metrics are collected in memory at runtime — they start empty after each restart Make some AI-Link requests first, then refresh the panel Verify that AI-Link targets are configured and working

The AI-Link module provides a unified, OpenAI-compatible gateway to multiple AI service providers. Providers are declared as AI-Link targets (aiTargets) and served by the Hub's new built-in AI engine — no separate gateway process, with native provider authentication, automatic retries, composite routing and guardrails. Legacy targets are deprecated Provider entries declared under targets: are served by the legacy AI gateway, a separate subprocess the Hub starts for them. They are deprecated since Hub 1.3.0: they keep working in 1.3.x, but every request logs a deprecation warning, and support will be removed in a future release. See Legacy targets for the old format and Migrating from targets to aiTargets for the conversion.

The simplest configuration requires an id, a provider, and an API key: aiTargets: - id: openai provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} options: model: gpt-6-luna Set the environment variable: OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-api-key-here

Make requests to AI-Link endpoints with the x-target header: curl -X POST http://localhost:$PROACTIONS_HUB_PORT/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-target: openai" \ -d '{ "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"} ] }' The model from the target's options is merged into the request body. A model in the request body overrides it.

The x-target header (or a ?target= query parameter) selects the target. Resolution order is: The id matches an entry in aiTargets → the Hub serves the request in-process through the matching provider. If the entry is a composite (strategy + routes), the Hub resolves the attempt order first — see Routing & Retries. Otherwise the id matches an entry in the legacy targets list → the request goes through the legacy AI gateway, and the Hub logs one deprecation warning for that id. Otherwise the Hub returns 400 with message: "INVALID_TARGET" and error: "No target with name <id> found" (when no legacy targets are configured at all, the error reads No targets configured with baseType targets). A request without x-target or ?target= returns 400 MISSING_TARGET. If the same id exists in both lists, the aiTargets entry wins — this is what makes migration transparent. Clients, and ProActions YAML HUB service target: / x-target values, need no change when a legacy target is migrated to an aiTargets entry with the same id.

AI-Link provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints: Chat Completions: POST /v1/chat/completions Image Generation: POST /v1/images/generations Audio Speech: POST /v1/audio/speech Audio Transcription: POST /v1/audio/transcriptions Audio Translation: POST /v1/audio/translations Responses API: POST /v1/responses All six are served by aiTargets. The Responses API is available on aiTargets only — there is no legacy fallback for it.

Not every provider supports every modality. An unsupported provider/modality combination returns 400 with the code UNSUPPORTED_MODALITY rather than a raw provider error — for example image generation on Anthropic or Mistral. Image generation forwards n, size, quality, output_format and background to OpenAI and Azure image models; an invalid value for the last three returns 400 INVALID_IMAGE_OPTION. Audio translation is available on openai and openai-compatible targets only, through the providers' OpenAI-compatible file-translation endpoint; other providers return UNSUPPORTED_MODALITY instead of silently performing same-language transcription. Accepted response_format values for translation are json, text, and verbose_json.

Supported: Input as a plain string, or message items with roles user, system, developer, assistant and input_text (or string) content Function tools and tool_choice Streaming (SSE) instructions text.format (structured output) reasoning.effort (same values as reasoning_effort) Rejected with 400: previous_response_id (send the full input on every request) and built-in tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter).
POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/completions and POST /v1/rerank are served only by legacy targets. Called with an aiTargets id, they return 400 with Endpoint <path> is not supported for aiTargets.
These HTTP endpoints do not provide OpenAI Realtime sessions. HUB_VOICE_AGENT uses the dedicated WebSocket relay instead — see Realtime Relay.

The Hub natively proxies Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming responses. Set "stream": true in the request body and the Hub forwards the upstream SSE stream directly to the client. curl -X POST http://localhost:${PROACTIONS_HUB_PORT}/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-target: openai" \ --no-buffer \ -d '{ "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a short story"}], "stream": true }' The response uses Content-Type: text/event-stream and follows the standard OpenAI streaming format — each event is a data: line containing a JSON chunk, terminated by data: [DONE]. Behaviour: Client disconnects are detected immediately — the upstream connection is torn down to prevent resource leaks. A client disconnect is never retried. Streaming requests appear separately in the Admin Panel AI-Link metrics (streaming ratio). A failure before the first byte reaches the client (connect error, 429, 5xx, timeout) is retried and can fall back to the next composite route; if every attempt fails, the client gets a clean 502 response and no partial stream. A failure after the headers are sent closes the stream — bytes already delivered cannot be un-sent.

Each aiTargets entry: Field Required Description id yes Identifier sent in the x-target header; unique across aiTargets provider yes Provider name (see Supported Providers) apiKey no Provider credential (API key) settings no Provider connection settings (baseURL, headers, region, …), passed to the provider client as-is options no Default request-body parameters, using OpenAI wire names. The model belongs here: options.model providerOptions no Provider-specific options keyed by provider id (e.g. anthropic), forwarded verbatim on chat, Responses, image, speech and transcription calls requestTimeout no Timeout in milliseconds; 0 disables the timeout. Default: hub.http_client.timeout (120000) retry no Per-target retry policy — see Routing & Retries debug no Per-target logPrompt / logResponse / logUpstream overrides — see Logging guardrails no Names of entries in the top-level guardrails: list — see Guardrails realtime no enabled, maxSessionDurationMs, idleTimeoutMs, maxMessageBytes, maxBytesPerSecond — see Realtime Relay No unknown keys aiTargets entries reject unknown keys. Provider-specific settings (region, headers, baseURL, AWS keys, Azure resource names, …) must live under settings:, never at the entry root. Startup fails with "<key>" is not allowed naming the offending key. aiTargets: - id: example provider: openai apiKey: ${EXAMPLE_API_KEY} settings: headers: X-Custom-Header: value options: model: gpt-6-luna max_completion_tokens: 2000 providerOptions: {} requestTimeout: 120000 retry: maxAttempts: 3 initialDelayMs: 500 maxDelayMs: 5000 backoffMultiplier: 2 debug: logUpstream: false guardrails: []

A composite entry fans one x-target id out to several concrete targets: aiTargets: - id: prod-chat strategy: fallback # or: loadbalance routes: - target: openai - target: anthropic weight: 1 # weights apply to loadbalance only Composites may not declare retry: or guardrails: directly (both are rejected with an id-specific error — attach them to the routes instead), may not nest other composites, and may not reference unknown ids. See Routing & Retries.

Provider id Aliases Authentication Common settings openai — apiKey baseURL, headers, organization, project azure azure-openai apiKey or Entra ID resourceName, apiVersion, baseURL, headers, useEntraId, entraScope anthropic — apiKey baseURL, headers, authToken google gemini, google-ai apiKey baseURL, headers vertex vertex-ai, google-vertex-ai Service account project, location, googleAuthOptions, baseURL, headers bedrock amazon-bedrock AWS keys, IAM role, or default chain region, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken, roleArn, externalId mistral — apiKey baseURL, headers groq — apiKey baseURL, headers deepseek — apiKey baseURL, headers xai — apiKey baseURL, headers cohere — apiKey baseURL, headers togetherai — apiKey baseURL, headers fireworks — apiKey baseURL, headers perplexity — apiKey baseURL, headers huggingface — apiKey baseURL, headers openrouter — apiKey baseURL, headers openai-compatible — apiKey baseURL (required in practice), headers Credentials and settings left unset fall back to the provider's environment variable where one exists: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY for the API key; AWS_REGION for Bedrock settings.region; GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT / GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION for Vertex settings.project / settings.location. Any other provider Any service exposing an OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be used through openai-compatible with settings.baseURL — Writer, Langdock, Ollama, Azure AI Inference, and similar. If a service has neither a native provider nor an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, keep it on a legacy target for now and contact Eidosmedia support.

aiTargets: - id: openai provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} settings: organization: ${OPENAI_ORG} # Optional project: ${OPENAI_PROJECT} # Optional options: model: gpt-6.1-sol max_completion_tokens: 2000

aiTargets: - id: azure-openai-chat provider: azure apiKey: ${AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY} settings: resourceName: ${AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE} apiVersion: ${AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION} options: model: ${AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT} # Azure addresses models by deployment name temperature: 0.7 max_tokens: 800 Microsoft Entra ID instead of a static key: aiTargets: - id: azure-openai-entra provider: azure settings: resourceName: ${AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE} apiVersion: ${AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION} useEntraId: true entraScope: https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default # optional, this is the default options: model: ${AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT} useEntraId resolves a token through DefaultAzureCredential (managed identity, Azure CLI, or an environment service principal), so no apiKey is configured.
aiTargets: - id: anthropic provider: anthropic apiKey: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} options: model: claude-sonnet-5-5 max_tokens: 12000

Static keys: aiTargets: - id: bedrock provider: bedrock settings: region: ${AWS_BEDROCK_REGION} accessKeyId: ${AWS_BEDROCK_ACCESS_KEY_ID} secretAccessKey: ${AWS_BEDROCK_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY} sessionToken: ${AWS_BEDROCK_SESSION_TOKEN} # Optional options: model: "eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5" max_tokens: 800 Cross-region inference profile (the ARN or profile id goes in options.model): aiTargets: - id: bedrock-inference-profile provider: bedrock settings: region: eu-north-1 accessKeyId: ${AWS_BEDROCK_ACCESS_KEY_ID} secretAccessKey: ${AWS_BEDROCK_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY} requestTimeout: 300000 # 5 minutes for larger models options: model: "arn:aws:bedrock:eu-north-1:123456789012:inference-profile/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5" max_tokens: 8000 IAM role assumption via STS: aiTargets: - id: bedrock-role provider: bedrock settings: region: ${AWS_BEDROCK_REGION} roleArn: ${AWS_BEDROCK_ROLE_ARN} externalId: ${AWS_BEDROCK_EXTERNAL_ID} # optional, for cross-account roles options: model: "eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5" max_tokens: 800 The STS call itself uses the target's default AWS credential chain; the assumed credentials are cached in memory and refreshed about 60 s before expiry, not re-requested on every call. Default credential chain (instance/container role, environment variables, shared config or SSO): aiTargets: - id: bedrock-default-chain provider: bedrock settings: region: ${AWS_BEDROCK_REGION} options: model: "eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5" max_tokens: 800 Credential precedence: static accessKeyId + secretAccessKey when both are set → otherwise roleArn STS assumption → otherwise the default AWS credential chain.
aiTargets: - id: gemini provider: google apiKey: ${GEMINI_API_KEY} options: model: gemini-3.8-flash

aiTargets: - id: vertex provider: vertex settings: project: ${VERTEX_PROJECT_ID} location: ${VERTEX_REGION} googleAuthOptions: credentials: client_email: ${VERTEX_CLIENT_EMAIL} private_key: ${VERTEX_PRIVATE_KEY} options: model: gemini-3.8-flash The default OAuth scope is https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform; set settings.googleAuthOptions.scopes: [<scope>] only to request something else. Literal \n sequences in the private key are converted to real newlines automatically.
aiTargets: - id: mistral provider: mistral apiKey: ${MISTRAL_API_KEY} options: model: mistral-small-latest max_tokens: 800
aiTargets: - id: openrouter provider: openrouter apiKey: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} options: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5
aiTargets: - id: huggingface-main provider: huggingface apiKey: ${HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY} options: model: meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B

Writer: aiTargets: - id: writer provider: openai-compatible apiKey: ${WRITER_API_KEY} settings: baseURL: https://api.writer.com/v1 options: model: palmyra-x6 Local Ollama: aiTargets: - id: local-ollama provider: openai-compatible settings: baseURL: http://localhost:11434/v1 options: model: muse-glimmer Azure AI Inference (OpenAI-v1-compatible endpoints): aiTargets: - id: azure-ai-inference-main provider: openai-compatible apiKey: ${AZURE_AI_INFERENCE_API_KEY} settings: baseURL: https://<your-resource>.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1 options: model: <your-deployment-name>

The effective request body is { ...target.options, ...requestBody } — request fields win, including model. Mapped chat-completion parameters: model, messages, tools (function tools), tool_choice, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, max_completion_tokens (wins over max_tokens), stop, seed, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, reasoning_effort (none | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max; invalid values return 400 INVALID_REASONING_EFFORT), stream, stream_options.include_usage, response_format (json_object | json_schema), n. Any other body key is dropped, and its name is logged: AI-Engine dropped unsupported params: <names> Provider-specific extras go into the target's providerOptions, keyed by provider id and forwarded verbatim to the provider. The example below raises Claude's thinking effort (Claude 5.5 models think adaptively; effort steers how much). aiTargets: - id: anthropic-thinking provider: anthropic apiKey: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} providerOptions: anthropic: effort: high options: model: claude-sonnet-5-5 max_tokens: 12000

response_format: json_object and response_format: json_schema are executed — the target model is wrapped so the provider enforces the requested format: curl -X POST http://localhost:${PROACTIONS_HUB_PORT}/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-target: openai" \ -d '{ "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the article in one sentence."}], "response_format": { "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "name": "summary", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["summary"], "additionalProperties": false } } } }' The Responses API supports the equivalent text.format.

Chat completions and the Responses API retry retryable upstream failures by default — 3 total attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) with equal-jitter exponential backoff — configurable globally under hub.http_client.retry and per target under retry. A route's retries share that route's requestTimeout budget, so raise the timeout if you raise the attempt count. Images, speech, transcription and translation make a single attempt. Full details, including composite fallback/loadbalance behaviour: Routing, Retries & Timeouts.

Top-level guardrails: entries (regex, length, JSON, PII, LLM judge, moderation API) attach to a concrete aiTargets entry by name and run before the request, after the response, or both. A deny action returns HTTP 422 with a guardrail_violation body. Full reference: Guardrails.

Status Meaning 400 Validation error — e.g. MISSING_TARGET, INVALID_TARGET, MISSING_MODEL, MISSING_MESSAGES, UNSUPPORTED_MODALITY, or a legacy-only endpoint on an aiTargets id 422 Guardrail violation (guardrail_violation) 502 Upstream provider failure or timeout 503 Legacy target requested while the legacy AI gateway is not ready Upstream failures return a JSON body: { "message": "External service error", "target": "openai", "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-6-luna", "timestamp": "2026-05-04T09:12:31.004Z", "endpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions", "statusCode": 500, "upstreamError": { "error": { "message": "..." } } } endpoint is the upstream URL. upstreamError is the provider's response body (parsed as JSON when possible). headers carries retry-after, x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset and x-request-id when the provider sent them. A timeout returns message: "Request timeout" with error, timeoutMs, timeoutSeconds and suggestion. Network failures return message Connection refused, DNS resolution failed or Connection reset, with error, code and suggestion.

# Test chat completion curl -X POST http://localhost:${PROACTIONS_HUB_PORT}/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-target: openai" \ -d '{ "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"} ] }' Add "stream": true to the body (and --no-buffer to curl) to exercise the streaming path.
If Swagger is enabled (swagger.enabled: true): Navigate to http://localhost:${PROACTIONS_HUB_PORT}/docs Find the /v1/chat/completions endpoint Add the x-target header Execute the test request

An aiTargets entry is served in-process, so: No AI-Link request served via deprecated legacy target — migrate '<id>' to aiTargets warning appears in the logs (log type aiLink) for that id. Once no legacy targets: entries remain, GET /ready reports the legacy gateway check (ai_gateway) as healthy with skipped: true, and no gateway subprocess is started.
documents.s: Verify the target is served by the new engine

documents.t: A legacy provider field was placed at the root of an aiTargets entry. Move it under settings: (or into options: if it is a request parameter) — see the field mapping table.
No aiTargets or legacy targets entry has the requested id. Check that the x-target header (or the ProActions target: value) matches an id exactly.
Neither the request body nor the target supplied a model. Set options.model on the target, or send "model" in the body.

Error: 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden. Verify the API key is set and substituted (${VAR} resolved, not left literal). Check the provider-specific settings (Azure resourceName, Bedrock region, Vertex project/location). Ensure the credential has the required permissions (for Bedrock: bedrock:InvokeModel; for Vertex: the Vertex AI role on the project).

Error: 502 with message: "Request timeout". Increase requestTimeout on the target: requestTimeout: 300000 # 5 minutes If the target has a blocking post-phase guardrail and serves streams, the timeout covers the whole generation, not just time-to-first-byte — see Guardrails.

The service-account private key is malformed. Literal \n sequences are normalized automatically, so check the surrounding quoting: the value must contain the PEM body between -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- and -----END PRIVATE KEY----- lines with no stray quotes or trailing whitespace.

No usable credential was found. Set settings.accessKeyId and settings.secretAccessKey, or settings.roleArn, or give the container a default AWS credential source (instance/container role or environment variables).

Guardrails are content checks that run around an AI-Link request: against the outbound messages before the provider is called (pre), against the generated text afterwards (post), or both. Each violated guardrail can deny the request, redact the offending content, or just record the event. Guardrails apply to aiTargets only — legacy targets use their own config.beforeRequestHooks (see Legacy targets).

Guardrails are declared once in the top-level guardrails: list and attached to a concrete target by name: aiTargets: - id: openai-main provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} options: model: gpt-6-luna guardrails: [no-cc, output-limit] guardrails: - name: no-cc type: regex phase: pre onFail: deny patterns: ["\\b\\d{16}\\b"] - name: output-limit type: length phase: post onFail: log maxChars: 20000 name must be unique across the guardrails list. A target may reference several guardrails; a guardrail may be referenced by several targets. Composites cannot declare guardrails: directly — attach them to the routes. A guardrail's own target (for type: llm) must be a concrete aiTargets entry that does not itself declare guardrails (recursive checks are rejected at startup), and it may not be a composite. guardrails is supported on chat completions and the Responses API. Image generation and audio endpoints have no guardrail coverage.

Field Values Default name string, unique required type regex, length, json, pii, llm required phase pre, post, both pre onFail deny, redact, log deny applyTo last-user-message, all-messages, output last-user-message (pre), output (post) onError allow, deny (llm only) allow Rules enforced at startup: onFail: redact is valid only for regex and pii — the other types never produce redacted content. type: json is post-phase only. applyTo: output requires phase: post or both.

Flags content matching any of the configured patterns. With onFail: redact, every match of every matching pattern is replaced with [REDACTED]. guardrails: - name: no-cc type: regex phase: pre onFail: deny patterns: ["\\b\\d{16}\\b"] - name: mask-emails type: regex phase: both onFail: redact patterns: ["[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"] An invalid pattern is a check error, not a violation. onError cannot be set on non-llm types, so the request proceeds and the error is counted in checkErrors.

Flags content exceeding maxChars and/or maxWords. Never redacts — combine it with onFail: deny or onFail: log. guardrails: - name: output-limit type: length phase: post onFail: deny maxChars: 20000 maxWords: 3000

Flags output that does not parse as JSON. Post phase only. guardrails: - name: must-be-json type: json phase: post onFail: log Pair it with response_format: json_object / json_schema (see Structured output) when you need the provider to produce JSON in the first place.

Detects built-in PII categories: email, iban, credit-card (Luhn-validated), phone. Omitting categories runs all of them. guardrails: - name: mask-pii type: pii phase: both onFail: redact categories: [email, iban] Higher-priority categories claim overlapping spans, so a 16-digit card number is not also reported as a phone number.

Asks a language model whether the content violates a written policy, and gates the verdict on a confidence score (a low-confidence "flagged" verdict does not deny). aiTargets: - id: brand-safety-target provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} options: model: gpt-6-luna guardrails: - name: brand-safety type: llm mode: judge target: brand-safety-target model: gpt-6-luna phase: both onFail: deny onError: allow threshold: 0.8 maxContentChars: 8000 timeout: 10000 policy: | Flag content that mentions competitor products by name. mode: judge requires policy.

Calls an OpenAI-compatible /moderations endpoint and flags content whose maximum category score reaches threshold, computed over only the categories the API flagged and that survive config.categories filtering (when set) — not over every category the API returns, and not an average. aiTargets: - id: mistral-moderation provider: mistral apiKey: ${MISTRAL_API_KEY} settings: baseURL: https://api.mistral.ai/v1 - id: guarded-chat provider: openai apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} options: model: gpt-6-luna guardrails: [moderation] guardrails: - name: moderation type: llm mode: moderation-api target: mistral-moderation model: mistral-moderation-latest categories: [pii, sexual, hate_and_discrimination] threshold: 0.8 onFail: deny onError: allow mode: moderation-api forbids policy and only works with targets whose provider is openai, openai-compatible, or mistral. An azure target passes config validation but rejects at runtime with a check error — its moderation endpoint is not wired up yet. Fail-open by default onError: allow (the default) means an outage, timeout or auth failure in the judge/moderation call silently disables enforcement for that guardrail. Use onError: deny when the check must be fail-closed.

onFail Effect deny Aborts the request with HTTP 422 (guardrail_violation); nothing is sent upstream/back redact Rewrites the flagged content in place and lets the request proceed (regex, pii only) log Records the event and proceeds with the request unchanged onError (llm only) separates a check execution failure (the judge model errored, timed out, or returned garbage) from a violation: allow proceeds, deny aborts with 422.

A deny action returns HTTP 422 with: { "error": { "type": "guardrail_violation", "guardrail": "no-cc", "phase": "pre", "categories": [], "reason": "content matched pattern(s): \\b\\d{16}\\b" } } Guardrails run before the response is committed, so a pre-phase deny never opens a stream.

A post/both guardrail that can still deny or redact (or whose onError is deny) cannot be enforced against a live stream — bytes already sent cannot be un-sent. For such a target, stream: true requests are generated in full internally, checked, and then replayed as a synthesized SSE stream that is wire-indistinguishable from a real one. Operational impact: No time-to-first-byte benefit. stream: true becomes full-generation latency. The timeout covers the whole generation — generateText plus guardrail time — not just TTFB as for a normal stream. Raise requestTimeout on any target that combines streaming with a blocking post guardrail, or a response that would have arrived in time as a real stream can now time out first. Log-only post guardrails (onFail: log, onError: allow) do not trigger buffering: they are evaluated after a real stream ends, against the exact text the client already received.

Post-phase guardrails inspect the generated text only — neither tool-call arguments nor reasoning output is covered. applyTo: all-messages checks each message individually, so a violation split across several messages is not detected. For llm guardrails it also means one upstream check call per message, so cost and latency scale with conversation length — prefer last-user-message on long conversations. Image generation, audio speech, audio transcription and audio translation have no guardrail coverage. llm with mode: moderation-api does not support azure targets at runtime.

The Admin Panel AI-Link tab lists every configured guardrail with per-guardrail counters: checks, flagged, denied, redacted, logged, and checkErrors. A rising checkErrors count with onError: allow means enforcement is silently bypassed.

Deprecated targets: entries are served by the legacy AI gateway, a separate subprocess, and are deprecated since Hub 1.3.0. They keep working in 1.3.x, but every request logs a deprecation warning, and support will be removed in a future release. Migrate to aiTargets using the migration guide. This page documents the legacy targets: section exactly as it behaves today, for operators who have not migrated yet. New deployments should configure aiTargets instead.

The config object is passed directly to the legacy AI gateway for advanced routing strategies.

Configure automatic failover between providers: targets: - id: with-failover config: strategy: mode: fallback targets: - provider: openai api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} override_params: model: gpt-6.1-sol - provider: anthropic api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} override_params: model: claude-sonnet-5-5

The following hub settings configure the legacy AI gateway subprocess. They are only used while at least one legacy target exists — an aiTargets-only deployment never spawns the subprocess, and these settings have no effect. Setting Default Description hub.ailink_port 3001 Port the legacy gateway listens on hub.ailink_host localhost Host the legacy gateway binds to hub.ailink_protocol http Protocol used to reach the legacy gateway hub.ailink_health_check_interval 30000 Health probe interval (ms) hub.ailink_max_restart_attempts 3 Restart attempts after a crash hub.ailink_max_consecutive_failures 3 Consecutive health failures before a restart hub.ailink_restart_delay 5000 Delay between restart attempts (ms) hub.ailink_startup_timeout 30000 How long to wait for the legacy gateway to become ready (ms) Each of these can be overridden through the matching PROACTIONS_HUB_AILINK_* environment variable. Removing the legacy gateway Once every legacy target is migrated, delete the targets: section (or leave it empty). On the next restart the Hub does not start the legacy AI gateway at all, and /ready reports its ai_gateway check as skipped: true.
Migrate to aiTargets AI-Link configuration for aiTargets

Hub 1.3.0 moves AI-Link to a new, built-in AI engine. Targets declared under aiTargets: run on it; the old targets: section still works through the legacy AI gateway, but is deprecated. Action required in Hub 1.3.0 Legacy targets: entries are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Every request served by a legacy target logs: AI-Link request served via deprecated legacy target — migrate '<id>' to aiTargets (log type aiLink, level warn). New capabilities exist only on aiTargets: composite routing, guardrails, engine-owned retries, the Responses API, the Realtime relay, and upstream wire logging. Migration is per-target and transparent to clients: an aiTargets entry with the same id takes over the same x-target value.

No separate gateway process. The Hub serves aiTargets with its new built-in AI engine. Once no legacy targets remain, the legacy AI gateway is not started at all: one less process, one less port, less memory and CPU, and /ready no longer depends on it. Engine-owned retries. Retryable upstream failures (429, 5xx, timeouts, network errors) are retried with backoff by default on chat completions and the Responses API. See Routing & Retries. Composite routing. fallback and weighted loadbalance across several targets under a single x-target id. Guardrails. Regex, length, JSON, PII, LLM-judge and moderation-API checks with deny / redact / log actions, applied before the request, after the response, or both. See Guardrails. POST /v1/responses. The Responses API is available on aiTargets only. Realtime relay. Voice-agent WebSocket sessions require a concrete OpenAI aiTargets entry. See Realtime Relay. Provider-native authentication. Azure OpenAI through Microsoft Entra ID, AWS Bedrock through STS role assumption or the default credential chain, Vertex AI with automatic private-key normalization. Upstream wire logging. logUpstream records the provider-native request/response bodies (and the upstream error body) for aiTargets.

Inventory the legacy ids. Every legacy request logs a deprecation warning naming its id; the Admin Panel AI-Link tab also lists the configured targets. Also check (access logs or client owners) whether any id is called on /v1/embeddings, /v1/completions or /v1/rerank — those must stay legacy, see Not migratable. Add an aiTargets entry per legacy target, keeping the same id. aiTargets wins when an id exists in both lists, so ProActions YAML (SERVICES.*.target: or a per-step target:) needs no change, and the legacy entry stays in place as a dormant rollback. Translate the fields using the general mapping and the provider sections below. Restart the Hub. Schema errors abort startup and name the offending key (for example "awsRegion" is not allowed). Test each target with curl, including "stream": true. Confirm no deprecation warnings appear for that id in the aiLink logs. Delete the legacy entries. Once targets: is empty or removed, the legacy AI gateway is not started and /ready reports its ai_gateway check as skipped: true. Restart to apply. Optionally remove the hub.ailink_* overrides from your environment (see Legacy targets). Rollback Delete the aiTargets entry (or rename its id) and the legacy entry with the same id serves again. The Gateway is only started when at least one legacy target exists at startup, so a restart is required.
