None false true None None voice Output voice: marin, cedar, alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, or verse. marin false false None None instruction Optional user-prompt passed through to OpenAIRequestBuilder for tool resolution (not sent to the Realtime API) None false false None None vad Voice activity detection configuration (type, eagerness, threshold, idleTimeoutMs, bargeIn, etc.). idleTimeoutMs (server_vad only, 5000–30000) makes the model prompt the user after a long silence. For server_vad, raise threshold (default 0.5) to require louder audio in noisy rooms. Set type: 'push_to_talk' to disable server-side VAD entirely — the user explicitly opens/closes the mic via a hold control in the voice bar; the VAD tuning fields are ignored in this mode. bargeIn controls when the user interrupts a speaking agent, in every mode: 'speech' (VAD default) interrupts on detected voice — under push_to_talk once actual voice is heard while holding; 'off' never interrupts (noisy rooms: VAD then answers the captured speech after the response finishes; push_to_talk refuses presses until the agent is done); 'press' (push_to_talk only, its default) cancels immediately on press. None false false None None noiseReduction Server-side input noise reduction applied before VAD and the model — reduces background noise falsely triggering the listening state. 'far_field' (default) for laptop/desk/conference mics, 'near_field' for headsets, 'none' to leave unconfigured. far_field false false None None reasoningEffort Reasoning effort for reasoning-capable Realtime models (gpt-realtime-2): minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | none. Defaults to low for gpt-realtime-2 models and is omitted for other model families. Use 'none' to omit it explicitly. Options: whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize. gpt-4o-transcribe false false None None maxDurationSecs Maximum session duration in seconds before auto-close (default: 300) 300 false false Range:1-3600 None showToolCalls When true, each tool call is shown in the monitor as a collapsible entry (name + args + result). Default: false. false false false None None toolsReuseContext When true and a tool uses steps, the full flowContext is passed to the sub-flow instead of a fresh context with only the tool arguments. None false false None None functionsReuseContext Whether to reuse full flowContext for legacy cfg.functions handlers (deprecated, use toolsReuseContext instead). None false false None None tools Array of user-defined tool/function descriptors available during the voice session. An optional when condition (template expression or boolean, evaluated once at session start) gates whether the tool is exposed to the model. None false false None None functions Array of legacy function descriptors for tool calling (deprecated, use tools instead). None false false None None builtinTools List of built-in tool classes to enable during the voice session. Object entries support an optional when condition (template expression or boolean, evaluated once at session start) that gates whether the tools are exposed to the model. None false false None None autoDiscoverTools Enable dynamic tool discovery during the voice session None false false None None toolStrict Enable strict validation of builtin tool arguments. false false false None None skills List of skill names to load for the voice session. Skill instructions are prepended to the behavior sent to the Realtime API, and skill reference documents become readable via the read_skill_reference tool. Each skill is loaded from /SysConfig/ProActions/Skills/<skillName>/SKILL.md. Entries can also be objects { name, when } where when (template expression or boolean, evaluated once at session start) gates whether the skill is loaded. None false false None None target Hub routing target name (overrides service-level target) None false false None None

Voice activity detection configuration (type, eagerness, threshold, idleTimeoutMs, bargeIn, etc.). idleTimeoutMs (server_vad only, 5000–30000) makes the model prompt the user after a long silence. Set type: 'push_to_talk' to disable server-side VAD entirely — the user explicitly opens/closes the mic via a hold control in the voice bar; the VAD tuning fields are ignored in this mode. bargeIn controls when the user interrupts a speaking agent, in every mode: 'speech' (VAD default) interrupts on detected voice — under push_to_talk once actual voice is heard while holding; 'off' never interrupts (noisy rooms: VAD then answers the captured speech after the response finishes; push_to_talk refuses presses until the agent is done); 'press' (push_to_talk only, its default) cancels immediately on press. Execute a conditional branch based on a condition
Category Control Version: 1.0.3 Applications: all Scope: all

Use IF when you need to execute different steps based on a true/false condition. Use IF when: You have a simple true/false decision to make You need to execute different workflows based on a condition You want to skip steps conditionally You need to validate data before proceeding You want to handle different cases in your workflow Don't use IF when: You have multiple distinct values to match against - use SWITCH instead (cleaner for 3+ options) You need complex boolean logic with many conditions - consider SCRIPTING for readability You only need to check if a variable exists - template syntax {{ var }} handles this Alternatives: SWITCH - Better for matching one value against multiple specific cases SCRIPTING - Better for complex conditional logic with multiple variables TRY/catch - Better for error handling scenarios

Required Context: Condition can reference any flowContext variables Template syntax {{ }} is Nunjucks, not JavaScript: use and / or / not and the built-in filters. JavaScript-only syntax (||, &&, !) raises no error but resolves to false, so the "then" branch is silently skipped
Reads flow context values referenced by condition or legacy test. Does not write directly; writes made by the selected then or else subflow are preserved.

Name Description Default Required Resolved Constraints Conditional Rules condition The condition to evaluate, e.g. "{{ flowContext.count > 0 }}". Templates are Nunjucks: use and / or / not (NOT && / || / !, which fail silently and make the condition false). Compare numbers directly, e.g. "{{ flowContext.count > 0 }}"; the | length filter works on arrays and strings only, never on a number. None false true None None test Legacy alternative to condition. The condition to evaluate using JavaScript syntax. None false false None None then Steps to execute if the condition is true None false false None None else Steps to execute if the condition is false None false false None None
Require Exactly One: Exactly one of: condition, test
- step: IF condition: "{{ flowContext.userInput == 'yes' }}" then: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Proceeding..."

Related Steps: SWITCH - Alternative for multi-value matching: Use SWITCH when checking one variable against 3+ specific values. Use IF for true/false or 2-value conditions. SCRIPTING - Alternative for complex logic: Use SCRIPTING for complex boolean logic with many variables. Use IF for simple condition checks. SET - Use together for conditional assignment: Wrap SET in IF to conditionally set variables. General Resources: Step Library Overview Configuration Basics Examples

Chat/completion step that calls OpenAI (or Hub/Azure variants). Supports messages, images, audio, attachments, tools (functions), structured outputs (json_schema/json_object/list), reasoning and audio output. Many step-level configuration options are supported via cfg.*.
Category LLM Aliases SERVICE_OPENAI_COMPLETION Version: 1.0.0 Applications: all Scope: all Default Service: OPENAI_COMPLETION

Use OPENAI_COMPLETION when you need to leverage OpenAI models for text generation, analysis, or transformation. Use OPENAI_COMPLETION when: You need text generation, completion, or transformation with OpenAI compatible APIs You want to analyze or extract structured information from text You need JSON/structured output from natural language input You want to use function/tool calling capabilities You need to process images with vision models (gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-sol) You need to process or generate audio (with supported models) Don't use OPENAI_COMPLETION when: You only need simple text templating without AI - use SET with `{{ }}` syntax instead You need translation specifically - use DEEPL_TRANSLATE for better quality You need local processing without external API calls - use SCRIPTING instead

Required Services: OPENAI_COMPLETION service must be configured in services.yaml Valid OpenAI API key in service configuration or proxy Required Context: flowContext.text (optional) - Input text for processing; if not provided, uses editor content or instruction templates flowContext.messages (optional) - Conversation history to continue from previous interactions Platform Requirements: Works on all platforms (Swing, Prime) Requires internet connectivity for API calls

Input Sources: `cfg.instruction` - User prompt (supports templates like `{{ flowContext.variable }}`) `cfg.behavior` - System prompt to set AI behavior and personality `flowContext.text` - Default input text (used when instruction contains templates) `cfg.images` / `cfg.image` - Optional image inputs (requires vision-capable model) `cfg.audio` / `cfg.audios` - Optional audio inputs (requires audio-capable model) `cfg.attachments` - Generic attachments (images, audio, or text files) `cfg.messages` - Full conversation history (overrides flowContext.messages) `cfg.tools` - Tool/function definitions for function calling (`cfg.functions` also supported for backward compatibility) Processing Flow: Resolves templates in instruction and behavior prompts Loads stored prompt if `promptId` is specified Builds messages array (system message + user message) Attaches images/audio/attachments if provided Calls OpenAI API with configured model and options Handles tool/function calls if tools are defined (iterative execution) Processes response based on `response_format` setting Extracts and formats output according to response type Output Destinations: `flowContext.text` - Text response (default output, always set) `flowContext.object` - Structured object (when `response_format` is "json_object" or json_schema) `flowContext.list` - Array of items (when `response_format` is "list") `flowContext.audio` - Audio data URL (when `outputAudio` is configured) `flowContext.audio_transcript` - Audio transcript text (optional) `flowContext.reasoning` - Reasoning trace (for reasoning-capable models) `flowContext.response` - Full API response object (optional, for debugging) `flowContext.usage` - Token usage statistics (optional) `flowContext.choices` - Raw choices array from API (optional) `flowContext.tool_results` - Results from function/tool executions (optional)

Name Description Default Required Resolved Constraints Conditional Rules model Model id or deployment id to use None false false None None promptId Id of a stored prompt configuration to reuse None false false None None instruction The user prompt to send to the LLM (supports templates) None false true None None behavior The system prompt to send to the LLM (supports templates) None false false None None options Additional request options object (temperature, n, top_p, model, etc.) None false false None None response_format Structured response format. Can be a string ("json_object", "list", "text_edits" or "text_cuts") or an object with json_schema definition None false false None None outputAudio Configuration object to request audio output (voice/format) None false false None None toolChoice Optional tool selection policy (mapped to tool_choice in the model request) None false false None None parallelToolCalls Allow model/providers to emit multiple tool calls in one assistant turn (mapped to parallel_tool_calls) None false false None None maxToolIterations Maximum number of tool iterations to perform None false false None None afterToolResultToolChoice Behavior after a tool result (none|auto) None false false None None toolErrorBehavior How to handle tool execution errors: "retry" allows LLM to retry failed tools (default), "fail" stops the flow immediately on any tool error, "once" prevents retrying the same tool after it fails once None false false None None functionErrorBehavior How to handle function execution errors (deprecated, use toolErrorBehavior instead) None false false None None tools Array of tool/function descriptors for tool calling. Each descriptor can define template, steps, script, or scriptRef. An optional when condition (template expression or boolean, evaluated once per request) gates whether the tool is exposed to the model. None false false None None functions Array of function descriptors for tool calling (deprecated, use tools instead). Supports template, steps, script, or scriptRef. When true, the agent can discover and activate tool providers on demand via listAvailableTools and activateTools meta-tools, instead of requiring all tools to be listed explicitly. Can be combined with builtinTools for aliases, MCP tools, and explicit provider configurations. false false false None None builtinTools List of built-in tool classes to enable for the AI model. Object entries support an optional when condition (template expression or boolean, evaluated once per request) that gates whether the tools are exposed to the model. None false false None None toolGuidance Optional tool schema guidance (e.g., addTableFeedback columns or addMetricsFeedback metric keys and ranges) None false false None None toolStrict Enable strict tool argument validation (reject missing/extra arguments) false false false None None stream Enable streaming mode for incremental response delivery. When enabled, tokens are delivered as they are generated rather than waiting for the full response. Streaming is automatically disabled for incompatible configurations (json_schema, list, audio output). Defaults to false. false false false None None feedback Show streaming response in the Flow Execution Monitor. Defaults to true when stream is enabled. Set to false to use streaming for performance (faster time-to-first-token) without monitor visualization. None false false None None skills List of skill names to load. Skills provide system instructions and reference documents. Each skill is loaded from /SysConfig/ProActions/Skills/<skillName>/SKILL.md. documents.t: - step: OPENAI_COMPLETION behavior: "You are a creative writing assistant." instruction: "Write a short story about a robot discovering nature for the first time." stream: true # Tokens are displayed incrementally in the Flow Monitor options: temperature: 0.8
documents.s: Enable streaming for real-time response display in Flow Monitor

documents.t: Don't use high temperature for factual or structured output tasks Why: High temperature (> 0.7) increases randomness, which can produce creative but inaccurate or inconsistent responses, especially problematic for JSON output or factual extraction Solution: Use temperature 0.0-0.3 for factual tasks, summaries, structured output, or data extraction. Use 0.7-1.0 only for creative writing, brainstorming, or varied responses. Don't forget to handle API failures and empty responses Why: API calls can fail due to rate limits, network issues, invalid API keys, or service outages. Empty responses can break subsequent steps that expect data. Solution: Wrap OPENAI_COMPLETION in TRY block for error handling, and validate output exists before using it in subsequent steps. Don't include sensitive or confidential data in prompts without data processing agreement Why: Data sent to OpenAI's API may be stored and potentially used for model training unless you have a specific data processing agreement. Solution: Use Azure OpenAI with private deployment for sensitive data, or sanitize/anonymize information before sending. Review OpenAI data usage policies.

API Call Timing: Simple completions (< 1k tokens): 1-3 seconds Large context (10k+ tokens): 3-10 seconds Function calling: +1-2 seconds per tool call iteration Vision (image analysis): +2-5 seconds depending on image size Cost Optimization: Use cheaper models (gpt-6-luna) for simple tasks Set `max_tokens` in options to prevent unexpectedly long (expensive) responses Cache results when processing identical content multiple times Use `response_format` for structured output instead of parsing free-form text

Related Steps: AZURE_OPENAI_COMPLETION - Alternative for Azure deployments: Use AZURE_OPENAI_COMPLETION when you have Azure-hosted OpenAI models. Same functionality but uses Azure endpoints and authentication. HUB_COMPLETION - Alternative using ProActions Hub: Use HUB_COMPLETION for centralized API key management and request routing through ProActions Hub middleware. Full-duplex voice session using the OpenAI Realtime API over WebRTC (default, with automatic WebSocket fallback). Captures microphone input, streams to the model, plays back the spoken response, and accumulates a conversation transcript. Supports tool calls and structured results.
Category LLM Version: 1.0.0 Applications: all Scope: all Default Service: OPENAI_COMPLETION

Use OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT when you need a real-time voice conversation with an OpenAI model. Use OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT when: You need a live voice conversation (microphone input + audio playback) You want the model to perform actions or call tools during the conversation You want a transcript of the conversation for downstream steps Don't use OPENAI_VOICE_AGENT when: You only need text input/output — use OPENAI_COMPLETION instead You need to transcribe audio without a live conversation — use OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION

Required Services: A dedicated OpenAI Realtime service is recommended. It must provide apiKey, a base endpoint without /v1 (for example https://api.openai.com), and a Realtime-capable model. Required Context: Platform Requirements: Requires a secure browser context with microphone permission, WebRTC, Web Audio API, AudioWorklet, and MediaDevices.getUserMedia support The browser must reach api.openai.com over HTTPS/WSS; WebRTC networks must also permit media negotiation or the step falls back to WebSocket

Reads resolved behavior and configured tool or skill conditions. Writes the transcript and optional end-session summary to text, optionally writes messages and usage outputs, and writes structured end-session results to object when supplied.

Executes inline JavaScript (script) or a JS-style template (template). Use with caution — only in trusted flows.
Category Utils Version: 1.0.4 Applications: all Scope: all

Use SCRIPTING when you need to execute custom JavaScript logic within your workflow. Use SCRIPTING when: You need complex multi-statement logic (loops, conditionals, variable assignments) You want to transform data structures using JavaScript methods You need to evaluate expressions and assign results to variables (`returnAs`) You want to build JSON output from template literals (`template` mode) You want to reuse centrally defined scripts via `scriptRef` You're working with AI tool call parameters that need processing Don't use SCRIPTING when: You only need simple variable assignment - use SET for single expressions You need user input - use FORM or PROMPT for interactive input You can accomplish the task with existing declarative steps Security Warning: SCRIPTING executes arbitrary JavaScript code without sandboxing. Only use in trusted workflows where: Configuration files are controlled by trusted developers User input is never passed directly to scripts You understand the security implications of code execution Available Context Variables: Scripts have access to these variables: `flowContext` - Current workflow context (read/write) `ctx` - Swing/Prime context object (platform-specific) `client` - ClientAdapter with methods like `getTextContent()`, `getSelectedWord()`, etc. `cfg` - Current step configuration `step` - Current step instance `params` - Parameters from AI tool calls (when used in function steps) Mode Selection: script mode - For JavaScript code blocks that return flowContext script + returnAs - For expressions that assign to a single variable template mode - For building JSON from template literals (auto-parsed) Performance Note: Uses JavaScript's Function constructor which has overhead. For high-frequency operations, consider using dedicated steps.
Scripts receive the complete flow context and can return a replacement context or mutate context keys. returnAs writes one named key; template mode parses JSON as the next flow context.

None false true None None mode Execution mode for scripts. Use "async" to run the script using the asynchronous evaluator. None false false None None returnAs When specified, the script is treated as an expression (no return statement needed) and the result is assigned to the specified property in flowContext. Cannot be used with template mode. None false false None None

documents.t: - step: SCRIPTING script: | // Access client adapter methods const selectedText = client.getSelectedText(); const documentId = client.getDocumentId(); // Access flowContext const existingData = flowContext.previousResult; // Combine and return flowContext.metadata = { selection: selectedText, docId: documentId, processedAt: new Date().toISOString(), data: existingData }; return flowContext;

# In an AI tool call function tools: - name: highlightImportantSections description: Highlight important text sections parameters: type: object properties: sections: type: array items: type: object properties: text: type: string importance: type: string enum: [high, medium, low] steps: - step: SCRIPTING script: | // params contains the AI's function call arguments params.sections .filter(s => s.importance === 'high') .map(s => ({ text: s.text, position: flowContext.originalText.indexOf(s.text) })) returnAs: highlights

- step: SCRIPTING script: | // Multi-statement script with loops and conditionals const items = flowContext.items || []; const results = []; for (const item of items) { if (item.score > 0.8) { results.push({ id: item.id, label: 'high-confidence', processed: true }); } else if (item.score > 0.5) { results.push({ id: item.id, label: 'medium-confidence', needsReview: true }); } } flowContext.processedItems = results; flowContext.totalProcessed = results.length; flowContext.timestamp = Date.now(); return flowContext;

Don't forget to return flowContext in normal script mode Why: Scripts must return the flowContext object (or a modified version) to continue the workflow. Forgetting this breaks the flow. Solution: Always end scripts with return flowContext; unless using returnAs mode. Use returnAs for simple expressions to avoid boilerplate. Don't mix template syntax with script syntax Why: Template mode uses ${} for interpolation and expects JSON output. Script mode uses pure JavaScript. Mixing them causes errors. Solution: Use template for building JSON with interpolation. Use script for JavaScript logic. Never use both in the same step. Don't forget await for async operations with returnAs Why: When using returnAs with async expressions, you must set mode: "async" or promises won't be resolved. Solution: Use mode: "async" with returnAs for any expression that returns a Promise (fetch, async functions, etc.). Don't pass user input directly to scripts Why: User input in scripts can lead to code injection vulnerabilities. SCRIPTING has no sandboxing. Solution: Validate and sanitize all user input before using in scripts. Better yet, use declarative steps instead of SCRIPTING for user data. Don't expect flowContext mutations in returnAs mode to persist Why: When using returnAs, only the specified property is set. Direct mutations to flowContext are ignored. Solution: Use normal script mode if you need to mutate multiple flowContext properties. Use returnAs only for single-value assignments.

Related Steps: SET - Alternative for simple expressions: Use SET for simple value assignments and single expressions. Use SCRIPTING for multi-line logic with loops and conditionals. IF - Use together for conditional logic: Use IF for flow control based on conditions. Use SCRIPTING inside IF blocks for complex conditional logic. FOR - Use together for iteration: Use FOR to iterate over arrays. Use SCRIPTING inside FOR loops for complex item processing. General Resources: Step Library Overview Configuration Basics Examples

documents.s: Set a variable using text (legacy syntax)

documents.t: Don't confuse new syntax with legacy syntax - mixing them causes unexpected behavior Why: SET supports two different syntaxes: direct properties (new) and name/text (legacy). Mixing them can create unintended variables or overwrite data. Solution: Use new syntax for most cases (simpler): SET userId: "123". Use legacy syntax only when needed for compatibility: SET name: "userId" text: "123". Don't forget that template strings are resolved - use raw_text for literal strings Why: The text property resolves {{ }} templates. If your string contains {{ or }}, it will be interpreted as a template. Solution: Use raw_text for literal strings that contain {{ or }} characters, or escape them in templates. Don't use convertTo — it's deprecated and unnecessary Why: Whole-string {{ … }} templates now return native types automatically. {{ flowContext.count + 1 }} yields a number; {{ flowContext.flag }} yields a boolean; {{ flowContext.items }} yields the actual array reference. Solution: Write the expression directly: count: "{{ flowContext.x + 1 }}" (already a number). For literal numbers, use plain YAML: count: 5. Remove convertTo from your SET steps.

Related Steps: SCRIPTING - Alternative for complex logic: Use SCRIPTING for multi-line JavaScript with loops and conditionals. Use SET for simple value assignments and single expressions. FORM - Alternative for user input: Use FORM to collect data from users interactively. Use SET to store programmatic values. PROMPT - Alternative for simple input: Use PROMPT for single user input. Use SET for storing calculated or static values. FOR - Use together for iteration: Use SET inside FOR loops to accumulate results or maintain counters. IF - Use together for conditional assignment: Wrap SET in IF to conditionally set variables based on logic. General Resources: Step Library Overview Configuration Basics Examples

Evaluates a switch value and executes the steps for the matching case. Supports both array and object syntax for cases.
Category Control Version: 1.0.3 Applications: all Scope: all
Use SWITCH to route one resolved value to one of several named cases or a default branch.
Reads flow context values referenced by condition, legacy switch, and legacy case tests. Does not write directly; writes from the selected case subflow are preserved.

Name Description Default Required Resolved Constraints Conditional Rules condition The condition to evaluate for the switch value. Can be a template expression with {{ }} syntax. None false true Length:1-∞ None switch Legacy alternative to condition. The switch value to evaluate using JavaScript syntax. None false false Length:1-∞ None cases The cases to match against the switch value. Each case key should match a possible switch value, with the value being an array of steps to execute. Use "default" as a fallback case. None true false None None

The cases to match against the switch value. Each case key should match a possible switch value, with the value being an array of steps to execute. Use "default" as a fallback case. Dynamic Properties: This object accepts dynamic keys. Each key-value pair should follow this structure: Key: Any string matching the switch value Value Type: stepArray Value Description: Array of steps to execute when this case matches the switch value Items: Array of workflow steps Special Keys: default (stepArray): Fallback steps to execute when no other case matches Object Constraints: Property Count:1-∞ properties
Require Exactly One: Exactly one of: condition, switch

- step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.userRole }}" cases: "admin": - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Welcome Admin" "user": - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Welcome User" "default": - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "Welcome Guest"

- step: FORM form: selectedAction: type: 'select' label: 'Choose action' options: - 'translate' - 'summarize' - 'improve' buttons: - type: 'submit' - step: SWITCH condition: "{{ flowContext.selectedAction }}" cases: "translate": - step: DEEPL_TRANSLATE instruction: "{textContent}" target_lang: "FR" "summarize": - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Summarize: {textContent}" "improve": - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Improve: {textContent}" "default": - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION message: "No action selected"

None false true None None virtual Whether tags should be virtual (temporary, not saved). Default is false (persistent tags). Only applies to Swing; Prime always persists tags. false false false None None

- step: TAG_PURE_TEXT tags: - tag: "mark" start: 100 size: 10 attributes: class: "highlight" - tag: "mark" start: 20 size: 15 attributes: class: "important"

Displays a selection modal allowing the user to pick one item from a list. The list may be provided directly or produced by a pre-processing step (inlineSteps). The selected value is written to the default text output.
Category UI Version: 1.0.0 Applications: all Scope: all
Use USER_SELECT when a user must choose one textual value from a prepared list or text-derived list.

Reads list, or converts text when list is absent; resolves prompt and info values. Writes the selected value to text or its configured output name; inline steps may also write context. With applySteps, each clicked option is applied by running applySteps on a copy of the flow context (option in the text output); Done writes the applied option to the text output, while "Restore original" and Cancel re-apply restoreValue.

Name Description Default Required Resolved Constraints Conditional Rules inlineSteps Optional steps to execute before showing the selection modal. Useful to prepare or transform input. None false false None None promptText Prompt or title text shown at the top of the selection modal (supports variable resolution). None false true None None infoTitle Optional title shown above additional info in the selection modal. None false true None None infoText Optional descriptive text shown in the selection modal (supports variable resolution). None false true None None enableKeyboardControl Enable keyboard navigation in the selection modal. None false false None None applySteps Enables try-out mode: steps run each time the user clicks an option, with the option in the text output. The dialog stays open; Done accepts the applied option and continues the flow. Requires restoreValue. None false false None Requires: restoreValue restoreValue Required with applySteps: the original value (supports variable resolution), resolved when the dialog opens. Backs the "Restore original" button and is re-applied via applySteps when the user cancels, so no tried option is left in the document. None false true None None
Type Description Default Required Resolved list List of options for the user to select from. If omitted, converts text input to a list automatically. None false false
Type Description Optional text The selected option (string) stored in the default text output. false
- step: USER_SELECT promptText: "Choose an option" # list can be taken from prior steps or from the flowContext
- step: TO_LIST # prepare list in flowContext.list - step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: - step: TO_LIST

- step: USER_SELECT inlineSteps: - step: HUB_COMPLETION instruction: "Suggest 6 headlines for: {textContent}" response_format: list enableKeyboardControl: true promptText: Suggestions infoTitle: Current Title infoText: '{{ client.getTextAtXpath("/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p") | safe }}' restoreValue: '{{ client.getTextAtXpath("/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p") | safe }}' applySteps: - step: REPLACE_TEXT at: XPATH xpath: "/doc/story/grouphead/headline/p"

User interaction steps handle communication with users through forms, prompts, notifications, and menus.
Requests a change of the view port size. Useful to resize the command palette view in Prime 8. Version: 1.0.12 Example: - step: CHANGE_VIEW_SIZE width: 800 height: 600

Opens a file upload dialog (modal) and stores selected file(s) into the flow context. Supports output mapping via the outputs config or default file output. Aliases: USER_FILE_UPLOAD Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: FILE_UPLOAD promptText: "Please upload your document"

Displays a configurable form to the user (via FormBuilder). The form definition is provided in cfg.form. When submitted, the returned values are merged into the flowContext. Version: 1.0.2 Example: - step: FORM title: "Your info" form: firstName: type: text label: "First name" required: true lastName: type: text label: "Last name" required: true
Hide any shown progress bar. Version: 1.0.8 Example: - step: HIDE_PROGRESS

Shows an image picker modal allowing the user to pick one image from a provided list of image objects ({ url, previewUrl?, label? }). The selected image object is stored as an output. Aliases: USER_IMAGE_PICKER Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: USER_IMAGE_PICKER promptText: "Choose an image" imageList: - url: "https://example.com/image1.jpg" previewUrl: "https://example.com/thumb1.jpg" label: "Image 1" - url: "https://example.com/image2.jpg" previewUrl: "https://example.com/thumb2.jpg" label: "Image 2"

Display a selection of choices in the Flow Monitor. Pauses workflow until user selects. Version: 1.2.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_CHOICE message: "Select export format:" choices: - id: pdf label: "📄 PDF Document" - id: docx label: "📝 Word Document" - id: html label: "🌐 HTML Page" - step: EXPORT_DOCUMENT format: "{{flowContext.text}}"

Display a confirmation dialog in the Flow Monitor. Pauses workflow until user responds. Version: 1.3.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_CONFIRM message: "Publish this article?" - step: IF condition: "{{flowContext.confirmed}}" then: - step: PUBLISH_ARTICLE
Display an inline text input field in the Flow Monitor. Version: 1.2.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_INPUT message: "Enter filename:" placeholder: "document" outputs: - type: text name: filename
Display JSON structured data in the Flow Monitor. Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_JSON title: "Model response" data: "{{flowContext.object}}" maxDepth: 4
Display key-value structured data in the Flow Monitor. Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_KEYVALUE title: "Result summary" data: "{{flowContext.object}}"
Display metrics in the Flow Monitor. Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_METRICS title: "Evaluation" data: score: 87 confidence: 0.92 tokens: 1420

Display status messages in the Flow Monitor during workflow execution. Version: 1.2.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_STATUS message: "Connecting to OpenAI API..." type: status - step: OPENAI_COMPLETION # ... OpenAI step config - step: MONITOR_STATUS message: "Response received!" type: success
Display tabular structured data in the Flow Monitor. Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: MONITOR_TABLE title: "Summary" data: "{{flowContext.list}}" maxRows: 20

Plays audio in a lightweight floating player. Audio source can be provided as a data URL, http(s) URL, raw base64 or a Blob (e.g. in: '{{ flowContext.blob }}' after HUB_SPEECH) via cfg.in, or via the default text input. The step mounts a closed Shadow DOM audio player and resolves when the player is closed by the user. Version: 1.1.0 Example: - step: SET text: "data:audio/mpeg;base64,..." - step: PLAY_AUDIO in: "{{flowContext.text}}" autoplay: true
Shows a simple prompt to the user and stores the entered text into the default text output. Aliases: USER_PROMPT Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: PROMPT promptText: "Please enter your name"

Shows a notification to the user with optional title and resolved message. Aliases: CTX_SHOW_NOTIFICATION Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: SHOW_NOTIFICATION notificationType: "info" message: "Processing completed for {{userName}}" title: "Done"

Show a progress bar with optional status text. Use position to place it and autoHide to auto-hide after completion. Version: 1.0.8 Example: - step: SHOW_PROGRESS status: "Processing..." position: "bottom" autoHide: true

Shows a response to the user in a modal. Can run inline steps before showing and supports HTML and Markdown modes. Aliases: CTX_SHOW_RESPONSE Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: SET text: "Text to show" - step: SHOW_RESPONSE

Update an existing progress bar. Provide percentage (0-100) and optional status text. Version: 1.0.8 Example: - step: UPDATE_PROGRESS percentage: "{{progressPercent}}" status: "Step {{progressStep}}/5"

Displays a selection modal allowing the user to pick one item from a list. The list may be provided directly or produced by a pre-processing step (inlineSteps). The selected value is written to the default text output. Version: 1.0.0 Example: - step: USER_SELECT promptText: "Choose an option" # list can be taken from prior steps or from the flowContext
